title: The Story of Aadam (AS) — Chosen by Allah
summary: The story of the creation of the first human being, his life in Paradise, the trial with Iblis, and his descent to Earth — a story of honour, temptation, and mercy.

chapters.title: The Creation of Adam
chapters.content:
Before any human walked the earth, Allah announced His plan to the angels.

وَإِذْ قَالَ رَبُّكَ لِلْمَلَٰٓئِكَةِ إِنِّى جَاعِلٌۭ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ خَلِيفَةًۭ ۖ قَالُوٓا۟ أَتَجْعَلُ فِيهَا مَن يُفْسِدُ فِيهَا وَيَسْفِكُ ٱلدِّمَآءَ وَنَحْنُ نُسَبِّحُ بِحَمْدِكَ وَنُقَدِّسُ لَكَ ۖ قَالَ إِنِّىٓ أَعْلَمُ مَا لَا تَعْلَمُونَ

"And [mention, O Muḥammad], when your Lord said to the angels, 'Indeed, I will make upon the earth a successive authority.' They said, 'Will You place upon it one who causes corruption therein and sheds blood, while we exalt You with praise and declare Your perfection?' He [Allāh] said, 'Indeed, I know that which you do not know.'"

— Surah Al-Baqarah 2:30

The angels, in their humility, wondered how a being capable of corruption and bloodshed could be placed on the earth, when they themselves only glorified Allah. Allah's answer was simple yet profound: He knew something they did not.

Allah then explained what this creation would be made from.

وَإِذْ قَالَ رَبُّكَ لِلْمَلَٰٓئِكَةِ إِنِّى خَٰلِقٌۢ بَشَرًۭا مِّن صَلْصَٰلٍۢ مِّنْ حَمَإٍۢ مَّسْنُونٍۢ

"And [mention, O Muḥammad], when your Lord said to the angels, 'I will create a human being out of clay from an altered black mud.'"

— Surah Al-Hijr 15:28

Not from light, like the angels. Not from fire, like the jinn. But from clay — humble, earthly material. Yet Allah was about to do something extraordinary with it.

فَإِذَا سَوَّيْتُهُۥ وَنَفَخْتُ فِيهِ مِن رُّوحِى فَقَعُوا۟ لَهُۥ سَٰجِدِينَ

"And when I have proportioned him and breathed into him of My [created] soul, then fall down to him in prostration."

— Surah Al-Hijr 15:29

Once Adam (AS) was shaped and given life from Allah's own breath, the angels were commanded to prostrate to him — not in worship of Adam, but in obedience to Allah's command, honoring this new creation.

Allah elaborates further on this process in another surah, describing the careful perfection behind every part of creation.

ٱلَّذِىٓ أَحْسَنَ كُلَّ شَىْءٍ خَلَقَهُۥ ۖ وَبَدَأَ خَلْقَ ٱلْإِنسَٰنِ مِن طِينٍۢ

"Who perfected everything which He created and began the creation of man from clay."

— Surah As-Sajdah 32:7

Nothing Allah creates is random or careless — every part of creation, including the very first human, was perfected with purpose.

ثُمَّ جَعَلَ نَسْلَهُۥ مِن سُلَٰلَةٍۢ مِّن مَّآءٍۢ مَّهِينٍۢ

"Then He made his posterity out of the extract of a liquid disdained."

— Surah As-Sajdah 32:8

From Adam (AS) came every human being after him — through a process Allah describes with both honesty and humility, reminding us that for all our pride, our origin was humble.

ثُمَّ سَوَّىٰهُ وَنَفَخَ فِيهِ مِن رُّوحِهِۦ ۖ وَجَعَلَ لَكُمُ ٱلسَّمْعَ وَٱلْأَبْصَٰرَ وَٱلْأَفْـِٔدَةَ ۚ قَلِيلًۭا مَّا تَشْكُرُونَ

"Then He proportioned him and breathed into him from His [created] soul and made for you hearing and vision and hearts [i.e., intellect]; little are you grateful."

— Surah As-Sajdah 32:9

And then Allah completed the creation — proportioning the body, breathing in the soul, and gifting humanity with hearing, sight, and hearts capable of understanding. Yet Allah closes this verse with a gentle rebuke: how little we actually show gratitude for these gifts.

This is where the story of every human being begins — not with arrogance, but with clay, breath, and the mercy of a Creator who gave us senses and understanding so that we might recognize Him.

chapters.title: The Names and the Honour of Adam
chapters.content:
After Adam (AS) was created, Allah gave him a gift unlike anything given to the angels before him — knowledge itself.

وَعَلَّمَ ءَادَمَ ٱلْأَسْمَآءَ كُلَّهَا ثُمَّ عَرَضَهُمْ عَلَى ٱلْمَلَٰٓئِكَةِ فَقَالَ أَنۢبِـُٔونِى بِأَسْمَآءِ هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ إِن كُنتُمْ صَٰدِقِينَ

"And He taught Adam the names - all of them. Then He showed them to the angels and said, 'Inform Me of the names of these, if you are truthful.'"

— Surah Al-Baqarah 2:31

Allah taught Adam (AS) the names of all things, then turned to the angels and asked them to do the same. It wasn't a test meant to embarrass them — it was meant to reveal something important about this new creation.

قَالُوا۟ سُبْحَٰنَكَ لَا عِلْمَ لَنَآ إِلَّا مَا عَلَّمْتَنَآ ۖ إِنَّكَ أَنتَ ٱلْعَلِيمُ ٱلْحَكِيمُ

"They said, 'Exalted are You; we have no knowledge except what You have taught us. Indeed, it is You who is the Knowing, the Wise.'"

— Surah Al-Baqarah 2:32

The angels responded with complete humility. They didn't pretend to know something they didn't. They acknowledged that all knowledge belongs to Allah, and whatever they know is only what He has taught them.

قَالَ يَٰٓـَٔادَمُ أَنۢبِئْهُم بِأَسْمَآئِهِمْ ۖ فَلَمَّآ أَنۢبَأَهُم بِأَسْمَآئِهِمْ قَالَ أَلَمْ أَقُل لَّكُمْ إِنِّىٓ أَعْلَمُ غَيْبَ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ وَأَعْلَمُ مَا تُبْدُونَ وَمَا كُنتُمْ تَكْتُمُونَ

"He said, 'O Adam, inform them of their names.' And when he had informed them of their names, He said, 'Did I not tell you that I know the unseen [aspects] of the heavens and the earth? And I know what you reveal and what you have concealed.'"

— Surah Al-Baqarah 2:33

Then Allah asked Adam (AS) to inform the angels of the names — and he did. This was the moment that revealed Adam's unique capacity: the ability to learn, to hold knowledge, and to communicate it. It was a sign of the trust Allah was placing in humanity.

وَإِذْ قُلْنَا لِلْمَلَٰٓئِكَةِ ٱسْجُدُوا۟ لِءَادَمَ فَسَجَدُوٓا۟ إِلَّآ إِبْلِيسَ أَبَىٰ وَٱسْتَكْبَرَ وَكَانَ مِنَ ٱلْكَٰفِرِينَ

"And [mention] when We said to the angels, 'Prostrate before Adam'; so they prostrated, except for Iblees. He refused and was arrogant and became of the disbelievers."

— Surah Al-Baqarah 2:34

Following this, Allah commanded the angels to prostrate before Adam (AS) — not in worship, but as an act of honor and recognition of his elevated status. Every single angel obeyed immediately. Except one. Iblis refused, driven by arrogance, and in that single act of disobedience, he placed himself among the disbelievers.

This honor given to Adam (AS) was not just for him alone — it was a gift extended to all of his children, for all time.

۞ وَلَقَدْ كَرَّمْنَا بَنِىٓ ءَادَمَ وَحَمَلْنَٰهُمْ فِى ٱلْبَرِّ وَٱلْبَحْرِ وَرَزَقْنَٰهُم مِّنَ ٱلطَّيِّبَٰتِ وَفَضَّلْنَٰهُمْ عَلَىٰ كَثِيرٍۢ مِّمَّنْ خَلَقْنَا تَفْضِيلًۭا

"And We have certainly honored the children of Adam and carried them on the land and sea and provided for them of the good things and preferred them over much of what We have created, with [definite] preference."

— Surah Al-Isra 17:70

Allah honored the children of Adam — every human being who would ever live — giving them the ability to travel across land and sea, providing them with good and pure sustenance, and favoring them above much of creation. This is a dignity given to humanity simply for being human, regardless of belief or background — a responsibility to live up to, and a blessing to be grateful for.

chapters.title: Iblis and the First Act of Arrogance
chapters.content:
After Adam (AS) was given form, Allah commanded all the angels to prostrate before him as a sign of honor.

وَلَقَدْ خَلَقْنَٰكُمْ ثُمَّ صَوَّرْنَٰكُمْ ثُمَّ قُلْنَا لِلْمَلَٰٓئِكَةِ ٱسْجُدُوا۟ لِءَادَمَ فَسَجَدُوٓا۟ إِلَّآ إِبْلِيسَ لَمْ يَكُن مِّنَ ٱلسَّٰجِدِينَ

"And We have certainly created you, [O mankind], and given you [human] form. Then We said to the angels, 'Prostrate to Adam'; so they prostrated, except for Iblees. He was not of those who prostrated."

— Surah Al-A'raf 7:11

Every single one obeyed — except Iblis. He alone refused, breaking ranks with all of creation in that moment.

Allah asked him directly why he disobeyed a clear command.

قَالَ مَا مَنَعَكَ أَلَّا تَسْجُدَ إِذْ أَمَرْتُكَ ۖ قَالَ أَنَا۠ خَيْرٌۭ مِّنْهُ خَلَقْتَنِى مِن نَّارٍۢ وَخَلَقْتَهُۥ مِن طِينٍۢ

"[Allāh] said, 'What prevented you from prostrating when I commanded you?' [Satan] said, 'I am better than him. You created me from fire and created him from clay [i.e., earth].'"

— Surah Al-A'raf 7:12

Iblis's answer revealed the root of his downfall: arrogance based on material origin. He believed fire made him superior to clay, placing his own judgment above Allah's command.

قَالَ فَٱهْبِطْ مِنْهَا فَمَا يَكُونُ لَكَ أَن تَتَكَبَّرَ فِيهَا فَٱخْرُجْ إِنَّكَ مِنَ ٱلصَّٰغِرِينَ

"[Allāh] said, 'Descend from it [i.e., Paradise], for it is not for you to be arrogant therein. So get out; indeed, you are of the debased.'"

— Surah Al-A'raf 7:13

Allah's response was immediate and final — Iblis was expelled from his elevated position, reduced to the lowest standing for his pride.

قَالَ أَنظِرْنِىٓ إِلَىٰ يَوْمِ يُبْعَثُونَ

"[Satan] said, 'Reprieve me until the Day they are resurrected.'"

— Surah Al-A'raf 7:14

Rather than repenting, Iblis asked for something else entirely: more time, until the Day of Judgment, to carry out the enmity he was now determined to hold against humanity.

Allah repeats this same moment in Surah Al-Hijr, adding further detail to Iblis's exact words and Allah's response.

إِلَّآ إِبْلِيسَ أَبَىٰٓ أَن يَكُونَ مَعَ ٱلسَّٰجِدِينَ

"Except Iblees; he refused to be with those who prostrated."

— Surah Al-Hijr 15:31

Allah then asked him directly why he had refused to prostrate.

قَالَ يَٰٓإِبْلِيسُ مَا لَكَ أَلَّا تَكُونَ مَعَ ٱلسَّٰجِدِينَ

"[Allāh] said, 'O Iblees, what is [the matter] with you that you are not with those who prostrate?'"

— Surah Al-Hijr 15:32

Allah asked again, almost giving Iblis the chance to reconsider — but his answer remained the same prideful refusal.

قَالَ لَمْ أَكُن لِّأَسْجُدَ لِبَشَرٍ خَلَقْتَهُۥ مِن صَلْصَٰلٍۢ مِّنْ حَمَإٍۢ مَّسْنُونٍۢ

"He said, 'Never would I prostrate to a human whom You created out of clay from an altered black mud.'"

— Surah Al-Hijr 15:33

Allah's response came at once, casting him out for his defiance.

قَالَ فَٱخْرُجْ مِنْهَا فَإِنَّكَ رَجِيمٌۭ

"[Allāh] said, 'Then depart from it, for indeed, you are expelled.'"

— Surah Al-Hijr 15:34

This expulsion carried with it a lasting consequence.

وَإِنَّ عَلَيْكَ ٱللَّعْنَةَ إِلَىٰ يَوْمِ ٱلدِّينِ

"And indeed, upon you is the curse until the Day of Recompense."

— Surah Al-Hijr 15:35

The curse placed upon him would last until the Day of Recompense — a permanent consequence for a single act of arrogance against a single command.

Instead of seeking forgiveness, Iblis made a vow that would define his role for the rest of human history.

قَالَ رَبِّ بِمَآ أَغْوَيْتَنِى لَأُزَيِّنَنَّ لَهُمْ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ وَلَأُغْوِيَنَّهُمْ أَجْمَعِينَ

"[Iblees] said, 'My Lord, because You have put me in error, I will surely make [disobedience] attractive to them [i.e., mankind] on earth, and I will mislead them all.'"

— Surah Al-Hijr 15:39

He declared open enmity against every human being, vowing to make sin appealing and to mislead as many as possible.

إِلَّا عِبَادَكَ مِنْهُمُ ٱلْمُخْلَصِينَ

"Except, among them, Your chosen servants."

— Surah Al-Hijr 15:40

Yet even in his vow, Allah's mercy is visible — Iblis himself acknowledged he would have no power over Allah's sincere, devoted servants. His arrogance could only affect those who chose to follow him; it could never overpower true sincerity to Allah.

This is the first lesson every human inherits from this moment: arrogance — placing one's own judgment above a clear command from Allah — is the root of disobedience. And yet, sincerity and devotion to Allah remain the believer's protection against it, for all time.

chapters.title: Paradise and the One Forbidden Tree
chapters.content:
Allah settled Adam (AS) and his wife in Paradise, granting them complete freedom with one single exception.

وَقُلْنَا يَٰٓـَٔادَمُ ٱسْكُنْ أَنتَ وَزَوْجُكَ ٱلْجَنَّةَ وَكُلَا مِنْهَا رَغَدًا حَيْثُ شِئْتُمَا وَلَا تَقْرَبَا هَٰذِهِ ٱلشَّجَرَةَ فَتَكُونَا مِنَ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ

"And We said, 'O Adam, dwell, you and your wife, in Paradise and eat therefrom in [ease and] abundance from wherever you will. But do not approach this tree, lest you be among the wrongdoers.'"

— Surah Al-Baqarah 2:35

Everything in Paradise was permitted to them except approaching one tree. It wasn't a harsh restriction — it was a simple test of obedience amid abundance.

But Iblis, true to his vow, found his opening.

فَأَزَلَّهُمَا ٱلشَّيْطَٰنُ عَنْهَا فَأَخْرَجَهُمَا مِمَّا كَانَا فِيهِ ۖ وَقُلْنَا ٱهْبِطُوا۟ بَعْضُكُمْ لِبَعْضٍ عَدُوٌّۭ ۖ وَلَكُمْ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ مُسْتَقَرٌّۭ وَمَتَٰعٌ إِلَىٰ حِينٍۢ

"But Satan caused them to slip out of it and removed them from that [condition] in which they had been. And We said, 'Go down, [all of you], as enemies to one another, and you will have upon the earth a place of settlement and provision for a time.'"

— Surah Al-Baqarah 2:36

Satan caused them to slip, and they were removed from the comfort they had known. Allah then informed them that they — and their offspring — would now descend to the earth, a place of both struggle and provision.

The same moment is described again in Surah Al-A'raf, with greater detail of how Iblis approached them.

وَيَٰٓـَٔادَمُ ٱسْكُنْ أَنتَ وَزَوْجُكَ ٱلْجَنَّةَ فَكُلَا مِنْ حَيْثُ شِئْتُمَا وَلَا تَقْرَبَا هَٰذِهِ ٱلشَّجَرَةَ فَتَكُونَا مِنَ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ

"And 'O Adam, dwell, you and your wife, in Paradise and eat from wherever you will but do not approach this tree, lest you be among the wrongdoers.'"

— Surah Al-A'raf 7:19

Then Satan came to whisper doubts into their hearts.

فَوَسْوَسَ لَهُمَا ٱلشَّيْطَٰنُ لِيُبْدِىَ لَهُمَا مَا وُۥرِىَ عَنْهُمَا مِن سَوْءَٰتِهِمَا وَقَالَ مَا نَهَىٰكُمَا رَبُّكُمَا عَنْ هَٰذِهِ ٱلشَّجَرَةِ إِلَّآ أَن تَكُونَا مَلَكَيْنِ أَوْ تَكُونَا مِنَ ٱلْخَٰلِدِينَ

"But Satan whispered to them to make apparent to them that which was concealed from them of their private parts. He said, 'Your Lord did not forbid you this tree except that you become angels or become of the immortal.'"

— Surah Al-A'raf 7:20

Iblis didn't simply tempt them with pleasure — he twisted Allah's prohibition into something it never was, suggesting the tree was being withheld from them out of jealousy, not mercy.

وَقَاسَمَهُمَآ إِنِّى لَكُمَا لَمِنَ ٱلنَّٰصِحِينَ

"And he swore [by Allāh] to them, 'Indeed, I am to you from among the sincere advisors.'"

— Surah Al-A'raf 7:21

He went further, swearing falsely that he had their best interests at heart — using Allah's name to deceive them, a tactic of manipulation that still echoes in how falsehood often disguises itself as sincerity.

فَدَلَّىٰهُمَا بِغُرُورٍۢ ۚ فَلَمَّا ذَاقَا ٱلشَّجَرَةَ بَدَتْ لَهُمَا سَوْءَٰتُهُمَا وَطَفِقَا يَخْصِفَانِ عَلَيْهِمَا مِن وَرَقِ ٱلْجَنَّةِ ۖ وَنَادَىٰهُمَا رَبُّهُمَآ أَلَمْ أَنْهَكُمَا عَن تِلْكُمَا ٱلشَّجَرَةِ وَأَقُل لَّكُمَآ إِنَّ ٱلشَّيْطَٰنَ لَكُمَا عَدُوٌّۭ مُّبِينٌۭ

"So he made them fall, through deception. And when they tasted of the tree, their private parts became apparent to them, and they began to fasten together over themselves from the leaves of Paradise. And their Lord called to them, 'Did I not forbid you from that tree and tell you that Satan is to you a clear enemy?'"

— Surah Al-A'raf 7:22

Once they tasted from the tree, the consequence was immediate — an awareness of vulnerability they had never experienced. They instinctively tried to cover themselves, and Allah's question to them wasn't out of ignorance, but to allow them the space to acknowledge what had happened.

Their response is one of the most important models of repentance in the entire Quran.

قَالَا رَبَّنَا ظَلَمْنَآ أَنفُسَنَا وَإِن لَّمْ تَغْفِرْ لَنَا وَتَرْحَمْنَا لَنَكُونَنَّ مِنَ ٱلْخَٰسِرِينَ

"They said, 'Our Lord, we have wronged ourselves, and if You do not forgive us and have mercy upon us, we will surely be among the losers.'"

— Surah Al-A'raf 7:23

No blame placed elsewhere. No argument. Just complete acknowledgment of their own wrongdoing and a sincere plea for mercy — this is what separated their slip from Iblis's outright rebellion.

Surah Ta-Ha adds yet another layer to how Iblis approached them.

فَوَسْوَسَ إِلَيْهِ ٱلشَّيْطَٰنُ قَالَ يَٰٓـَٔادَمُ هَلْ أَدُلُّكَ عَلَىٰ شَجَرَةِ ٱلْخُلْدِ وَمُلْكٍۢ لَّا يَبْلَىٰ

"Then Satan whispered to him; he said, 'O Adam, shall I direct you to the tree of eternity and possession that will not deteriorate?'"

— Surah Ta-Ha 20:120

He didn't call it a "forbidden tree" — he called it the tree of eternal life and a kingdom that never fades, appealing directly to humanity's deepest desires: permanence and power.

فَأَكَلَا مِنْهَا فَبَدَتْ لَهُمَا سَوْءَٰتُهُمَا وَطَفِقَا يَخْصِفَانِ عَلَيْهِمَا مِن وَرَقِ ٱلْجَنَّةِ ۚ وَعَصَىٰٓ ءَادَمُ رَبَّهُۥ فَغَوَىٰ

"And they [i.e., Adam and his wife] ate of it, and their private parts became apparent to them, and they began to fasten over themselves from the leaves of Paradise. And Adam disobeyed his Lord and erred."

— Surah Ta-Ha 20:121

And so they ate from it, and their vulnerability became apparent. The verse is direct in stating that Adam (AS) disobeyed his Lord — but this single word should never be confused with rebellion. As we will see, what follows this moment defines the entire difference between a human mistake and a satanic one.

chapters.title: The Descent and the Promise
chapters.content:
After the trial in Paradise, Allah gave Adam (AS) and Hawwa a path forward — not abandonment, but guidance.

قُلْنَا ٱهْبِطُوا۟ مِنْهَا جَمِيعًۭا ۖ فَإِمَّا يَأْتِيَنَّكُم مِّنِّى هُدًۭى فَمَن تَبِعَ هُدَاىَ فَلَا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلَا هُمْ يَحْزَنُونَ

"We said, 'Go down from it, all of you. And when guidance comes to you from Me, whoever follows My guidance - there will be no fear concerning them, nor will they grieve.'"

— Surah Al-Baqarah 2:38

Despite their descent to the earth, Allah immediately offered the solution to every struggle they would face: His guidance. Whoever follows it has nothing to fear and nothing to grieve over — a promise that extends to every human being who would ever live.

But Allah also makes the alternative clear.

وَٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ وَكَذَّبُوا۟ بِـَٔايَٰتِنَآ أُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ أَصْحَٰبُ ٱلنَّارِ ۖ هُمْ فِيهَا خَٰلِدُونَ

"And those who disbelieve and deny Our signs - those will be companions of the Fire; they will abide therein eternally."

— Surah Al-Baqarah 2:39

Those who reject Allah's signs and persist in disbelief choose a path that leads to the Fire, eternally. The choice Adam's children would face — guidance or rejection — was set from this very first moment.

Surah Ta-Ha reveals something beautiful that happened before this descent — Allah's response to Adam's sincere repentance.

ثُمَّ ٱجْتَبَٰهُ رَبُّهُۥ فَتَابَ عَلَيْهِ وَهَدَىٰ

"Then his Lord chose him and turned to him in forgiveness and guided [him]."

— Surah Ta-Ha 20:122

Allah didn't just forgive Adam (AS) — He chose him. Turned to him with mercy and guided him. This is the moment that distinguishes Adam's mistake from Iblis's rebellion: Adam turned back to Allah, and Allah turned back to him.

Only after this forgiveness does the descent to earth take place.

قَالَ ٱهْبِطَا مِنْهَا جَمِيعًۢا ۖ بَعْضُكُمْ لِبَعْضٍ عَدُوٌّۭ ۖ فَإِمَّا يَأْتِيَنَّكُم مِّنِّى هُدًۭى فَمَنِ ٱتَّبَعَ هُدَاىَ فَلَا يَضِلُّ وَلَا يَشْقَىٰ

"[Allāh] said, 'Descend from it [i.e., Paradise] - all, [your descendants] being enemies to one another. And if there should come to you guidance from Me - then whoever follows My guidance will neither go astray [in the world] nor suffer [in the Hereafter].'"

— Surah Ta-Ha 20:123

Adam (AS) and Hawwa would descend together, their offspring destined to sometimes be at odds with one another — yet the door of guidance would always remain open. Whoever follows it would neither go astray in this world, nor suffer in the next.

This is where Adam's story finds its true ending — not in punishment, but in promise. He became the first human, the first prophet, and the first to demonstrate the path every believer would walk after him: stumble, return to Allah sincerely, and be guided. The story of Adam (AS) is, in many ways, the story of every one of us.

title: The Story of Yunus (AS) — Dhun-Nun — Man of the Whale
summary: The powerful story of a prophet who left his people without permission, was swallowed by a whale, and called upon Allah from the depths of darkness — and was answered.

chapters.title: The Prophet Who Left Without Permission
chapters.content:
Yunus (AS) was sent as a messenger to his people, but his story took an unexpected turn.

وَإِنَّ يُونُسَ لَمِنَ ٱلْمُرْسَلِينَ

"And indeed, Jonah was among the messengers."

— Surah As-Saffat 37:139

Allah confirms his status clearly — Yunus (AS) was truly one of His messengers, sent with a mission to call his people to worship Allah alone.

إِذْ أَبَقَ إِلَى ٱلْفُلْكِ ٱلْمَشْحُونِ

"[Mention] when he ran away to the laden ship."

— Surah As-Saffat 37:140

But frustrated by his people's persistent rejection, Yunus (AS) left them without waiting for Allah's permission to do so — boarding a ship that was already full, an action not befitting his station as a prophet.

فَسَاهَمَ فَكَانَ مِنَ ٱلْمُدْحَضِينَ

"And he drew lots and was among the losers."

— Surah As-Saffat 37:141

When the ship encountered trouble, the sailors drew lots to decide who would be thrown overboard to lighten the load. The lot fell upon Yunus (AS).

فَٱلْتَقَمَهُ ٱلْحُوتُ وَهُوَ مُلِيمٌۭ

"Then the fish swallowed him, while he was blameworthy."

— Surah As-Saffat 37:142

He was cast into the sea, and at that moment, a great fish swallowed him whole — a consequence directly tied to his decision to leave his people without Allah's command. The word "blameworthy" here is not a condemnation of his prophethood, but an acknowledgment that even prophets, who are otherwise protected from major sin, can make a misstep deserving of correction.

chapters.title: The Darkness Within Darkness
chapters.content:
In the depths of the sea, swallowed by the fish, Yunus (AS) found himself in a darkness unlike anything experienced before.

وَذَا ٱلنُّونِ إِذ ذَّهَبَ مُغَٰضِبًۭا فَظَنَّ أَن لَّن نَّقْدِرَ عَلَيْهِ فَنَادَىٰ فِى ٱلظُّلُمَٰتِ أَن لَّآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّآ أَنتَ سُبْحَٰنَكَ إِنِّى كُنتُ مِنَ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ

"And [mention] the man of the fish [i.e., Jonah], when he went off in anger and thought that We would not decree [anything] upon him. And he called out within the darknesses, 'There is no deity except You; exalted are You. Indeed, I have been of the wrongdoers.'"

— Surah Al-Anbiya 21:87

Allah describes him here as the "man of the fish" — Yunus (AS) had left in anger, not anticipating the trial Allah had decreed for him. Yet in that overwhelming darkness — the darkness of the fish's belly, the darkness of the ocean depths, and the darkness of night layered together — he turned entirely to Allah. His call was not one of excuses or blame, but pure acknowledgment: there is no god but Allah, and he himself had wronged himself by leaving without permission.

This single dua would become one of the most powerful supplications ever recorded in the Quran. But Allah also reveals what would have happened had Yunus (AS) not been a man of constant remembrance.

فَلَوْلَآ أَنَّهُۥ كَانَ مِنَ ٱلْمُسَبِّحِينَ

"And had he not been of those who exalt Allāh,"

— Surah As-Saffat 37:143

Allah then reveals the fate he would have faced had he not been of the righteous.

لَلَبِثَ فِى بَطْنِهِۦٓ إِلَىٰ يَوْمِ يُبْعَثُونَ

"He would have remained inside its belly until the Day they are resurrected."

— Surah As-Saffat 37:144

Had Yunus (AS) not been someone who regularly glorified and remembered Allah throughout his life — not just in this moment of crisis — he would have remained trapped in the belly of the fish until the Day of Resurrection. This is a profound lesson: the habits of worship built before hardship are what sustain a person during it. Yunus (AS) was saved not only because of his dua in that moment, but because of a lifetime of closeness to Allah that made that dua sincere and accepted.

chapters.title: The Answer and the Miracle
chapters.content:
Allah's response to Yunus's sincere call was immediate and merciful.

فَٱسْتَجَبْنَا لَهُۥ وَنَجَّيْنَٰهُ مِنَ ٱلْغَمِّ ۚ وَكَذَٰلِكَ نُۨجِى ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ

"So We responded to him and saved him from the distress. And thus do We save the believers."

— Surah Al-Anbiya 21:88

Allah responded to him and saved him from his distress — and Allah reminds us that this is how He saves all believers who turn to Him sincerely. This single verse holds a universal promise, not limited to Yunus (AS) alone.

The fish released him onto dry land, but in a weakened, ill state.

۞ فَنَبَذْنَٰهُ بِٱلْعَرَآءِ وَهُوَ سَقِيمٌۭ

"But We threw him onto the open shore while he was ill."

— Surah As-Saffat 37:145

Allah didn't simply save him and leave him to recover alone — He provided for him directly.

وَأَنۢبَتْنَا عَلَيْهِ شَجَرَةًۭ مِّن يَقْطِينٍۢ

"And We caused to grow over him a gourd vine."

— Surah As-Saffat 37:146

A gourd vine grew over him, giving him shade and nourishment as his body recovered from the ordeal — a small but meaningful mercy after such hardship.

Then Yunus (AS) returned to his mission, this time with Allah's full support.

وَأَرْسَلْنَٰهُ إِلَىٰ مِا۟ئَةِ أَلْفٍ أَوْ يَزِيدُونَ

"And We sent him to [his people of] a hundred thousand or more."

— Surah As-Saffat 37:147

And the result of this second mission was immediate.

فَـَٔامَنُوا۟ فَمَتَّعْنَٰهُمْ إِلَىٰ حِينٍۢ

"And they believed, so We gave them enjoyment [of life] for a time."

— Surah As-Saffat 37:148

He was sent back to his people — a community of over a hundred thousand — and remarkably, they believed. Allah granted them enjoyment of life for a time as a result of their faith.

This miracle is so significant that Allah highlights it elsewhere in the Quran as something unique among nations.

فَلَوْلَا كَانَتْ قَرْيَةٌ ءَامَنَتْ فَنَفَعَهَآ إِيمَٰنُهَآ إِلَّا قَوْمَ يُونُسَ لَمَّآ ءَامَنُوا۟ كَشَفْنَا عَنْهُمْ عَذَابَ ٱلْخِزْىِ فِى ٱلْحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا وَمَتَّعْنَٰهُمْ إِلَىٰ حِينٍۢ

"Then has there not been a [single] city that believed so its faith benefited it except the people of Jonah? When they believed, We removed from them the punishment of disgrace in worldly life and gave them enjoyment [i.e., provision] for a time."

— Surah Yunus 10:98

Allah points out something extraordinary: throughout history, very few entire communities believed all at once and had that belief genuinely benefit them — except the people of Yunus (AS). When they believed, Allah lifted the punishment of disgrace from them in this world and gave them provision for a time.

The story of Yunus (AS) closes with a powerful reminder for every believer: no matter how dark the moment, no matter the mistake that led you there, sincere return to Allah is always met with His mercy — and sometimes, that mercy extends far beyond just the one who called upon Him.

title: The Story of Nuh (AS) — Grateful Servant of Allah
subject: Nuh
summary: Nuh (AS) called his people to Allah for 950 years with patience and clarity. His story teaches perseverance in calling others to truth, even when faced with constant rejection.

chapters.title: Sent to a Corrupt People
chapters.content:
Long ago, the people of Nuh (AS) had turned away from Allah and begun worshipping idols instead. Allah chose Nuh and sent him with an urgent warning for his people.

إِنَّآ أَرْسَلْنَا نُوحًا إِلَىٰ قَوْمِهِۦٓ أَنْ أَنذِرْ قَوْمَكَ مِن قَبْلِ أَن يَأْتِيَهُمْ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌۭ

"Indeed, We sent Noah to his people, [saying], 'Warn your people before there comes to them a painful punishment.'"

— Surah Nuh 71:1

Nuh (AS) wasted no time. He stood before his people and told them plainly who he was — not a poet, not a fortune-teller, but someone sent by Allah to warn them clearly, with no confusion about his message.

قَالَ يَٰقَوْمِ إِنِّى لَكُمْ نَذِيرٌۭ مُّبِينٌ

"He said, 'O my people, indeed I am to you a clear warner —'"

— Surah Nuh 71:2

His message was simple and direct: worship Allah alone, be mindful of Him, and obey what he was telling them.

أَنِ ٱعْبُدُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ وَٱتَّقُوهُ وَأَطِيعُونِ

"'To worship Allāh, fear Him and obey me.'"

— Surah Nuh 71:3

This one message — worship Allah, fear Him, obey His messenger — became the heart of everything Nuh (AS) would repeat for the next 950 years, no matter how his people responded.

chapters.title: 950 Years of Calling
chapters.content:
Nuh (AS) did not call his people for a few years and give up. He kept calling them for centuries, day and night, without rest.

قَالَ رَبِّ إِنِّى دَعَوْتُ قَوْمِى لَيْلًۭا وَنَهَارًۭا

"He said, 'My Lord, indeed I invited my people [to truth] night and day.'"

— Surah Nuh 71:5

He tried every way to reach their hearts. Sometimes he spoke to them openly, in front of everyone.

ثُمَّ إِنِّى دَعَوْتُهُمْ جِهَارًۭا

"'Then I invited them publicly.'"

— Surah Nuh 71:8

Other times he spoke to them privately, one person at a time, and other times he announced his message loudly. He used every method he could think of to help his people understand.

ثُمَّ إِنِّىٓ أَعْلَنتُ لَهُمْ وَأَسْرَرْتُ لَهُمْ إِسْرَارًۭا

"'Then I announced to them and [also] confided to them secretly'"

— Surah Nuh 71:9

Allah tells us exactly how long Nuh (AS) continued this mission — a number that shows just how patient he truly was.

وَلَقَدْ أَرْسَلْنَا نُوحًا إِلَىٰ قَوْمِهِۦ فَلَبِثَ فِيهِمْ أَلْفَ سَنَةٍ إِلَّا خَمْسِينَ عَامًۭا فَأَخَذَهُمُ ٱلطُّوفَانُ وَهُمْ ظَٰلِمُونَ

"And We certainly sent Noah to his people, and he remained among them a thousand years minus fifty years, and the flood seized them while they were wrongdoers."

— Surah Al-Ankabut 29:14

Nine hundred and fifty years of calling people to the truth. Most of his people still refused to believe, but Nuh (AS) never stopped trying, never lost hope, and never gave up his duty to Allah.

chapters.title: The Command to Build the Ark
chapters.content:
After centuries of calling his people with no success, Allah told Nuh (AS) that the time for warning was over. A different kind of command came.

فَأَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَيْهِ أَنِ ٱصْنَعِ ٱلْفُلْكَ بِأَعْيُنِنَا وَوَحْيِنَا فَإِذَا جَآءَ أَمْرُنَا وَفَارَ ٱلتَّنُّورُ ۙ فَٱسْلُكْ فِيهَا مِن كُلٍّۢ زَوْجَيْنِ ٱثْنَيْنِ وَأَهْلَكَ إِلَّا مَن سَبَقَ عَلَيْهِ ٱلْقَوْلُ مِنْهُمْ ۖ وَلَا تُخَٰطِبْنِى فِى ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوٓا۟ ۖ إِنَّهُم مُّغْرَقُونَ

"So We inspired to him, 'Construct the ship under Our observation and Our inspiration, and when Our command comes and the oven overflows, put into it [i.e., the ship] from each [creature] two mates and your family, except him for whom the decree [of destruction] has proceeded. And do not address Me concerning those who have wronged; indeed, they are to be drowned.'"

— Surah Al-Mu'minun 23:27

Allah told Nuh (AS) exactly what to do: build a ship, under Allah's own guidance and protection. When the moment came and water began bursting out everywhere, he was to bring two of every kind of creature onto the ship, along with his family — except those who had already been judged. Nuh (AS) was told not to argue on behalf of the wrongdoers anymore; their fate was already decided.

وَٱصْنَعِ ٱلْفُلْكَ بِأَعْيُنِنَا وَوَحْيِنَا وَلَا تُخَٰطِبْنِى فِى ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوٓا۟ ۚ إِنَّهُم مُّغْرَقُونَ

"And construct the ship under Our observation and Our inspiration and do not address Me concerning those who have wronged; indeed, they are [to be] drowned."

— Surah Hud 11:37

Allah repeated this same instruction in another part of the Quran, making the command unmistakably clear — build the ship, and stop pleading for those who had chosen to disbelieve.

As Nuh (AS) began building this massive ship — likely far from any sea or river — his own people walked by and laughed at him.

وَيَصْنَعُ ٱلْفُلْكَ وَكُلَّمَا مَرَّ عَلَيْهِ مَلَأٌۭ مِّن قَوْمِهِۦ سَخِرُوا۟ مِنْهُ ۚ قَالَ إِن تَسْخَرُوا۟ مِنَّا فَإِنَّا نَسْخَرُ مِنكُمْ كَمَا تَسْخَرُونَ

"And he constructed the ship, and whenever an assembly of the eminent of his people passed by him, they ridiculed him. He said, 'If you ridicule us, then we will ridicule you just as you ridicule.'"

— Surah Hud 11:38

Nuh (AS) did not get discouraged by their mockery. He simply told them that the time would come when they would understand exactly who deserved to be laughed at.

chapters.title: The Great Flood
chapters.content:
When Allah's command finally came, the punishment arrived in a way no one could escape. Water poured down from the sky like never before.

فَفَتَحْنَآ أَبْوَٰبَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ بِمَآءٍۢ مُّنْهَمِرٍۢ

"Then We opened the gates of the heaven with rain pouring down"

— Surah Al-Qamar 54:11

At the very same time, water also burst out from the ground itself. The water from the sky and the water from the earth met together, exactly as Allah had already planned.

وَفَجَّرْنَا ٱلْأَرْضَ عُيُونًۭا فَٱلْتَقَى ٱلْمَآءُ عَلَىٰٓ أَمْرٍۢ قَدْ قُدِرَ

"And caused the earth to burst with springs, and the waters met for a matter already predestined."

— Surah Al-Qamar 54:12

The ship sailed through waves as tall as mountains. In the middle of this terrifying scene, Nuh (AS) saw his own son standing apart from the rest, refusing to board the ship. As a father, he called out to him with love and worry.

وَهِىَ تَجْرِى بِهِمْ فِى مَوْجٍۢ كَٱلْجِبَالِ وَنَادَىٰ نُوحٌ ٱبْنَهُۥ وَكَانَ فِى مَعْزِلٍۢ يَٰبُنَىَّ ٱرْكَب مَّعَنَا وَلَا تَكُن مَّعَ ٱلْكَٰفِرِينَ

"And it sailed with them through waves like mountains, and Noah called to his son who was apart [from them], 'O my son, come aboard with us and be not with the disbelievers.'"

— Surah Hud 11:42

His son still refused, believing he could save himself by climbing a high mountain instead of trusting Allah. Nuh (AS) told him the painful truth — that day, nothing could protect anyone except Allah's mercy. Moments later, a wave came between them, and his son was lost to the flood.

قَالَ سَـَٔاوِىٓ إِلَىٰ جَبَلٍۢ يَعْصِمُنِى مِنَ ٱلْمَآءِ ۚ قَالَ لَا عَاصِمَ ٱلْيَوْمَ مِنْ أَمْرِ ٱللَّهِ إِلَّا مَن رَّحِمَ ۚ وَحَالَ بَيْنَهُمَا ٱلْمَوْجُ فَكَانَ مِنَ ٱلْمُغْرَقِينَ

"[But] he said, 'I will take refuge on a mountain to protect me from the water.' [Noah] said, 'There is no protector today from the decree of Allāh, except for whom He gives mercy.' And the waves came between them, and he was among the drowned."

— Surah Hud 11:43

This was one of the hardest moments in Nuh's life — watching his own son choose disbelief over safety, even as the storm raged around them.

chapters.title: The Ark Rests — A New Beginning
chapters.content:
After the flood had done what it was sent to do, Allah commanded the water itself to stop.

وَقِيلَ يَٰٓأَرْضُ ٱبْلَعِى مَآءَكِ وَيَٰسَمَآءُ أَقْلِعِى وَغِيضَ ٱلْمَآءُ وَقُضِىَ ٱلْأَمْرُ وَٱسْتَوَتْ عَلَى ٱلْجُودِىِّ ۖ وَقِيلَ بُعْدًۭا لِّلْقَوْمِ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ

"And it was said, 'O earth, swallow your water, and O sky, withhold [your rain].' And the water subsided, and the matter was accomplished, and it [i.e., the ship] came to rest on the [mountain of] Jūdiyy. And it was said, 'Away with the wrongdoing people.'"

— Surah Hud 11:44

The earth swallowed the water, the sky stopped pouring rain, and the ship finally came to rest on a mountain called Judiyy. The long trial was over, and Allah made clear that the wrongdoers who had rejected Nuh (AS) were gone.

After everything that had happened, Nuh (AS) still carried the pain of losing his son in the flood. He turned to Allah, reminding Him gently that his son was part of his family, and that Allah's promises are always true.

وَنَادَىٰ نُوحٌۭ رَّبَّهُۥ فَقَالَ رَبِّ إِنَّ ٱبْنِى مِنْ أَهْلِى وَإِنَّ وَعْدَكَ ٱلْحَقُّ وَأَنتَ أَحْكَمُ ٱلْحَٰكِمِينَ

"And Noah called to his Lord and said, 'My Lord, indeed my son is of my family; and indeed, Your promise is true; and You are the most just of judges!'"

— Surah Hud 11:45

Allah's response was firm but loving. He explained to Nuh (AS) that his son had not truly been "of his family" in the way that mattered most, because of his choice to disbelieve. Allah reminded Nuh (AS) not to ask about things he didn't have full knowledge of.

قَالَ يَٰنُوحُ إِنَّهُۥ لَيْسَ مِنْ أَهْلِكَ ۖ إِنَّهُۥ عَمَلٌ غَيْرُ صَٰلِحٍۢ ۖ فَلَا تَسْـَٔلْنِ مَا لَيْسَ لَكَ بِهِۦ عِلْمٌ ۖ إِنِّىٓ أَعِظُكَ أَن تَكُونَ مِنَ ٱلْجَٰهِلِينَ

"He said, 'O Noah, indeed he is not of your family; indeed, he is [one whose] work was other than righteous, so ask Me not for that about which you have no knowledge. Indeed, I advise you, lest you be among the ignorant.'"

— Surah Hud 11:46

Nuh (AS) immediately understood. He did not argue or defend himself. Instead, he turned back to Allah straight away, asking for forgiveness for asking something beyond his knowledge.

قَالَ رَبِّ إِنِّىٓ أَعُوذُ بِكَ أَنْ أَسْـَٔلَكَ مَا لَيْسَ لِى بِهِۦ عِلْمٌۭ ۖ وَإِلَّا تَغْفِرْ لِى وَتَرْحَمْنِىٓ أَكُن مِّنَ ٱلْخَٰسِرِينَ

"[Noah] said, 'My Lord, I seek refuge in You from asking that of which I have no knowledge. And unless You forgive me and have mercy upon me, I will be among the losers.'"

— Surah Hud 11:47

This moment teaches us something every believer needs: even a great prophet like Nuh (AS), after 950 years of patience and a lifetime of devotion, still humbly corrected himself the instant Allah pointed it out. True faith means accepting Allah's wisdom, even when it's painful, and turning back to Him quickly when we make a mistake.

title: The Story of Ibrahim (AS) — Khalilullah — Friend of Allah
summary: Ibrahim (AS) stood alone against his people's idol worship, was thrown into fire and emerged unharmed, was tested with the sacrifice of his son, and built the Ka'bah. His unwavering faith earned him the title Khalilullah — Friend of Allah.

chapters.title: Disputing with His Father
chapters.content:
Before Ibrahim (AS) ever confronted his people publicly, he first turned to the person closest to him — his own father, Azar.

۞ وَإِذْ قَالَ إِبْرَٰهِيمُ لِأَبِيهِ ءَازَرَ أَتَتَّخِذُ أَصْنَامًا ءَالِهَةً ۖ إِنِّىٓ أَرَىٰكَ وَقَوْمَكَ فِى ضَلَٰلٍۢ مُّبِينٍۢ

"And [mention, O Muḥammad], when Abraham said to his father Āzar, 'Do you take idols as deities? Indeed, I see you and your people to be in manifest error.'"

— Surah Al-An'am 6:74

Ibrahim (AS) didn't accuse his father harshly. He simply named what he saw clearly: his father and his people were worshipping idols, and this was manifest error. This was the beginning of a private, personal struggle long before any public confrontation.

The conversation continues with remarkable gentleness, despite the seriousness of what Ibrahim (AS) was saying.

إِذْ قَالَ لِأَبِيهِ يَٰٓأَبَتِ لِمَ تَعْبُدُ مَا لَا يَسْمَعُ وَلَا يُبْصِرُ وَلَا يُغْنِى عَنكَ شَيْـًۭٔا

"[Mention] when he said to his father, 'O my father, why do you worship that which does not hear and does not see and will not benefit you at all?'"

— Surah Maryam 19:42

He appealed to his father's reason first — these idols could not hear, could not see, and could offer no real benefit. Why worship something so powerless?

يَٰٓأَبَتِ إِنِّى قَدْ جَآءَنِى مِنَ ٱلْعِلْمِ مَا لَمْ يَأْتِكَ فَٱتَّبِعْنِىٓ أَهْدِكَ صِرَٰطًۭا سَوِيًّۭا

"O my father, indeed there has come to me of knowledge that which has not come to you, so follow me; I will guide you to an even path."

— Surah Maryam 19:43

Ibrahim (AS) didn't claim superiority — he humbly offered what knowledge had reached him, inviting his father to follow him toward a straight path, out of love and concern, not arrogance.

يَٰٓأَبَتِ لَا تَعْبُدِ ٱلشَّيْطَٰنَ ۖ إِنَّ ٱلشَّيْطَٰنَ كَانَ لِلرَّحْمَٰنِ عَصِيًّۭا

"O my father, do not worship [i.e., obey] Satan. Indeed Satan has ever been, to the Most Merciful, disobedient."

— Surah Maryam 19:44

He warned his father plainly: worshipping idols was, in truth, obedience to Satan, who has always been in open defiance of the Most Merciful.

يَٰٓأَبَتِ إِنِّىٓ أَخَافُ أَن يَمَسَّكَ عَذَابٌۭ مِّنَ ٱلرَّحْمَٰنِ فَتَكُونَ لِلشَّيْطَٰنِ وَلِيًّۭا

"O my father, indeed I fear that there will touch you a punishment from the Most Merciful so you would be to Satan a companion [in Hellfire]."

— Surah Maryam 19:45

His fear here is deeply personal — he feared punishment touching his own father, and feared his father becoming an ally of Satan in the Hereafter. This was not a debate Ibrahim (AS) wanted to win; it was his father's soul he was trying to save.

But his father's response revealed how firmly rejection had taken hold.

قَالَ أَرَاغِبٌ أَنتَ عَنْ ءَالِهَتِى يَٰٓإِبْرَٰهِيمُ ۖ لَئِن لَّمْ تَنتَهِ لَأَرْجُمَنَّكَ ۖ وَٱهْجُرْنِى مَلِيًّۭا

"[His father] said, 'Have you no desire for my gods, O Abraham? If you do not desist, I will surely stone you, so avoid me a prolonged time.'"

— Surah Maryam 19:46

Rather than reflecting, his father turned to threats — accusing Ibrahim (AS) of turning away from "his gods" and threatening to stone him if he persisted, demanding he leave for good. This rejection from his own father, the person who should have loved and protected him most, set the stage for everything that would follow — a believer standing alone, even against his own family, for the sake of truth.

chapters.title: Breaking the Idols
chapters.content:
Having failed to convince his father privately, Ibrahim (AS) turned to question his entire people about the very foundation of their worship.

إِذْ قَالَ لِأَبِيهِ وَقَوْمِهِۦ مَا هَٰذِهِ ٱلتَّمَاثِيلُ ٱلَّتِىٓ أَنتُمْ لَهَا عَٰكِفُونَ

"When he said to his father and his people, 'What are these statues to which you are devoted?'"

— Surah Al-Anbiya 21:52

He asked them directly — what exactly were these statues they devoted themselves to so completely?

قَالُوا۟ وَجَدْنَآ ءَابَآءَنَا لَهَا عَٰبِدِينَ

"They said, 'We found our fathers worshippers of them.'"

— Surah Al-Anbiya 21:53

Their answer revealed the real basis of their belief: not reason, not evidence, but simple inherited tradition. They worshipped these idols only because their forefathers had done so before them.

قَالَ لَقَدْ كُنتُمْ أَنتُمْ وَءَابَآؤُكُمْ فِى ضَلَٰلٍۢ مُّبِينٍۢ

"He said, 'You were certainly, you and your fathers, in manifest error.'"

— Surah Al-Anbiya 21:54

Ibrahim (AS) responded without hesitation — both they and their ancestors had been in manifest, undeniable error. Blind tradition is never proof of truth.

Quietly, Ibrahim (AS) made a decision.

وَتَٱللَّهِ لَأَكِيدَنَّ أَصْنَٰمَكُم بَعْدَ أَن تُوَلُّوا۟ مُدْبِرِينَ

"And [I swear] by Allāh, I will surely plan against your idols after you have turned and gone away."

— Surah Al-Anbiya 21:57

He vowed — by Allah Himself — that he would act against these idols once the people turned away. This wasn't impulsive; it was a deliberate plan to demonstrate their powerlessness.

فَجَعَلَهُمْ جُذَٰذًا إِلَّا كَبِيرًۭا لَّهُمْ لَعَلَّهُمْ إِلَيْهِ يَرْجِعُونَ

"So he made them into fragments, except a large one among them, that they might return to it [and question]."

— Surah Al-Anbiya 21:58

When the moment came, he shattered every idol except the largest one, leaving it deliberately intact — so that when the people returned, they would be forced to question it themselves.

The people's reaction was immediate outrage.

قَالُوا۟ مَن فَعَلَ هَٰذَا بِـَٔالِهَتِنَآ إِنَّهُۥ لَمِنَ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ

"They said, 'Who has done this to our gods? Indeed, he is of the wrongdoers.'"

— Surah Al-Anbiya 21:59

They demanded to know who had done this to their gods, certain that whoever it was deserved to be called a wrongdoer.

قَالُوٓا۟ ءَأَنتَ فَعَلْتَ هَٰذَا بِـَٔالِهَتِنَا يَٰٓإِبْرَٰهِيمُ

"They said, 'Have you done this to our gods, O Abraham?'"

— Surah Al-Anbiya 21:62

Word spread, and they confronted Ibrahim (AS) directly, asking if he was responsible.

قَالَ بَلْ فَعَلَهُۥ كَبِيرُهُمْ هَٰذَا فَسْـَٔلُوهُمْ إِن كَانُوا۟ يَنطِقُونَ

"He said, 'Rather, this - the largest of them - did it, so ask them, if they should [be able to] speak.'"

— Surah Al-Anbiya 21:63

His answer was deliberately ironic — he pointed to the very idol he had spared, telling them to ask it themselves, if it could speak. The point wasn't to lie; it was to expose, through their own logic, the absurdity of worshipping something that couldn't even defend or explain itself.

And remarkably, it worked.

فَرَجَعُوٓا۟ إِلَىٰٓ أَنفُسِهِمْ فَقَالُوٓا۟ إِنَّكُمْ أَنتُمُ ٱلظَّٰلِمُونَ

"So they returned to [blaming] themselves and said [to each other], 'Indeed, you are the wrongdoers.'"

— Surah Al-Anbiya 21:64

For a brief moment, they turned inward and acknowledged the truth — that they themselves were the wrongdoers, not Ibrahim (AS). Even those most attached to falsehood can recognize truth, if only for a moment, when confronted with it clearly.

chapters.title: Thrown into the Fire
chapters.content:
Even after momentarily acknowledging their own wrongdoing, the people's pride quickly took over again.

ثُمَّ نُكِسُوا۟ عَلَىٰ رُءُوسِهِمْ لَقَدْ عَلِمْتَ مَا هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ يَنطِقُونَ

"Then they reversed themselves, [saying], 'You have already known that these do not speak!'"

— Surah Al-Anbiya 21:65

They reversed course, hardening themselves against the very truth they had just admitted — insisting, almost absurdly, that Ibrahim (AS) already knew these idols couldn't speak, as if this somehow excused their worship of them.

Ibrahim (AS) didn't relent. He pressed the question further.

قَالَ أَفَتَعْبُدُونَ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ مَا لَا يَنفَعُكُمْ شَيْـًۭٔا وَلَا يَضُرُّكُمْ

"He said, 'Then do you worship instead of Allāh that which does not benefit you at all or harm you?'"

— Surah Al-Anbiya 21:66

Why worship something that could neither benefit nor harm them in any way? The logic was undeniable, yet their hearts remained closed.

أُفٍّۢ لَّكُمْ وَلِمَا تَعْبُدُونَ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ ۖ أَفَلَا تَعْقِلُونَ

"Uff to you and to what you worship instead of Allāh. Then will you not use reason?"

— Surah Al-Anbiya 21:67

His exasperation here is genuine — "Uff to you" is an expression of real frustration. He directly questioned their reasoning: how could intelligent people continue worshipping something so powerless?

Unable to answer his logic, they turned to violence instead.

قَالُوا۟ حَرِّقُوهُ وَٱنصُرُوٓا۟ ءَالِهَتَكُمْ إِن كُنتُمْ فَٰعِلِينَ

"They said, 'Burn him and support your gods - if you are to act.'"

— Surah Al-Anbiya 21:68

Their response revealed the depth of their inability to counter him with reason — they called for him to be burned, framing it as defending their gods, when in truth it was simply rage at being exposed.

A massive fire was prepared, and Ibrahim (AS) was cast into it. But Allah's command overruled every law of nature in that moment.

قُلْنَا يَٰنَارُ كُونِى بَرْدًۭا وَسَلَٰمًا عَلَىٰٓ إِبْرَٰهِيمَ

"We [i.e., Allāh] said, 'O fire, be coolness and safety upon Abraham.'"

— Surah Al-Anbiya 21:69

Allah commanded the fire itself — not to be extinguished, not to simply spare him, but to become coolness and safety specifically for Ibrahim (AS). The fire retained its nature for everything else, yet became gentle and protective for the one who trusted Allah completely.

وَأَرَادُوا۟ بِهِۦ كَيْدًۭا فَجَعَلْنَٰهُمُ ٱلْأَخْسَرِينَ

"And they intended for him a plan [i.e., harm], but We made them the greatest losers."

— Surah Al-Anbiya 21:70

What they had intended as the ultimate harm became, instead, the clearest proof of Allah's power and Ibrahim's truthfulness. Those who plotted against him became the greatest losers — humiliated by their own failed scheme, while Ibrahim (AS) emerged from the fire completely unharmed, his faith now undeniable before all who witnessed it.

chapters.title: Seeking Certainty — The Debate with Nimrod & the Four Birds
chapters.content:
After the miracle of the fire, Ibrahim (AS) faced another kind of challenge — a king who believed his own power made him equal to Allah.

أَلَمْ تَرَ إِلَى ٱلَّذِى حَآجَّ إِبْرَٰهِۦمَ فِى رَبِّهِۦٓ أَنْ ءَاتَىٰهُ ٱللَّهُ ٱلْمُلْكَ إِذْ قَالَ إِبْرَٰهِۦمُ رَبِّىَ ٱلَّذِى يُحْىِۦ وَيُمِيتُ قَالَ أَنَا۠ أُحْىِۦ وَأُمِيتُ ۖ قَالَ إِبْرَٰهِۦمُ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَأْتِى بِٱلشَّمْسِ مِنَ ٱلْمَشْرِقِ فَأْتِ بِهَا مِنَ ٱلْمَغْرِبِ فَبُهِتَ ٱلَّذِى كَفَرَ ۗ وَٱللَّهُ لَا يَهْدِى ٱلْقَوْمَ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ

"Have you not considered the one who argued with Abraham about his Lord [merely] because Allāh had given him kingship? When Abraham said, 'My Lord is the one who gives life and causes death,' he said, 'I give life and cause death.' Abraham said, 'Indeed, Allāh brings up the sun from the east, so bring it up from the west.' So the disbeliever was overwhelmed [by astonishment], and Allāh does not guide the wrongdoing people."

— Surah Al-Baqarah 2:258

This king, emboldened by the authority Allah had given him, argued with Ibrahim (AS) about the very nature of his Lord. When Ibrahim (AS) described Allah as the one who gives life and causes death, the king arrogantly claimed he could do the same — likely referring to his power to pardon or execute people, mistaking worldly authority for true creation.

Ibrahim (AS) didn't argue back with abstract theology. He pointed to something undeniable and beyond any human's control.

He challenged the king to bring the sun from the west, since Allah brings it from the east every single day without fail. The king had no answer. He was utterly silenced, overwhelmed by a challenge no human power could ever meet. This is one of the clearest examples in the Quran of how true faith can dismantle false arrogance — not through anger, but through simple, undeniable truth.

In a separate, deeply personal moment, Ibrahim (AS) sought something for himself — not to prove a point to others, but to deepen his own certainty.

وَإِذْ قَالَ إِبْرَٰهِۦمُ رَبِّ أَرِنِى كَيْفَ تُحْىِ ٱلْمَوْتَىٰ ۖ قَالَ أَوَلَمْ تُؤْمِن ۖ قَالَ بَلَىٰ وَلَٰكِن لِّيَطْمَئِنَّ قَلْبِى ۖ قَالَ فَخُذْ أَرْبَعَةًۭ مِّنَ ٱلطَّيْرِ فَصُرْهُنَّ إِلَيْكَ ثُمَّ ٱجْعَلْ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ جَبَلٍۢ مِّنْهُنَّ جُزْءًۭا ثُمَّ ٱدْعُهُنَّ يَأْتِينَكَ سَعْيًۭا ۚ وَٱعْلَمْ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَزِيزٌ حَكِيمٌۭ

"And [mention] when Abraham said, 'My Lord, show me how You give life to the dead.' [Allāh] said, 'Have you not believed?' He said, 'Yes, but [I ask] only that my heart may be satisfied.' [Allāh] said, 'Take four birds and commit them to yourself. Then [after slaughtering them] put on each hill a portion of them; then call them - they will come [flying] to you in haste. And know that Allāh is Exalted in Might and Wise.'"

— Surah Al-Baqarah 2:260

He asked Allah directly to show him how the dead are brought back to life. Allah's response wasn't a rebuke — it was a gentle question: had he not already believed? Ibrahim (AS) affirmed his faith immediately, clarifying that his request wasn't born of doubt, but a desire for his heart to feel that certainty directly, not just intellectually accept it.

Allah's instruction was specific and remarkable — take four birds, become familiar with them, then place a portion of each on different hills, and call them. They would return to him, alive and whole, flying back from every direction. This was Allah teaching him — and every believer after him — a profound truth: seeking certainty in faith is not a flaw, and Allah welcomes sincere hearts that wish to know Him more deeply, not less.

chapters.title: The Sacrifice of Ismail
chapters.content:
Years earlier, Ibrahim (AS) had made a heartfelt request to Allah.

رَبِّ هَبْ لِى مِنَ ٱلصَّٰلِحِينَ

"My Lord, grant me [a child] from among the righteous.'"

— Surah As-Saffat 37:100

He asked simply for a righteous child. Allah answered this dua generously.

فَبَشَّرْنَٰهُ بِغُلَٰمٍ حَلِيمٍۢ

"So We gave him good tidings of a forbearing boy."

— Surah As-Saffat 37:101

Allah gave him glad tidings of a son who would grow to be forbearing and patient — a quality that would soon be tested in the most extraordinary way imaginable.

Years passed, and that son grew old enough to walk and work alongside his father.

فَلَمَّا بَلَغَ مَعَهُ ٱلسَّعْىَ قَالَ يَٰبُنَىَّ إِنِّىٓ أَرَىٰ فِى ٱلْمَنَامِ أَنِّىٓ أَذْبَحُكَ فَٱنظُرْ مَاذَا تَرَىٰ ۚ قَالَ يَٰٓأَبَتِ ٱفْعَلْ مَا تُؤْمَرُ ۖ سَتَجِدُنِىٓ إِن شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ مِنَ ٱلصَّٰبِرِينَ

"And when he reached with him [the age of] exertion, he said, 'O my son, indeed I have seen in a dream that I [must] sacrifice you, so see what you think.' He said, 'O my father, do as you are commanded. You will find me, if Allāh wills, of the steadfast.'"

— Surah As-Saffat 37:102

Ibrahim (AS) saw a vision — that he was to sacrifice his own son. Rather than acting alone or hiding this from Ismail, he shared it with him directly, asking for his perspective. Ismail's response is among the most remarkable statements of submission in the entire Quran: he didn't plead, didn't resist — he told his father to carry out what he had been commanded, and expressed his own hope that he would be found patient through it, with Allah's will.

Both father and son moved forward together in complete submission to Allah.

فَلَمَّآ أَسْلَمَا وَتَلَّهُۥ لِلْجَبِينِ

"And when they had both submitted and he put him down upon his forehead,"

— Surah As-Saffat 37:103

Both had submitted fully — Ibrahim (AS) to the command, and Ismail to his fate — and the moment for the sacrifice had come.

But at the very last moment, Allah intervened.

وَنَٰدَيْنَٰهُ أَن يَٰٓإِبْرَٰهِيمُ

"We called to him, 'O Abraham,'"

— Surah As-Saffat 37:104

Allah called out to Ibrahim (AS) directly, by name.

قَدْ صَدَّقْتَ ٱلرُّءْيَآ ۚ إِنَّا كَذَٰلِكَ نَجْزِى ٱلْمُحْسِنِينَ

"You have fulfilled the vision.' Indeed, We thus reward the doers of good."

— Surah As-Saffat 37:105

He had already fulfilled the vision — not in the act of sacrifice itself, but in his complete willingness to carry it out. Allah rewards those who strive to do good in this way, regardless of the outcome He ultimately decrees.

إِنَّ هَٰذَا لَهُوَ ٱلْبَلَٰٓؤُا۟ ٱلْمُبِينُ

"Indeed, this was the clear trial."

— Surah As-Saffat 37:106

Allah names this moment exactly as it was — a clear, unmistakable trial, one that tested the depths of both Ibrahim's and Ismail's devotion.

وَفَدَيْنَٰهُ بِذِبْحٍ عَظِيمٍۢ

"And We ransomed him with a great sacrifice,"

— Surah As-Saffat 37:107

In place of Ismail, Allah provided a great sacrifice instead — sparing his life entirely. This single moment, this complete willingness of a father and son to submit fully to Allah's command, is commemorated by Muslims every year during Eid al-Adha, a reminder that true faith means trusting Allah's command even when it demands everything we hold dear.

chapters.title: Building the Ka'bah & the Dua for Makkah
chapters.content:
Together with his son, Ibrahim (AS) undertook one of the most significant acts of his life — raising the very foundations of the House of Allah.

وَإِذْ يَرْفَعُ إِبْرَٰهِۦمُ ٱلْقَوَاعِدَ مِنَ ٱلْبَيْتِ وَإِسْمَٰعِيلُ رَبَّنَا تَقَبَّلْ مِنَّآ ۖ إِنَّكَ أَنتَ ٱلسَّمِيعُ ٱلْعَلِيمُ

"And [mention] when Abraham was raising the foundations of the House and [with him] Ishmael, [saying], 'Our Lord, accept [this] from us. Indeed, You are the Hearing, the Knowing.'"

— Surah Al-Baqarah 2:127

Ibrahim (AS) and Ismail worked side by side, raising the foundations of the House together. As they built, they didn't take pride in their effort — instead, they turned to Allah, asking Him simply to accept this work from them, acknowledging that He alone truly hears and knows.

Their dua continued, reaching far beyond just the building itself.

رَبَّنَا وَٱجْعَلْنَا مُسْلِمَيْنِ لَكَ وَمِن ذُرِّيَّتِنَآ أُمَّةًۭ مُّسْلِمَةًۭ لَّكَ وَأَرِنَا مَنَاسِكَنَا وَتُبْ عَلَيْنَآ ۖ إِنَّكَ أَنتَ ٱلتَّوَّابُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ

"Our Lord, and make us Muslims [in submission] to You and from our descendants a Muslim nation [in submission] to You. And show us our rites [of worship] and accept our repentance. Indeed, You are the Accepting of Repentance, the Merciful."

— Surah Al-Baqarah 2:128

They asked Allah to make them both fully submitted to Him, and asked something even greater — that their descendants become an entire nation submitted to Allah. They asked to be shown the correct rites of worship, and for their repentance to be accepted, acknowledging Allah as the Accepting, the Merciful.

Then came perhaps the most far-reaching part of their dua — a request not just for guidance, but for a messenger to come generations later.

رَبَّنَا وَٱبْعَثْ فِيهِمْ رَسُولًۭا مِّنْهُمْ يَتْلُوا۟ عَلَيْهِمْ ءَايَٰتِكَ وَيُعَلِّمُهُمُ ٱلْكِتَٰبَ وَٱلْحِكْمَةَ وَيُزَكِّيهِمْ ۚ إِنَّكَ أَنتَ ٱلْعَزِيزُ ٱلْحَكِيمُ

"Our Lord, and send among them a messenger from themselves who will recite to them Your verses and teach them the Book and wisdom and purify them. Indeed, You are the Exalted in Might, the Wise."

— Surah Al-Baqarah 2:129

They asked Allah to send a messenger from among their own descendants — one who would recite Allah's verses, teach the Book and wisdom, and purify the people. Muslims believe this dua found its ultimate fulfillment centuries later in the sending of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, a descendant of Ismail (AS), confirming how far-reaching Ibrahim's prayer truly was.

Alongside building the Ka'bah, Ibrahim (AS) also prayed specifically for the safety and provision of the city itself.

وَإِذْ قَالَ إِبْرَٰهِۦمُ رَبِّ ٱجْعَلْ هَٰذَا بَلَدًا ءَامِنًۭا وَٱرْزُقْ أَهْلَهُۥ مِنَ ٱلثَّمَرَٰتِ مَنْ ءَامَنَ مِنْهُم بِٱللَّهِ وَٱلْيَوْمِ ٱلْءَاخِرِ ۖ قَالَ وَمَن كَفَرَ فَأُمَتِّعُهُۥ قَلِيلًۭا ثُمَّ أَضْطَرُّهُۥٓ إِلَىٰ عَذَابِ ٱلنَّارِ ۖ وَبِئْسَ ٱلْمَصِيرُ

"And [mention] when Abraham said, 'My Lord, make this a secure city and provide its people with fruits - whoever of them believes in Allāh and the Last Day.' [Allāh] said, 'And whoever disbelieves - I will grant him enjoyment for a little; then I will force him to the punishment of the Fire, and wretched is the destination.'"

— Surah Al-Baqarah 2:126

He asked Allah to make this city secure, and to provide its people with fruits — specifically for those who believed in Allah and the Last Day. Allah's response carried both mercy and warning: even those who disbelieve would be granted some worldly enjoyment, but ultimately their destination would be one of consequence. Ibrahim's prayer for Makkah's security and provision continues to be felt today, in a city that draws people from every nation, just as he had asked.

chapters.title: Khalilullah — Friend of Allah
chapters.content:
Of all the prophets, Ibrahim (AS) was given a title unlike any other — one that captures the depth of his relationship with his Creator.

وَمَنْ أَحْسَنُ دِينًۭا مِّمَّنْ أَسْلَمَ وَجْهَهُۥ لِلَّهِ وَهُوَ مُحْسِنٌۭ وَٱتَّبَعَ مِلَّةَ إِبْرَٰهِيمَ حَنِيفًۭا ۗ وَٱتَّخَذَ ٱللَّهُ إِبْرَٰهِيمَ خَلِيلًۭا

"And who is better in religion than one who submits himself to Allāh while being a doer of good and follows the religion of Abraham, inclining toward truth? And Allāh took Abraham as an intimate friend."

— Surah An-Nisa 4:125

Allah asks who could possibly have better religion than one who submits fully to Him while doing good, following the way of Ibrahim (AS), who inclined wholly toward truth. And then comes the remarkable statement: Allah took Ibrahim (AS) as an intimate friend — Khalil. This is a unique honor, reflecting not just obedience, but a depth of closeness and love between Ibrahim (AS) and his Lord.

Allah describes the qualities that earned him this honor.

إِنَّ إِبْرَٰهِيمَ كَانَ أُمَّةًۭ قَانِتًۭا لِّلَّهِ حَنِيفًۭا وَلَمْ يَكُ مِنَ ٱلْمُشْرِكِينَ

"Indeed, Abraham was a [comprehensive] leader, devoutly obedient to Allāh, inclining toward truth, and he was not of those who associate others with Allāh."

— Surah An-Nahl 16:120

He is described as "an Ummah" — a nation unto himself — devoutly obedient, inclined entirely toward truth, never associating anything with Allah in worship.

شَاكِرًۭا لِّأَنْعُمِهِ ۚ ٱجْتَبَىٰهُ وَهَدَىٰهُ إِلَىٰ صِرَٰطٍۢ مُّسْتَقِيمٍۢ

"[He was] grateful for His favors. He [i.e., Allāh] chose him and guided him to a straight path."

— Surah An-Nahl 16:121

He was grateful for every favor Allah gave him, and in turn, Allah chose him and guided him to a straight path.

وَءَاتَيْنَٰهُ فِى ٱلدُّنْيَا حَسَنَةًۭ ۖ وَإِنَّهُۥ فِى ٱلْءَاخِرَةِ لَمِنَ ٱلصَّٰلِحِينَ

"And We gave him good in this world, and indeed, in the Hereafter he will be among the righteous."

— Surah An-Nahl 16:122

Allah granted him good in this worldly life, and confirms that in the Hereafter, he is among the righteous — a promise fulfilled both in this life and the next.

ثُمَّ أَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَيْكَ أَنِ ٱتَّبِعْ مِلَّةَ إِبْرَٰهِيمَ حَنِيفًۭا ۖ وَمَا كَانَ مِنَ ٱلْمُشْرِكِينَ

"Then We revealed to you, [O Muḥammad], to follow the religion of Abraham, inclining toward truth; and he was not of those who associate with Allāh."

— Surah An-Nahl 16:123

Allah then commands Prophet Muhammad ﷺ directly to follow the religion of Ibrahim (AS) — inclining toward truth, free from associating partners with Allah. This connects Ibrahim's legacy directly to the final message brought to all of humanity.

Even his harshest critics could find no real fault with his way.

وَمَن يَرْغَبُ عَن مِّلَّةِ إِبْرَٰهِۦمَ إِلَّا مَن سَفِهَ نَفْسَهُۥ ۚ وَلَقَدِ ٱصْطَفَيْنَٰهُ فِى ٱلدُّنْيَا ۖ وَإِنَّهُۥ فِى ٱلْءَاخِرَةِ لَمِنَ ٱلصَّٰلِحِينَ

"And who would be averse to the religion of Abraham except one who makes a fool of himself. And We had chosen him in this world, and indeed he, in the Hereafter, will be among the righteous."

— Surah Al-Baqarah 2:130

Allah states plainly that only a fool would turn away from the religion of Ibrahim (AS) — a man Allah Himself chose in this world, destined for righteousness in the next.

His entire life is summarized in a single, complete moment of submission.

إِذْ قَالَ لَهُۥ رَبُّهُۥٓ أَسْلِمْ ۖ قَالَ أَسْلَمْتُ لِرَبِّ ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ

"When his Lord said to him, 'Submit,' he said, 'I have submitted [in Islām] to the Lord of the worlds.'"

— Surah Al-Baqarah 2:131

When Allah commanded him to submit, his answer held nothing back — complete submission to the Lord of all the worlds, without hesitation or condition.

And in his final years, Ibrahim (AS) left something behind for his own children — not wealth, not status, but the one thing that truly mattered.

وَوَصَّىٰ بِهَآ إِبْرَٰهِۦمُ بَنِيهِ وَيَعْقُوبُ يَٰبَنِىَّ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ ٱصْطَفَىٰ لَكُمُ ٱلدِّينَ فَلَا تَمُوتُنَّ إِلَّا وَأَنتُم مُّسْلِمُونَ

"And Abraham instructed his sons [to do the same] and [so did] Jacob, [saying], 'O my sons, indeed Allāh has chosen for you this religion, so do not die except while you are Muslims.'"

— Surah Al-Baqarah 2:132

He instructed his sons — and Yaqub (AS) did the same for his own children after him — that Allah had chosen this religion for them, and they should not let death come upon them except in a state of complete submission to Allah.

This is how the story of Ibrahim (AS) closes — not with idols, not with fire, not even with the sacrifice, but with a legacy passed down through generations: complete trust in Allah, complete submission to His command, and complete gratitude for His favors. He remains, to this day, a model for every believer who seeks to walk the same path — the path of Khalilullah, the Friend of Allah.

title: The Story of Musa (AS) — Kalimullah — One who spoke to Allah
summary: Musa (AS) was raised in Pharaoh's palace, called to prophethood at the burning bush, confronted the tyranny of Pharaoh with miraculous signs, led his people out of Egypt through the parted sea, and received the Torah on Mount Sinai. His is the most extensively narrated story in the Quran.

chapters.title: Born Under Pharaoh's Shadow
chapters.content:
Musa (AS) was born during one of the darkest periods for the Israelites — Pharaoh had ordered the killing of every newborn son among them, fearing they would one day rise against him. In this terrifying context, Allah gave his mother specific instructions.

وَأَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَىٰٓ أُمِّ مُوسَىٰٓ أَنْ أَرْضِعِيهِ ۖ فَإِذَا خِفْتِ عَلَيْهِ فَأَلْقِيهِ فِى ٱلْيَمِّ وَلَا تَخَافِى وَلَا تَحْزَنِىٓ ۖ إِنَّا رَآدُّوهُ إِلَيْكِ وَجَاعِلُوهُ مِنَ ٱلْمُرْسَلِينَ

"And We inspired to the mother of Moses, 'Suckle him; but when you fear for him, cast him into the river and do not fear and do not grieve. Indeed, We will return him to you and will make him [one] of the messengers.'"

— Surah Al-Qasas 28:7

Allah inspired her directly — to nurse him, and when she feared for his safety, to place him in the river without fear or grief, with a promise: Allah would return him to her, and he would become one of the messengers. This promise, given before anything had even happened, is a profound display of trust required of her.

What happened next seems, by every human measure, like the worst possible outcome.

فَٱلْتَقَطَهُۥٓ ءَالُ فِرْعَوْنَ لِيَكُونَ لَهُمْ عَدُوًّۭا وَحَزَنًا ۗ إِنَّ فِرْعَوْنَ وَهَٰمَٰنَ وَجُنُودَهُمَا كَانُوا۟ خَٰطِـِٔينَ

"And the family of Pharaoh picked him up [out of the river] so that he would become to them an enemy and a [cause of] grief. Indeed, Pharaoh and Hāmān and their soldiers were deliberate sinners."

— Surah Al-Qasas 28:8

Pharaoh's own family retrieved him from the river — the very household that posed the greatest danger to him. Allah notes that Pharaoh, Haman, and their forces were deliberate sinners, yet even their actions would unknowingly serve Allah's plan.

But then something unexpected happened within that household.

وَقَالَتِ ٱمْرَأَتُ فِرْعَوْنَ قُرَّتُ عَيْنٍۢ لِّى وَلَكَ ۖ لَا تَقْتُلُوهُ عَسَىٰٓ أَن يَنفَعَنَآ أَوْ نَتَّخِذَهُۥ وَلَدًۭا وَهُمْ لَا يَشْعُرُونَ

"And the wife of Pharaoh said, '[He will be] a comfort of the eye [i.e., pleasure] for me and for you. Do not kill him; perhaps he may benefit us, or we may adopt him as a son.' And they perceived not."

— Surah Al-Qasas 28:9

Pharaoh's wife saw the infant and felt an immediate tenderness toward him, pleading that he not be killed, hoping instead to adopt him — completely unaware of who he truly was or what he represented.

Meanwhile, his own mother endured something almost unbearable.

وَأَصْبَحَ فُؤَادُ أُمِّ مُوسَىٰ فَٰرِغًا ۖ إِن كَادَتْ لَتُبْدِى بِهِۦ لَوْلَآ أَن رَّبَطْنَا عَلَىٰ قَلْبِهَا لِتَكُونَ مِنَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ

"And the heart of Moses' mother became empty [of all else]. She was about to disclose [the matter concerning] him had We not bound fast her heart that she would be of the believers."

— Surah Al-Qasas 28:10

Her heart became consumed with anxiety for her son, so much that she nearly revealed the truth herself — had Allah not strengthened her heart specifically so that she would remain among the believers, trusting His promise even in her most vulnerable moment.

She took a careful, faithful step to stay close to her son.

وَقَالَتْ لِأُخْتِهِۦ قُصِّيهِ ۖ فَبَصُرَتْ بِهِۦ عَن جُنُبٍۢ وَهُمْ لَا يَشْعُرُونَ

"And she said to his sister, 'Follow him'; so she watched him from a distance while they perceived not."

— Surah Al-Qasas 28:11

She instructed his sister to follow him from a distance, watching over him without anyone noticing — a mother's love finding a way, even under impossible circumstances.

Then Allah's promise began to unfold in a remarkable way.

۞ وَحَرَّمْنَا عَلَيْهِ ٱلْمَرَاضِعَ مِن قَبْلُ فَقَالَتْ هَلْ أَدُلُّكُمْ عَلَىٰٓ أَهْلِ بَيْتٍۢ يَكْفُلُونَهُۥ لَكُمْ وَهُمْ لَهُۥ نَٰصِحُونَ

"And We had prevented from him [all] wet nurses before, so she said, 'Shall I direct you to a household that will be responsible for him for you while they are to him [for his upbringing] sincere?'"

— Surah Al-Qasas 28:12

Allah had caused the infant to refuse every wet nurse offered to him. Seeing this, his sister suggested a household that could properly care for him — one that would be sincere in his upbringing.

And so, the impossible became reality.

فَرَدَدْنَٰهُ إِلَىٰٓ أُمِّهِۦ كَىْ تَقَرَّ عَيْنُهَا وَلَا تَحْزَنَ وَلِتَعْلَمَ أَنَّ وَعْدَ ٱللَّهِ حَقٌّۭ وَلَٰكِنَّ أَكْثَرَهُمْ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ

"So We restored him to his mother that she might be content and not grieve and that she would know that the promise of Allāh is true. But most of them [i.e., the people] do not know."

— Surah Al-Qasas 28:13

Musa (AS) was returned to his own mother — within Pharaoh's own household, no less — so that her heart could be at ease, free from grief, and so that she would know with certainty that Allah's promise is always true. Allah closes this verse with a quiet but powerful reminder: most people simply do not recognize this truth, even when it unfolds directly before them.

chapters.title: Fleeing to Midian
chapters.content:
As a grown man living in Egypt, Musa (AS) found himself caught in a moment that would change the course of his life.

وَدَخَلَ ٱلْمَدِينَةَ عَلَىٰ حِينِ غَفْلَةٍۢ مِّنْ أَهْلِهَا فَوَجَدَ فِيهَا رَجُلَيْنِ يَقْتَتِلَانِ هَٰذَا مِن شِيعَتِهِۦ وَهَٰذَا مِنْ عَدُوِّهِۦ ۖ فَٱسْتَغَٰثَهُ ٱلَّذِى مِن شِيعَتِهِۦ عَلَى ٱلَّذِى مِنْ عَدُوِّهِۦ فَوَكَزَهُۥ مُوسَىٰ فَقَضَىٰ عَلَيْهِ ۖ قَالَ هَٰذَا مِنْ عَمَلِ ٱلشَّيْطَٰنِ ۖ إِنَّهُۥ عَدُوٌّۭ مُّضِلٌّۭ مُّبِينٌۭ

"And he entered the city at a time of inattention by its people and found therein two men fighting: one from his faction and one from among his enemy. And the one from his faction called for help to him against the one from his enemy, so Moses struck him and [unintentionally] killed him. [Moses] said, 'This is from the work of Satan. Indeed, he is a manifest, misleading enemy.'"

— Surah Al-Qasas 28:15

He entered the city while its people were inattentive and came upon two men fighting — one from his own people, one from his enemies. The man from his own faction called for his help, and Musa (AS) struck the other man, accidentally killing him. Immediately, he recognized this as the work of Satan, acknowledging the seriousness of what had happened rather than excusing it.

His response was immediate, sincere repentance.

قَالَ رَبِّ إِنِّى ظَلَمْتُ نَفْسِى فَٱغْفِرْ لِى فَغَفَرَ لَهُۥٓ ۚ إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ ٱلْغَفُورُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ

"He said, 'My Lord, indeed I have wronged myself, so forgive me,' and He forgave him. Indeed, He is the Forgiving, the Merciful."

— Surah Al-Qasas 28:16

He turned directly to Allah, admitting he had wronged himself, and asked for forgiveness — and Allah forgave him at once, for He is the Forgiving, the Merciful. This moment teaches something vital: even an unintentional wrong calls for sincere return to Allah, and Allah's mercy meets that sincerity immediately.

The next day, fear and uncertainty filled him.

فَأَصْبَحَ فِى ٱلْمَدِينَةِ خَآئِفًۭا يَتَرَقَّبُ فَإِذَا ٱلَّذِى ٱسْتَنصَرَهُۥ بِٱلْأَمْسِ يَسْتَصْرِخُهُۥ ۚ قَالَ لَهُۥ مُوسَىٰٓ إِنَّكَ لَغَوِىٌّۭ مُّبِينٌۭ

"And he became inside the city fearful and anticipating [exposure], when suddenly the one who sought his help the previous day cried out to him [once again]. Moses said to him, 'Indeed, you are an evident, [persistent] deviator.'"

— Surah Al-Qasas 28:18

He moved through the city anxiously, watching for any sign of exposure, when the very man he had helped the day before called out to him again for assistance. Musa (AS), now wary, called him an evident troublemaker.

As he moved to intervene again, the truth of his situation became dangerously clear.

فَلَمَّآ أَنْ أَرَادَ أَن يَبْطِشَ بِٱلَّذِى هُوَ عَدُوٌّۭ لَّهُمَا قَالَ يَٰمُوسَىٰٓ أَتُرِيدُ أَن تَقْتُلَنِى كَمَا قَتَلْتَ نَفْسًۢا بِٱلْأَمْسِ ۖ إِن تُرِيدُ إِلَّآ أَن تَكُونَ جَبَّارًۭا فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ وَمَا تُرِيدُ أَن تَكُونَ مِنَ ٱلْمُصْلِحِينَ

"And when he wanted to strike the one who was an enemy to both of them, he said, 'O Moses, do you intend to kill me as you killed someone yesterday? You only want to be a tyrant in the land and do not want to be of the amenders.'"

— Surah Al-Qasas 28:19

The man he was about to confront turned the situation against him, accusing Musa (AS) of wanting to kill him just as he had killed someone the day before — revealing that word of the incident had already spread, and accusing him of seeking tyranny rather than reform.

Word of what happened reached those in power, and a warning came just in time.

وَجَآءَ رَجُلٌۭ مِّنْ أَقْصَا ٱلْمَدِينَةِ يَسْعَىٰ قَالَ يَٰمُوسَىٰٓ إِنَّ ٱلْمَلَأَ يَأْتَمِرُونَ بِكَ لِيَقْتُلُوكَ فَٱخْرُجْ إِنِّى لَكَ مِنَ ٱلنَّٰصِحِينَ

"And a man came from the farthest end of the city, running. He said, 'O Moses, indeed the eminent ones are conferring over you [intending] to kill you, so leave [the city]; indeed, I am to you of the sincere advisors.'"

— Surah Al-Qasas 28:20

A man ran from the far end of the city specifically to warn him — the city's leaders were plotting to kill him, and he urged Musa (AS) to leave immediately, offering this warning out of sincere concern.

Musa (AS) had no choice but to flee everything he knew.

فَخَرَجَ مِنْهَا خَآئِفًۭا يَتَرَقَّبُ ۖ قَالَ رَبِّ نَجِّنِى مِنَ ٱلْقَوْمِ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ

"So he left it, fearful and anticipating [apprehension]. He said, 'My Lord, save me from the wrongdoing people.'"

— Surah Al-Qasas 28:21

He left the city in fear, watching for danger at every turn, turning to Allah with a simple, urgent plea — to be saved from the wrongdoing people who sought to harm him.

With no clear destination, he placed his trust entirely in Allah's guidance.

وَلَمَّا تَوَجَّهَ تِلْقَآءَ مَدْيَنَ قَالَ عَسَىٰ رَبِّىٓ أَن يَهْدِيَنِى سَوَآءَ ٱلسَّبِيلِ

"And when he directed himself toward Madyan, he said, 'Perhaps my Lord will guide me to the sound way.'"

— Surah Al-Qasas 28:22

As he turned toward Madyan, he expressed hope rather than certainty — that perhaps his Lord would guide him to the right way. This wasn't a confident plan; it was complete reliance on Allah amid total uncertainty.

Arriving exhausted and alone in an unfamiliar land, Musa (AS) still found a way to be of service.

فَسَقَىٰ لَهُمَا ثُمَّ تَوَلَّىٰٓ إِلَى ٱلظِّلِّ فَقَالَ رَبِّ إِنِّى لِمَآ أَنزَلْتَ إِلَىَّ مِنْ خَيْرٍۢ فَقِيرٌۭ

"So he watered [their flocks] for them; then he went back to the shade and said, 'My Lord, indeed I am, for whatever good You would send down to me, in need.'"

— Surah Al-Qasas 28:24

He helped water the flocks of two women he encountered, then withdrew to the shade and made one of the most quietly profound duas in the Quran — acknowledging his complete need for whatever good Allah would send his way. Alone, exiled, and without resources, Musa (AS) modeled total dependence on Allah, a lesson for anyone who finds themselves stripped of everything familiar.

chapters.title: The Burning Bush — Calling to Prophethood
chapters.content:
Allah introduces this profound moment with a direct question.

وَهَلْ أَتَىٰكَ حَدِيثُ مُوسَىٰٓ

"And has the story of Moses reached you? -"

— Surah Ta-Ha 20:9

Years after fleeing Egypt, traveling with his family, Musa (AS) noticed something unusual in the distance.

إِذْ رَءَا نَارًۭا فَقَالَ لِأَهْلِهِ ٱمْكُثُوٓا۟ إِنِّىٓ ءَانَسْتُ نَارًۭا لَّعَلِّىٓ ءَاتِيكُم مِّنْهَا بِقَبَسٍ أَوْ أَجِدُ عَلَى ٱلنَّارِ هُدًۭى

"When he saw a fire and said to his family, 'Stay here; indeed, I have perceived a fire; perhaps I can bring you a torch or find at the fire some guidance.'"

— Surah Ta-Ha 20:10

He saw a fire and told his family to wait, hoping to bring back a torch for warmth, or perhaps find guidance from whoever was there. He had no idea this fire would change everything.

As he approached, he was called by name.

فَلَمَّآ أَتَىٰهَا نُودِىَ يَٰمُوسَىٰٓ

"And when he came to it, he was called, 'O Moses,'"

— Surah Ta-Ha 20:11

Allah then spoke directly to him.

إِنِّىٓ أَنَا۠ رَبُّكَ فَٱخْلَعْ نَعْلَيْكَ ۖ إِنَّكَ بِٱلْوَادِ ٱلْمُقَدَّسِ طُوًۭى

"Indeed, I am your Lord, so remove your sandals. Indeed, you are in the blessed valley of Ṭuwā."

— Surah Ta-Ha 20:12

Allah addressed him directly — identifying Himself as his Lord, instructing him to remove his sandals, for he stood in a blessed, sacred valley.

وَأَنَا ٱخْتَرْتُكَ فَٱسْتَمِعْ لِمَا يُوحَىٰٓ

"And I have chosen you, so listen to what is revealed [to you]."

— Surah Ta-Ha 20:13

Allah told him plainly: he had been chosen, and was now to listen carefully to what would be revealed to him.

إِنَّنِىٓ أَنَا ٱللَّهُ لَآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّآ أَنَا۠ فَٱعْبُدْنِى وَأَقِمِ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ لِذِكْرِىٓ

"Indeed, I am Allāh. There is no deity except Me, so worship Me and establish prayer for My remembrance."

— Surah Ta-Ha 20:14

The very foundation of his mission was declared immediately — there is no god but Allah, so he was to worship Him alone and establish prayer in His remembrance. This is the core message every prophet was sent to deliver, stated here with complete clarity.

Then Allah turned his attention to something ordinary in his hand.

وَمَا تِلْكَ بِيَمِينِكَ يَٰمُوسَىٰ

"And what is that in your right hand, O Moses?'"

— Surah Ta-Ha 20:17

Musa (AS) answered simply.

قَالَ هِىَ عَصَاىَ أَتَوَكَّؤُا۟ عَلَيْهَا وَأَهُشُّ بِهَا عَلَىٰ غَنَمِى وَلِىَ فِيهَا مَـَٔارِبُ أُخْرَىٰ

"He said, 'It is my staff; I lean upon it, and I bring down leaves for my sheep and I have therein other uses.'"

— Surah Ta-Ha 20:18

Musa (AS) explained simply — it was his staff, something he leaned on and used for his sheep, among other practical uses. An everyday object, nothing more.

قَالَ أَلْقِهَا يَٰمُوسَىٰ

"[Allāh] said, 'Throw it down, O Moses.'"

— Surah Ta-Ha 20:19

Allah instructed him to throw it down.

فَأَلْقَىٰهَا فَإِذَا هِىَ حَيَّةٌۭ تَسْعَىٰ

"So he threw it down, and thereupon it was a snake, moving swiftly."

— Surah Ta-Ha 20:20

The moment he did, the staff transformed into a swiftly moving snake — a clear sign of Allah's power over creation, given directly to Musa (AS) as preparation for what awaited him.

قَالَ خُذْهَا وَلَا تَخَفْ ۖ سَنُعِيدُهَا سِيرَتَهَا ٱلْأُولَىٰ

"[Allāh] said, 'Seize it and fear not; We will return it to its former condition.'"

— Surah Ta-Ha 20:21

Allah reassured him immediately — to seize it without fear, promising it would return to its original form. This pattern — showing a sign, then offering reassurance — reflects Allah's mercy even in moments meant to test and prepare His prophets.

Aware of the weight of the mission now placed on him, Musa (AS) made a heartfelt request.

قَالَ رَبِّ ٱشْرَحْ لِى صَدْرِى

"[Moses] said, 'My Lord, expand [i.e., relax] for me my breast [with assurance]'"

— Surah Ta-Ha 20:25

He continued his heartfelt request.

وَيَسِّرْ لِىٓ أَمْرِى

"And ease for me my task"

— Surah Ta-Ha 20:26

He asked further.

وَٱحْلُلْ عُقْدَةًۭ مِّن لِّسَانِى

"And untie the knot from my tongue"

— Surah Ta-Ha 20:27

So that his message would be understood clearly.

يَفْقَهُوا۟ قَوْلِى

"That they may understand my speech."

— Surah Ta-Ha 20:28

He asked Allah to expand his chest with assurance, to ease his task, and to remove the difficulty from his speech — so that the people he was sent to could understand him clearly. Musa (AS) didn't pretend to feel ready or confident. He was honest about his limitations and asked Allah directly for help in overcoming them — a model for every believer facing a task that feels too great for them alone.

chapters.title: Confronting Pharaoh
chapters.content:
After his calling at the burning bush, Musa (AS) was given a direct mission, alongside his brother Harun (AS).

ٱذْهَبَآ إِلَىٰ فِرْعَوْنَ إِنَّهُۥ طَغَىٰ

"Go, both of you, to Pharaoh. Indeed, he has transgressed."

— Surah Ta-Ha 20:43

Allah sent them both to Pharaoh, who had transgressed far beyond reasonable limits.

فَقُولَا لَهُۥ قَوْلًۭا لَّيِّنًۭا لَّعَلَّهُۥ يَتَذَكَّرُ أَوْ يَخْشَىٰ

"And speak to him with gentle speech that perhaps he may be reminded or fear [Allāh].'"

— Surah Ta-Ha 20:44

Remarkably, Allah instructed them to speak to him gently — not out of weakness, but in the hope that he might be reminded or come to fear Allah. Even toward the most tyrannical of rulers, the approach commanded was patience and softness, not immediate harshness.
