فَأْتِيَاهُ فَقُولَآ إِنَّا رَسُولَا رَبِّكَ فَأَرْسِلْ مَعَنَا بَنِىٓ إِسْرَٰٓءِيلَ وَلَا تُعَذِّبْهُمْ ۖ قَدْ جِئْنَٰكَ بِـَٔايَةٍۢ مِّن رَّبِّكَ ۖ وَٱلسَّلَٰمُ عَلَىٰ مَنِ ٱتَّبَعَ ٱلْهُدَىٰٓ

"So go to him and say, 'Indeed, we are messengers of your Lord, so send with us the Children of Israel and do not torment them. We have come to you with a sign from your Lord. And peace will be upon he who follows the guidance.'"

— Surah Ta-Ha 20:47

Their message was clear and direct: they were messengers of his Lord, sent to ask that the Children of Israel be released from his torment, bringing with them a sign as proof.

Pharaoh, unfamiliar with the concept entirely, asked a basic but telling question.

قَالَ فَمَن رَّبُّكُمَا يَٰمُوسَىٰ

"[Pharaoh] said, 'So who is the Lord of you two, O Moses?'"

— Surah Ta-Ha 20:49

He asked who exactly this "Lord" was that they spoke of.

قَالَ رَبُّنَا ٱلَّذِىٓ أَعْطَىٰ كُلَّ شَىْءٍ خَلْقَهُۥ ثُمَّ هَدَىٰ

"He said, 'Our Lord is He who gave each thing its form and then guided [it].'"

— Surah Ta-Ha 20:50

Musa (AS) answered with simple, profound clarity — their Lord is the One who gave every single thing its form, then guided it. A description rooted in observable creation, not abstract claims.

Rather than reflecting on this, Pharaoh turned to personal attacks.

قَالَ أَلَمْ نُرَبِّكَ فِينَا وَلِيدًۭا وَلَبِثْتَ فِينَا مِنْ عُمُرِكَ سِنِينَ

"[Pharaoh] said, 'Did we not raise you among us as a child, and you remained among us for years of your life?'"

— Surah Ash-Shu'ara 26:18

He reminded Musa (AS) that he had been raised in his own household, spending years of his life among them.

وَفَعَلْتَ فَعْلَتَكَ ٱلَّتِى فَعَلْتَ وَأَنتَ مِنَ ٱلْكَٰفِرِينَ

"And [then] you did your deed which you did, and you were of the ungrateful.'"

— Surah Ash-Shu'ara 26:19

He brought up the past incident, framing Musa (AS) as ungrateful for what had been done for him.

Musa (AS) responded by exposing the deeper injustice Pharaoh himself was guilty of.

وَتِلْكَ نِعْمَةٌۭ تَمُنُّهَا عَلَىَّ أَنْ عَبَّدتَّ بَنِىٓ إِسْرَٰٓءِيلَ

"And is this a favor of which you remind me - that you have enslaved the Children of Israel?'"

— Surah Ash-Shu'ara 26:22

He turned the accusation back — was raising him in the palace really something to be thanked for, when Pharaoh had simultaneously enslaved the entire Children of Israel?

Demanding proof, Pharaoh issued a challenge.

قَالَ إِن كُنتَ جِئْتَ بِـَٔايَةٍۢ فَأْتِ بِهَآ إِن كُنتَ مِنَ ٱلصَّٰدِقِينَ

"[Pharaoh] said, 'If you have come with a sign, then bring it forth, if you should be of the truthful.'"

— Surah Al-A'raf 7:106

He told Musa (AS) to bring forth a sign, if he was truly being truthful.

فَأَلْقَىٰ عَصَاهُ فَإِذَا هِىَ ثُعْبَانٌۭ مُّبِينٌۭ

"So he [i.e., Moses] threw his staff, and suddenly it was a serpent, manifest."

— Surah Al-A'raf 7:107

Musa (AS) threw down his staff, and it became a clear, visible serpent.

وَنَزَعَ يَدَهُۥ فَإِذَا هِىَ بَيْضَآءُ لِلنَّٰظِرِينَ

"And he drew out his hand; thereupon it was white [with radiance] for the observers."

— Surah Al-A'raf 7:108

He then drew out his hand, and it shone white with radiance for all who watched.

Pharaoh's own advisors recognized the skill involved, but dismissed it as mere trickery.

قَالَ ٱلْمَلَأُ مِن قَوْمِ فِرْعَوْنَ إِنَّ هَٰذَا لَسَٰحِرٌ عَلِيمٌۭ

"Said the eminent among the people of Pharaoh, 'Indeed, this is a learned magician'"

— Surah Al-A'raf 7:109

They claimed this was simply the work of a learned magician.

قَالُوٓا۟ أَرْجِهْ وَأَخَاهُ وَأَرْسِلْ فِى ٱلْمَدَآئِنِ حَٰشِرِينَ

"They said, 'Postpone [the matter of] him and his brother and send among the cities gatherers'"

— Surah Al-A'raf 7:111

They explained exactly who these gatherers should bring.

يَأْتُوكَ بِكُلِّ سَٰحِرٍ عَلِيمٍۢ

"Who will bring you every learned magician.'"

— Surah Al-A'raf 7:112

They suggested delaying judgment and instead gathering every skilled magician from across the cities to challenge him properly.

وَجَآءَ ٱلسَّحَرَةُ فِرْعَوْنَ قَالُوٓا۟ إِنَّ لَنَا لَأَجْرًا إِن كُنَّا نَحْنُ ٱلْغَٰلِبِينَ

"And the magicians came to Pharaoh. They said, 'Indeed for us is a reward if we are the predominant.'"

— Surah Al-A'raf 7:113

The magicians arrived, openly asking what reward awaited them if they proved victorious — revealing their true motivation from the very start.

قَالُوا۟ يَٰمُوسَىٰٓ إِمَّآ أَن تُلْقِىَ وَإِمَّآ أَن نَّكُونَ نَحْنُ ٱلْمُلْقِينَ

"They said, 'O Moses, either you throw [your staff], or we will be the ones to throw [first].'"

— Surah Al-A'raf 7:115

They gave Musa (AS) the choice — would he throw first, or would they?

قَالَ أَلْقُوا۟ ۖ فَلَمَّآ أَلْقَوْا۟ سَحَرُوٓا۟ أَعْيُنَ ٱلنَّاسِ وَٱسْتَرْهَبُوهُمْ وَجَآءُو بِسِحْرٍ عَظِيمٍۢ

"He said, 'Throw,' and when they threw, they bewitched the eyes of the people and struck terror into them, and they presented a great [feat of] magic."

— Surah Al-A'raf 7:116

He told them to throw first. When they did, they bewitched the eyes of everyone watching, striking genuine terror into the crowd with what appeared to be powerful magic.

But what followed dismantled their illusion completely.

۞ وَأَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَىٰ مُوسَىٰٓ أَنْ أَلْقِ عَصَاكَ ۖ فَإِذَا هِىَ تَلْقَفُ مَا يَأْفِكُونَ

"And We inspired to Moses, 'Throw your staff,' and at once it devoured what they were falsifying."

— Surah Al-A'raf 7:117

Allah inspired Musa (AS) to throw his own staff — and instantly, it swallowed up everything they had falsely presented.

فَوَقَعَ ٱلْحَقُّ وَبَطَلَ مَا كَانُوا۟ يَعْمَلُونَ

"So the truth was established, and abolished was what they were doing."

— Surah Al-A'raf 7:118

In that single moment, truth was firmly established, and every illusion they had created was undone entirely.

فَغُلِبُوا۟ هُنَالِكَ وَٱنقَلَبُوا۟ صَٰغِرِينَ

"And they [i.e., Pharaoh and his people] were overcome right there and became debased."

— Surah Al-A'raf 7:119

Pharaoh and his people were overcome right there, utterly humiliated before everyone watching.

And then came one of the most remarkable turns in the entire story.

وَأُلْقِىَ ٱلسَّحَرَةُ سَٰجِدِينَ

"And the magicians fell down in prostration [to Allāh]."

— Surah Al-A'raf 7:120

The very magicians who had been brought specifically to defeat Musa (AS) fell down in prostration.

قَالُوٓا۟ ءَامَنَّا بِرَبِّ ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ

"They said, 'We have believed in the Lord of the worlds,'"

— Surah Al-A'raf 7:121

They specified exactly whose Lord they meant.

رَبِّ مُوسَىٰ وَهَٰرُونَ

"The Lord of Moses and Aaron.'"

— Surah Al-A'raf 7:122

They declared their belief in the Lord of all the worlds — the Lord of Musa and Harun. These men, recruited for the sole purpose of opposing Allah's messenger, recognized truth the instant they witnessed it clearly, and submitted immediately, regardless of the consequences that would follow from defying Pharaoh himself.

chapters.title: The Plagues and Pharaoh's Hardened Heart
chapters.content:
Despite witnessing the magicians' defeat and their immediate submission to Allah, Pharaoh and his people remained unmoved. Allah began sending direct trials upon them.

وَلَقَدْ أَخَذْنَآ ءَالَ فِرْعَوْنَ بِٱلسِّنِينَ وَنَقْصٍۢ مِّنَ ٱلثَّمَرَٰتِ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَذَّكَّرُونَ

"And We certainly seized the people of Pharaoh with years of famine and a deficiency in fruits that perhaps they would be reminded."

— Surah Al-A'raf 7:130

Allah seized them with years of famine and a noticeable decline in produce, hoping this hardship would cause them to be reminded and turn back to Him.

But rather than reflecting, their response revealed deep spiritual blindness.

فَإِذَا جَآءَتْهُمُ ٱلْحَسَنَةُ قَالُوا۟ لَنَا هَٰذِهِۦ ۖ وَإِن تُصِبْهُمْ سَيِّئَةٌۭ يَطَّيَّرُوا۟ بِمُوسَىٰ وَمَن مَّعَهُۥٓ ۗ أَلَآ إِنَّمَا طَٰٓئِرُهُمْ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ وَلَٰكِنَّ أَكْثَرَهُمْ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ

"But when good [i.e., provision] came to them, they said, 'This is ours [by right].' And if a bad [condition] struck them, they saw an evil omen in Moses and those with him. Unquestionably, their fortune is with Allāh, but most of them do not know."

— Surah Al-A'raf 7:131

Whenever good came to them, they claimed it as something they deserved by right. Yet whenever hardship struck, they blamed Musa (AS) and those with him, seeing them as a bad omen — completely missing that their circumstances were entirely in Allah's hands, not caused by Musa's presence.

Even after everything they had witnessed, they remained defiant.

وَقَالُوا۟ مَهْمَا تَأْتِنَا بِهِۦ مِنْ ءَايَةٍۢ لِّتَسْحَرَنَا بِهَا فَمَا نَحْنُ لَكَ بِمُؤْمِنِينَ

"And they said, 'No matter what sign you bring us with which to bewitch us, we will not be believers in you.'"

— Surah Al-A'raf 7:132

They declared outright that no matter what sign was shown to them, they would never believe — revealing that their rejection wasn't about lack of evidence, but a hardened refusal to accept truth regardless of what proof appeared.

Allah then sent a series of distinct, unmistakable signs.

فَأَرْسَلْنَا عَلَيْهِمُ ٱلطُّوفَانَ وَٱلْجَرَادَ وَٱلْقُمَّلَ وَٱلضَّفَادِعَ وَٱلدَّمَ ءَايَٰتٍۢ مُّفَصَّلَٰتٍۢ فَٱسْتَكْبَرُوا۟ وَكَانُوا۟ قَوْمًۭا مُّجْرِمِينَ

"So We sent upon them the flood and locusts and lice and frogs and blood as distinct signs, but they were arrogant and were a criminal people."

— Surah Al-A'raf 7:133

Flooding, locusts, lice, frogs, and blood — each one a clear, separate trial. Yet their arrogance only deepened, and they continued in their criminal ways despite every warning.

Each time the punishment intensified, a familiar pattern emerged.

وَلَمَّا وَقَعَ عَلَيْهِمُ ٱلرِّجْزُ قَالُوا۟ يَٰمُوسَى ٱدْعُ لَنَا رَبَّكَ بِمَا عَهِدَ عِندَكَ ۖ لَئِن كَشَفْتَ عَنَّا ٱلرِّجْزَ لَنُؤْمِنَنَّ لَكَ وَلَنُرْسِلَنَّ مَعَكَ بَنِىٓ إِسْرَٰٓءِيلَ

"And when the punishment descended upon them, they said, 'O Moses, invoke for us your Lord by what He has promised you. If you [can] remove the punishment from us, we will surely believe you, and we will send with you the Children of Israel.'"

— Surah Al-A'raf 7:134

They would beg Musa (AS) to call upon his Lord to remove the affliction, promising that if he did, they would finally believe and release the Children of Israel.

But this promise proved hollow every single time.

فَلَمَّا كَشَفْنَا عَنْهُمُ ٱلرِّجْزَ إِلَىٰٓ أَجَلٍ هُم بَٰلِغُوهُ إِذَا هُمْ يَنكُثُونَ

"But when We removed the punishment from them until a term which they were to reach, then at once they broke their word."

— Surah Al-A'raf 7:135

Whenever Allah lifted the punishment, giving them a set period of relief, they would break their word almost immediately — the exact same cycle repeating itself again and again.

This pattern of broken promises eventually reached its end.

فَٱنتَقَمْنَا مِنْهُمْ فَأَغْرَقْنَٰهُمْ فِى ٱلْيَمِّ بِأَنَّهُمْ كَذَّبُوا۟ بِـَٔايَٰتِنَا وَكَانُوا۟ عَنْهَا غَٰفِلِينَ

"So We took retribution from them, and We drowned them in the sea because they denied Our signs and were heedless of them."

— Surah Al-A'raf 7:136

Allah's retribution finally came in full — they were drowned in the sea, a direct consequence of their persistent denial of Allah's signs and their complete heedlessness toward them. This chapter stands as a sobering reminder: signs and trials are opportunities for reflection, but only for hearts genuinely willing to be moved by them.

chapters.title: The Exodus and Parting of the Sea
chapters.content:
After enduring years of oppression, the moment finally came for Musa (AS) and his people to leave Egypt entirely.

۞ وَأَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَىٰ مُوسَىٰٓ أَنْ أَسْرِ بِعِبَادِىٓ إِنَّكُم مُّتَّبَعُونَ

"And We inspired to Moses, 'Travel by night with My servants; indeed, you will be pursued.'"

— Surah Ash-Shu'ara 26:52

Allah inspired Musa (AS) to travel by night with His servants, warning him directly that they would be pursued. This was no secret escape — Allah told him plainly to expect chase.

True to that warning, Pharaoh moved quickly.

فَأَرْسَلَ فِرْعَوْنُ فِى ٱلْمَدَآئِنِ حَٰشِرِينَ

"Then Pharaoh sent among the cities gatherers"

— Surah Ash-Shu'ara 26:53

He sent gatherers throughout the cities, rallying his forces to pursue them.

فَأَتْبَعُوهُم مُّشْرِقِينَ

"So they pursued them at sunrise."

— Surah Ash-Shu'ara 26:60

They caught up with them at sunrise — a massive force in pursuit of a fleeing people with nowhere left to run.

The moment the two groups saw each other, fear gripped Musa's companions.

فَلَمَّا تَرَٰٓءَا ٱلْجَمْعَانِ قَالَ أَصْحَٰبُ مُوسَىٰٓ إِنَّا لَمُدْرَكُونَ

"And when the two companies saw one another, the companions of Moses said, 'Indeed, we are to be overtaken!'"

— Surah Ash-Shu'ara 26:61

They cried out that they were certainly about to be overtaken — trapped between Pharaoh's army behind them and the sea ahead.

Musa's response, in this moment of apparent hopelessness, reflects the depth of his trust in Allah.

قَالَ كَلَّآ ۖ إِنَّ مَعِىَ رَبِّى سَيَهْدِينِ

"[Moses] said, 'No! Indeed, with me is my Lord; He will guide me.'"

— Surah Ash-Shu'ara 26:62

He told them firmly — no, they would not be overtaken, because his Lord was with him, and would guide him through it. Not certainty in a plan, not confidence in human strategy — but absolute trust in Allah's presence and guidance.

What happened next remains one of the most extraordinary miracles ever recorded.

فَأَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَىٰ مُوسَىٰٓ أَنِ ٱضْرِب بِّعَصَاكَ ٱلْبَحْرَ ۖ فَٱنفَلَقَ فَكَانَ كُلُّ فِرْقٍۢ كَٱلطَّوْدِ ٱلْعَظِيمِ

"Then We inspired to Moses, 'Strike with your staff the sea,' and it parted, and each portion was like a great towering mountain."

— Surah Ash-Shu'ara 26:63

Allah inspired him to strike the sea with his staff — and it split apart, each section standing like an enormous mountain. An impossible escape route appeared exactly where there had been none.

وَأَزْلَفْنَا ثَمَّ ٱلْءَاخَرِينَ

"And We advanced thereto the others [i.e., the pursuers]."

— Surah Ash-Shu'ara 26:64

Pharaoh and his pursuers were drawn directly into that same path, following close behind.

وَأَنجَيْنَا مُوسَىٰ وَمَن مَّعَهُۥٓ أَجْمَعِينَ

"And We saved Moses and those with him, all together."

— Surah Ash-Shu'ara 26:65

Musa (AS) and every single person with him were saved completely — not one left behind.

ثُمَّ أَغْرَقْنَا ٱلْءَاخَرِينَ

"Then We drowned the others."

— Surah Ash-Shu'ara 26:66

And then the others — Pharaoh and his forces — were drowned entirely. The very sea that had parted to save the believers became the means of destruction for those who had oppressed them. This moment stands as one of the clearest demonstrations in the Quran that no situation is ever truly hopeless when Allah's help arrives — even when every human possibility appears exhausted.

chapters.title: Mount Sinai and the Torah
chapters.content:
After the exodus, Allah called Musa (AS) for an appointment of immense significance.

وَإِذْ وَٰعَدْنَا مُوسَىٰٓ أَرْبَعِينَ لَيْلَةًۭ ثُمَّ ٱتَّخَذْتُمُ ٱلْعِجْلَ مِنۢ بَعْدِهِۦ وَأَنتُمْ ظَٰلِمُونَ

"And [recall] when We made an appointment with Moses for forty nights. Then you took [for worship] the calf after him [i.e., his departure], while you were wrongdoers."

— Surah Al-Baqarah 2:51

Allah set an appointment with him for forty nights. Yet in his absence, his people turned to worshipping a calf instead — a profound act of wrongdoing committed almost immediately after their miraculous rescue.

This forty-night period unfolded with specific structure.

۞ وَوَٰعَدْنَا مُوسَىٰ ثَلَٰثِينَ لَيْلَةًۭ وَأَتْمَمْنَٰهَا بِعَشْرٍۢ فَتَمَّ مِيقَٰتُ رَبِّهِۦٓ أَرْبَعِينَ لَيْلَةًۭ ۚ وَقَالَ مُوسَىٰ لِأَخِيهِ هَٰرُونَ ٱخْلُفْنِى فِى قَوْمِى وَأَصْلِحْ وَلَا تَتَّبِعْ سَبِيلَ ٱلْمُفْسِدِينَ

"And We made an appointment with Moses for thirty nights and perfected them by [the addition of] ten; so the term of his Lord was completed as forty nights. And Moses said to his brother Aaron, 'Take my place among my people, do right [by them], and do not follow the way of the corrupters.'"

— Surah Al-A'raf 7:142

Allah appointed thirty nights, then completed it with ten more, totaling forty. Before leaving, Musa (AS) entrusted leadership of his people to his brother Harun (AS), instructing him to act rightly and avoid the path of corruption.

When Musa (AS) reached the appointed place, something extraordinary happened.

وَلَمَّا جَآءَ مُوسَىٰ لِمِيقَٰتِنَا وَكَلَّمَهُۥ رَبُّهُۥ قَالَ رَبِّ أَرِنِىٓ أَنظُرْ إِلَيْكَ ۚ قَالَ لَن تَرَىٰنِى وَلَٰكِنِ ٱنظُرْ إِلَى ٱلْجَبَلِ فَإِنِ ٱسْتَقَرَّ مَكَانَهُۥ فَسَوْفَ تَرَىٰنِى ۚ فَلَمَّا تَجَلَّىٰ رَبُّهُۥ لِلْجَبَلِ جَعَلَهُۥ دَكًّۭا وَخَرَّ مُوسَىٰ صَعِقًۭا ۚ فَلَمَّآ أَفَاقَ قَالَ سُبْحَٰنَكَ تُبْتُ إِلَيْكَ وَأَنَا۠ أَوَّلُ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ

"And when Moses arrived at Our appointed time and his Lord spoke to him, he said, 'My Lord, show me [Yourself] that I may look at You.' [Allāh] said, 'You will not see Me, but look at the mountain; if it should remain in place, then you will see Me.' But when his Lord appeared to the mountain, He rendered it level, and Moses fell unconscious. And when he awoke, he said, 'Exalted are You! I have repented to You, and I am the first [among my people] of the believers.'"

— Surah Al-A'raf 7:143

His Lord spoke to him directly, and in that intimacy, Musa (AS) made a bold request — to see Allah Himself. Allah responded that he could not see Him, but to instead watch the mountain — if it remained steady, he would see Him. When Allah's manifestation touched the mountain, it crumbled entirely, and Musa (AS) fell unconscious from the overwhelming experience. Upon waking, he immediately glorified Allah, repented, and declared himself first among the believers. This moment reveals both the limits of human capacity before Allah's majesty, and Musa's complete humility in response to it.

Meanwhile, back among his people, something deeply troubling had occurred.

وَٱتَّخَذَ قَوْمُ مُوسَىٰ مِنۢ بَعْدِهِۦ مِنْ حُلِيِّهِمْ عِجْلًۭا جَسَدًۭا لَّهُۥ خُوَارٌ ۚ أَلَمْ يَرَوْا۟ أَنَّهُۥ لَا يُكَلِّمُهُمْ وَلَا يَهْدِيهِمْ سَبِيلًا ۘ ٱتَّخَذُوهُ وَكَانُوا۟ ظَٰلِمِينَ

"And the people of Moses made, after [his departure], from their ornaments a calf - an image having a lowing sound. Did they not see that it could neither speak to them nor guide them to a way? They took it [for worship], and they were wrongdoers."

— Surah Al-A'raf 7:148

In his absence, his people fashioned a calf from their own ornaments — an object that could neither speak to them nor guide them anywhere. Despite this obvious powerlessness, they took to worshipping it, becoming wrongdoers in the process.

Eventually, regret set in.

وَلَمَّا سُقِطَ فِىٓ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَرَأَوْا۟ أَنَّهُمْ قَدْ ضَلُّوا۟ قَالُوا۟ لَئِن لَّمْ يَرْحَمْنَا رَبُّنَا وَيَغْفِرْ لَنَا لَنَكُونَنَّ مِنَ ٱلْخَٰسِرِينَ

"And when regret overcame them and they saw that they had gone astray, they said, 'If our Lord does not have mercy upon us and forgive us, we will surely be among the losers.'"

— Surah Al-A'raf 7:149

Once they recognized how far astray they had gone, they acknowledged that without Allah's mercy and forgiveness, they would certainly be among the losers.

When Musa (AS) returned and witnessed what had happened, his reaction reflected the depth of his grief and anger.

وَلَمَّا رَجَعَ مُوسَىٰٓ إِلَىٰ قَوْمِهِۦ غَضْبَٰنَ أَسِفًۭا قَالَ بِئْسَمَا خَلَفْتُمُونِى مِنۢ بَعْدِىٓ ۖ أَعَجِلْتُمْ أَمْرَ رَبِّكُمْ ۖ وَأَلْقَى ٱلْأَلْوَاحَ وَأَخَذَ بِرَأْسِ أَخِيهِ يَجُرُّهُۥٓ إِلَيْهِ ۚ قَالَ ٱبْنَ أُمَّ إِنَّ ٱلْقَوْمَ ٱسْتَضْعَفُونِى وَكَادُوا۟ يَقْتُلُونَنِى فَلَا تُشْمِتْ بِىَ ٱلْأَعْدَآءَ وَلَا تَجْعَلْنِى مَعَ ٱلْقَوْمِ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ

"And when Moses returned to his people, angry and grieved, he said, 'How wretched is that by which you have replaced me after [my departure]. Were you impatient over the matter of your Lord?' And he threw down the tablets and seized his brother by [the hair of] his head, pulling him toward him. [Aaron] said, 'O son of my mother, indeed the people overpowered me and were about to kill me, so let not the enemies rejoice over me and do not place me among the wrongdoing people.'"

— Surah Al-A'raf 7:150

He confronted his people directly, questioning their impatience regarding their Lord's command, even throwing down the tablets in his distress. He then turned to his own brother, pulling him by the head — until Harun (AS) explained that the people had overpowered him and nearly killed him, pleading not to be grouped among the wrongdoers for something beyond his control.

Once the full picture became clear, Musa (AS) turned immediately to Allah.

قَالَ رَبِّ ٱغْفِرْ لِى وَلِأَخِى وَأَدْخِلْنَا فِى رَحْمَتِكَ ۖ وَأَنتَ أَرْحَمُ ٱلرَّٰحِمِينَ

"[Moses] said, 'My Lord, forgive me and my brother and admit us into Your mercy, for You are the most merciful of the merciful.'"

— Surah Al-A'raf 7:151

He asked forgiveness for both himself and his brother, seeking entry into Allah's mercy — acknowledging Allah as the most merciful of all who show mercy.

Allah then addressed the consequence awaiting those responsible.

إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱتَّخَذُوا۟ ٱلْعِجْلَ سَيَنَالُهُمْ غَضَبٌۭ مِّن رَّبِّهِمْ وَذِلَّةٌۭ فِى ٱلْحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا ۚ وَكَذَٰلِكَ نَجْزِى ٱلْمُفْتَرِينَ

"Indeed, those who took the calf [for worship] will obtain anger from their Lord and humiliation in the life of this world, and thus do We recompense the inventors [of falsehood]."

— Surah Al-A'raf 7:152

Those who had taken the calf for worship would face Allah's anger and humiliation in this worldly life — the natural consequence for those who invent falsehood against their own Creator.

But Allah immediately followed this with a door of hope.

وَٱلَّذِينَ عَمِلُوا۟ ٱلسَّيِّـَٔاتِ ثُمَّ تَابُوا۟ مِنۢ بَعْدِهَا وَءَامَنُوٓا۟ إِنَّ رَبَّكَ مِنۢ بَعْدِهَا لَغَفُورٌۭ رَّحِيمٌۭ

"But those who committed misdeeds and then repented after them and believed - indeed your Lord, thereafter, is Forgiving and Merciful."

— Surah Al-A'raf 7:153

For those who commit wrongdoing but then sincerely repent and believe afterward, Allah remains Forgiving and Merciful — mercy is always available to those who genuinely return.

As Musa's anger settled, he returned his attention to what mattered most.

وَلَمَّا سَكَتَ عَن مُّوسَى ٱلْغَضَبُ أَخَذَ ٱلْأَلْوَاحَ ۖ وَفِى نُسْخَتِهَا هُدًۭى وَرَحْمَةٌۭ لِّلَّذِينَ هُمْ لِرَبِّهِمْ يَرْهَبُونَ

"And when the anger subsided in Moses, he took up the tablets; and in their inscription was guidance and mercy for those who are fearful of their Lord."

— Surah Al-A'raf 7:154

He took up the tablets once more, recognizing that within their inscription was guidance and mercy specifically for those who hold reverence for their Lord.

In the aftermath, Musa (AS) selected representatives from his people for another appointment with Allah.

وَٱخْتَارَ مُوسَىٰ قَوْمَهُۥ سَبْعِينَ رَجُلًۭا لِّمِيقَٰتِنَا ۖ فَلَمَّآ أَخَذَتْهُمُ ٱلرَّجْفَةُ قَالَ رَبِّ لَوْ شِئْتَ أَهْلَكْتَهُم مِّن قَبْلُ وَإِيَّٰىَ ۖ أَتُهْلِكُنَا بِمَا فَعَلَ ٱلسُّفَهَآءُ مِنَّآ ۖ إِنْ هِىَ إِلَّا فِتْنَتُكَ تُضِلُّ بِهَا مَن تَشَآءُ وَتَهْدِى مَن تَشَآءُ ۖ أَنتَ وَلِيُّنَا فَٱغْفِرْ لَنَا وَٱرْحَمْنَا ۖ وَأَنتَ خَيْرُ ٱلْغَٰفِرِينَ

"And Moses chose from his people seventy men for Our appointment. And when the earthquake seized them, he said, 'My Lord, if You had willed, You could have destroyed them before and me [as well]. Would You destroy us for what the foolish among us have done? This is not but Your trial by which You send astray whom You will and guide whom You will. You are our Protector, so forgive us and have mercy upon us; and You are the best of forgivers.'"

— Surah Al-A'raf 7:155

When a powerful tremor seized these seventy chosen men, Musa (AS) pleaded on their behalf, acknowledging that this was Allah's trial — one through which He guides some and allows others to go astray, according to His will. He appealed to Allah as their Protector, asking for forgiveness and mercy, affirming that Allah is the best of those who forgive. This entire chapter reveals the weight of leadership, the depth of sincere repentance, and the boundless scope of Allah's mercy even after serious wrongdoing.

chapters.title: Trials in the Wilderness
chapters.content:
Even after the miraculous rescue from Pharaoh, the people's gratitude proved short-lived. Allah had provided for them generously in the wilderness.

وَظَلَّلْنَا عَلَيْكُمُ ٱلْغَمَامَ وَأَنزَلْنَا عَلَيْكُمُ ٱلْمَنَّ وَٱلسَّلْوَىٰ ۖ كُلُوا۟ مِن طَيِّبَٰتِ مَا رَزَقْنَٰكُمْ ۖ وَمَا ظَلَمُونَا وَلَٰكِن كَانُوٓا۟ أَنفُسَهُمْ يَظْلِمُونَ

"And We shaded you with clouds and sent down to you manna and quails, [saying], 'Eat from the good things with which We have provided you.' And they wronged Us not - but they were [only] wronging themselves."

— Surah Al-Baqarah 2:57

Allah shaded them with clouds and sent down manna and quails, inviting them to eat from the good provisions given to them. Allah notes that in their later ingratitude, they wronged no one but themselves.

That ingratitude soon surfaced directly.

وَإِذْ قُلْتُمْ يَٰمُوسَىٰ لَن نَّصْبِرَ عَلَىٰ طَعَامٍۢ وَٰحِدٍۢ فَٱدْعُ لَنَا رَبَّكَ يُخْرِجْ لَنَا مِمَّا تُنۢبِتُ ٱلْأَرْضُ مِنۢ بَقْلِهَا وَقِثَّآئِهَا وَفُومِهَا وَعَدَسِهَا وَبَصَلِهَا ۖ قَالَ أَتَسْتَبْدِلُونَ ٱلَّذِى هُوَ أَدْنَىٰ بِٱلَّذِى هُوَ خَيْرٌ ۚ ٱهْبِطُوا۟ مِصْرًۭا فَإِنَّ لَكُم مَّا سَأَلْتُمْ ۗ وَضُرِبَتْ عَلَيْهِمُ ٱلذِّلَّةُ وَٱلْمَسْكَنَةُ وَبَآءُو بِغَضَبٍۢ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ ۗ ذَٰلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمْ كَانُوا۟ يَكْفُرُونَ بِـَٔايَٰتِ ٱللَّهِ وَيَقْتُلُونَ ٱلنَّبِيِّۦنَ بِغَيْرِ ٱلْحَقِّ ۗ ذَٰلِكَ بِمَا عَصَوا۟ وَّكَانُوا۟ يَعْتَدُونَ

"And [recall] when you said, 'O Moses, we can never endure one [kind of] food. So call upon your Lord to bring forth for us from the earth its green herbs and its cucumbers and its garlic and its lentils and its onions.' [Moses] said, 'Would you exchange what is better for what is less? Go into [any] settlement and indeed, you will have what you have asked.' And they were covered with humiliation and poverty and returned with anger from Allāh [upon them]. That was because they [repeatedly] disbelieved in the signs of Allāh and killed the prophets without right. That was because they disobeyed and were [habitually] transgressing."

— Surah Al-Baqarah 2:61

They complained to Musa (AS), saying they could no longer endure eating the same food, demanding variety — vegetables, cucumbers, garlic, lentils, onions. Musa (AS) responded with a piercing question: would they really exchange what was better for what was lesser? Allah's response to their persistent disbelief and unwarranted demands was humiliation and poverty — consequences directly tied to their disbelief in Allah's signs, their killing of prophets without right, and their habitual transgression and disobedience.

A different kind of trial emerged from within their own community — the story of Qarun.

۞ إِنَّ قَٰرُونَ كَانَ مِن قَوْمِ مُوسَىٰ فَبَغَىٰ عَلَيْهِمْ ۖ وَءَاتَيْنَٰهُ مِنَ ٱلْكُنُوزِ مَآ إِنَّ مَفَاتِحَهُۥ لَتَنُوٓأُ بِٱلْعُصْبَةِ أُو۟لِى ٱلْقُوَّةِ إِذْ قَالَ لَهُۥ قَوْمُهُۥ لَا تَفْرَحْ ۖ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يُحِبُّ ٱلْفَرِحِينَ

"Indeed, Qārūn was from the people of Moses, but he tyrannized them. And We gave him of treasures whose keys would burden a band of strong men; thereupon his people said to him, 'Do not exult. Indeed, Allāh does not like the exultant.'"

— Surah Al-Qasas 28:76

Qarun was from Musa's own people, yet he became a tyrant among them. Allah had granted him such immense treasure that its very keys would burden a group of strong men to carry. His own people warned him directly not to exult in his wealth, reminding him that Allah does not love those consumed by arrogant joy.

They offered him sincere guidance.

وَٱبْتَغِ فِيمَآ ءَاتَىٰكَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلدَّارَ ٱلْءَاخِرَةَ ۖ وَلَا تَنسَ نَصِيبَكَ مِنَ ٱلدُّنْيَا ۖ وَأَحْسِن كَمَآ أَحْسَنَ ٱللَّهُ إِلَيْكَ ۖ وَلَا تَبْغِ ٱلْفَسَادَ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ ۖ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يُحِبُّ ٱلْمُفْسِدِينَ

"But seek, through that which Allāh has given you, the home of the Hereafter; and [yet], do not forget your share of the world. And do good as Allāh has done good to you. And desire not corruption in the land. Indeed, Allāh does not like corrupters.'"

— Surah Al-Qasas 28:77

They urged him to use what Allah had given him to seek the Hereafter, without neglecting his rightful share of this world — to do good just as Allah had been good to him, and to avoid seeking corruption in the land, since Allah does not love corrupters.

But Qarun's response revealed the depth of his self-deception.

قَالَ إِنَّمَآ أُوتِيتُهُۥ عَلَىٰ عِلْمٍ عِندِىٓ ۚ أَوَلَمْ يَعْلَمْ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ قَدْ أَهْلَكَ مِن قَبْلِهِۦ مِنَ ٱلْقُرُونِ مَنْ هُوَ أَشَدُّ مِنْهُ قُوَّةًۭ وَأَكْثَرُ جَمْعًۭا ۚ وَلَا يُسْـَٔلُ عَن ذُنُوبِهِمُ ٱلْمُجْرِمُونَ

"He said, 'I was only given it because of knowledge I have.' Did he not know that Allāh had destroyed before him of generations those who were greater than him in power and greater in accumulation [of wealth]? But the criminals, about their sins, will not be asked."

— Surah Al-Qasas 28:78

He claimed his wealth was solely due to his own knowledge — completely overlooking that Allah had destroyed entire generations before him who possessed even greater strength and wealth. Allah notes that criminals will not even be questioned about their sins in the way they imagine — their reckoning is far more serious than mere questioning.

His arrogance then became a public display.

فَخَرَجَ عَلَىٰ قَوْمِهِۦ فِى زِينَتِهِۦ ۖ قَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ يُرِيدُونَ ٱلْحَيَوٰةَ ٱلدُّنْيَا يَٰلَيْتَ لَنَا مِثْلَ مَآ أُوتِىَ قَٰرُونُ إِنَّهُۥ لَذُو حَظٍّ عَظِيمٍۢ

"So he came out before his people in his adornment. Those who desired the worldly life said, 'Oh, would that we had like what was given to Qārūn. Indeed, he is one of great fortune.'"

— Surah Al-Qasas 28:79

He paraded before his people in full adornment, and those who desired worldly life looked on with envy, wishing they had been given what Qarun possessed, believing him to be a man of tremendous fortune.

But this admiration would not last.

فَخَسَفْنَا بِهِۦ وَبِدَارِهِ ٱلْأَرْضَ فَمَا كَانَ لَهُۥ مِن فِئَةٍۢ يَنصُرُونَهُۥ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ وَمَا كَانَ مِنَ ٱلْمُنتَصِرِينَ

"And We caused the earth to swallow him and his home. And there was for him no company to aid him other than Allāh, nor was he of those who [could] defend themselves."

— Surah Al-Qasas 28:81

Allah caused the earth to swallow him entirely, along with his home. No group could aid him against Allah, and he himself was powerless to defend his own position.

The same people who had envied him just the day before now saw clearly.

وَأَصْبَحَ ٱلَّذِينَ تَمَنَّوْا۟ مَكَانَهُۥ بِٱلْأَمْسِ يَقُولُونَ وَيْكَأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَبْسُطُ ٱلرِّزْقَ لِمَن يَشَآءُ مِنْ عِبَادِهِۦ وَيَقْدِرُ ۖ لَوْلَآ أَن مَّنَّ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيْنَا لَخَسَفَ بِنَا ۖ وَيْكَأَنَّهُۥ لَا يُفْلِحُ ٱلْكَٰفِرُونَ

"And those who had wished for his position the previous day began to say, 'Oh, how Allāh extends provision to whom He wills of His servants and restricts it! If not that Allāh had conferred favor on us, He would have caused it to swallow us. Oh, how the disbelievers do not succeed!'"

— Surah Al-Qasas 28:82

They realized that Allah extends or restricts provision according to His will, completely unrelated to merit or deserving. They recognized that had Allah not shown them favor, they too could have met the same fate, and acknowledged plainly that disbelievers never truly succeed. This chapter, taken as a whole, reveals two enduring lessons: gratitude for what Allah provides, even when it seems simple or repetitive, and the danger of mistaking wealth for personal merit rather than recognizing it as a trust from Allah alone.

chapters.title: The Journey with Al-Khidr
chapters.content:
Musa (AS) once set out on a journey with his young servant, determined to keep traveling until he reached the meeting point of two seas, no matter how long it took.

وَإِذْ قَالَ مُوسَىٰ لِفَتَىٰهُ لَآ أَبْرَحُ حَتَّىٰٓ أَبْلُغَ مَجْمَعَ ٱلْبَحْرَيْنِ أَوْ أَمْضِىَ حُقُبًۭا

"And [mention] when Moses said to his boy [i.e., servant], 'I will not cease [traveling] until I reach the junction of the two seas or continue for a long period.'"

— Surah Al-Kahf 18:60

Along the way, they had brought a fish to eat. But when they reached the meeting point of the two seas, they forgot about it, and the fish slipped away, taking its own course into the sea.

فَلَمَّا بَلَغَا مَجْمَعَ بَيْنِهِمَا نَسِيَا حُوتَهُمَا فَٱتَّخَذَ سَبِيلَهُۥ فِى ٱلْبَحْرِ سَرَبًۭا

"But when they reached the junction between them, they forgot their fish, and it took its course into the sea, slipping away."

— Surah Al-Kahf 18:61

They carried on past that point, until Musa (AS) felt the tiredness of the journey and asked his servant to bring their food.

فَلَمَّا جَاوَزَا قَالَ لِفَتَىٰهُ ءَاتِنَا غَدَآءَنَا لَقَدْ لَقِينَا مِن سَفَرِنَا هَٰذَا نَصَبًۭا

"So when they had passed beyond it, [Moses] said to his boy, 'Bring us our morning meal. We have certainly suffered in this, our journey, [much] fatigue.'"

— Surah Al-Kahf 18:62

It was then that the servant remembered and explained what had happened to the fish at the rock, and that nothing made him forget to mention it except Satan.

قَالَ أَرَءَيْتَ إِذْ أَوَيْنَآ إِلَى ٱلصَّخْرَةِ فَإِنِّى نَسِيتُ ٱلْحُوتَ وَمَآ أَنسَىٰنِيهُ إِلَّا ٱلشَّيْطَٰنُ أَنْ أَذْكُرَهُۥ ۚ وَٱتَّخَذَ سَبِيلَهُۥ فِى ٱلْبَحْرِ عَجَبًۭا

"He said, 'Did you see when we retired to the rock? Indeed, I forgot [there] the fish. And none made me forget it except Satan - that I should mention it. And it took its course into the sea amazingly.'"

— Surah Al-Kahf 18:63

Musa (AS) realized this was exactly the sign they had been seeking, so they turned back, retracing their own footsteps.

قَالَ ذَٰلِكَ مَا كُنَّا نَبْغِ ۚ فَٱرْتَدَّا عَلَىٰٓ ءَاثَارِهِمَا قَصَصًۭا

"[Moses] said, 'That is what we were seeking.' So they returned, following their footprints."

— Surah Al-Kahf 18:64

There, they found a righteous servant of Allah — known as Al-Khidr — to whom Allah had given mercy and taught a special knowledge directly from Him.

فَوَجَدَا عَبْدًۭا مِّنْ عِبَادِنَآ ءَاتَيْنَٰهُ رَحْمَةًۭ مِّنْ عِندِنَا وَعَلَّمْنَٰهُ مِن لَّدُنَّا عِلْمًۭا

"And they found a servant from among Our servants [i.e., al-Khiḍr] to whom We had given mercy from Us and had taught him from Us a [certain] knowledge."

— Surah Al-Kahf 18:65

Musa (AS) humbly asked if he could follow him, in order to learn from the sound judgment he had been taught.

قَالَ لَهُۥ مُوسَىٰ هَلْ أَتَّبِعُكَ عَلَىٰٓ أَن تُعَلِّمَنِ مِمَّا عُلِّمْتَ رُشْدًۭا

"Moses said to him, 'May I follow you on [the condition] that you teach me from what you have been taught of sound judgement?'"

— Surah Al-Kahf 18:66

Al-Khidr warned him plainly that he would not be able to have patience with him.

قَالَ إِنَّكَ لَن تَسْتَطِيعَ مَعِىَ صَبْرًۭا

"He said, 'Indeed, with me you will never be able to have patience.'"

— Surah Al-Kahf 18:67

He explained why — how could Musa (AS) be patient with matters he did not have full knowledge of?

وَكَيْفَ تَصْبِرُ عَلَىٰ مَا لَمْ تُحِطْ بِهِۦ خُبْرًۭا

"And how can you have patience for what you do not encompass in knowledge?"

— Surah Al-Kahf 18:68

Still, Musa (AS) promised, with Allah's will, to be patient and not disobey any instruction given to him.

قَالَ سَتَجِدُنِىٓ إِن شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ صَابِرًۭا وَلَآ أَعْصِى لَكَ أَمْرًۭا

"[Moses] said, 'You will find me, if Allāh wills, patient, and I will not disobey you in [any] order.'"

— Surah Al-Kahf 18:69

Al-Khidr set one condition: Musa (AS) must not ask about anything until he himself chose to explain it.

قَالَ فَإِنِ ٱتَّبَعْتَنِى فَلَا تَسْـَٔلْنِى عَن شَىْءٍ حَتَّىٰٓ أُحْدِثَ لَكَ مِنْهُ ذِكْرًۭا

"He said, 'Then if you follow me, do not ask me about anything until I make to you about it mention [i.e., explanation].'"

— Surah Al-Kahf 18:70

They set out together. When they boarded a ship, Al-Khidr tore a hole in it. Musa (AS) could not stay silent, objecting that this could drown its people.

فَٱنطَلَقَا حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا رَكِبَا فِى ٱلسَّفِينَةِ خَرَقَهَا ۖ قَالَ أَخَرَقْتَهَا لِتُغْرِقَ أَهْلَهَا لَقَدْ جِئْتَ شَيْـًٔا إِمْرًۭا

"So they set out, until when they had embarked on the ship, he [i.e., al-Khiḍr] tore it open. [Moses] said, 'Have you torn it open to drown its people? You have certainly done a grave thing.'"

— Surah Al-Kahf 18:71

Al-Khidr reminded him of his earlier warning — that he would not be able to have patience.

قَالَ أَلَمْ أَقُلْ إِنَّكَ لَن تَسْتَطِيعَ مَعِىَ صَبْرًۭا

"[Al-Khiḍr] said, 'Did I not say that with me you would never be able to have patience?'"

— Surah Al-Kahf 18:72

Musa (AS) asked not to be blamed for forgetting his promise, and asked not to be made to face too much difficulty.

قَالَ لَا تُؤَاخِذْنِى بِمَا نَسِيتُ وَلَا تُرْهِقْنِى مِنْ أَمْرِى عُسْرًۭا

"[Moses] said, 'Do not blame me for what I forgot and do not overwhelm me in my matter with difficulty.'"

— Surah Al-Kahf 18:73

They continued on, until they met a boy, and Al-Khidr killed him. This time Musa (AS) objected even more strongly, calling it a deplorable act against an innocent soul.

فَٱنطَلَقَا حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا لَقِيَا غُلَٰمًۭا فَقَتَلَهُۥ قَالَ أَقَتَلْتَ نَفْسًۭا زَكِيَّةًۢ بِغَيْرِ نَفْسٍۢ لَّقَدْ جِئْتَ شَيْـًۭٔا نُّكْرًۭا

"So they set out, until when they met a boy, he [i.e., al-Khiḍr] killed him. [Moses] said, 'Have you killed a pure soul for other than [having killed] a soul? You have certainly done a deplorable thing.'"

— Surah Al-Kahf 18:74

Al-Khidr again reminded him of his warning.

۞ قَالَ أَلَمْ أَقُل لَّكَ إِنَّكَ لَن تَسْتَطِيعَ مَعِىَ صَبْرًۭا

"[Al-Khiḍr] said, 'Did I not tell you that with me you would never be able to have patience?'"

— Surah Al-Kahf 18:75

Musa (AS) then gave his final word — if he questioned anything again after this, Al-Khidr could rightfully part ways with him.

قَالَ إِن سَأَلْتُكَ عَن شَىْءٍۭ بَعْدَهَا فَلَا تُصَٰحِبْنِى ۖ قَدْ بَلَغْتَ مِن لَّدُنِّى عُذْرًۭا

"[Moses] said, 'If I should ask you about anything after this, then do not keep me as a companion. You have obtained from me an excuse.'"

— Surah Al-Kahf 18:76

They went on until they reached a town. Its people refused to host them, yet they found a wall about to collapse, and Al-Khidr repaired it without asking for payment. Musa (AS) pointed out that he could have taken a wage for the work.

فَٱنطَلَقَا حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَآ أَتَيَآ أَهْلَ قَرْيَةٍ ٱسْتَطْعَمَآ أَهْلَهَا فَأَبَوْا۟ أَن يُضَيِّفُوهُمَا فَوَجَدَا فِيهَا جِدَارًۭا يُرِيدُ أَن يَنقَضَّ فَأَقَامَهُۥ ۖ قَالَ لَوْ شِئْتَ لَتَّخَذْتَ عَلَيْهِ أَجْرًۭا

"So they set out, until when they came to the people of a town, they asked its people for food, but they refused to offer them hospitality. And they found therein a wall about to collapse, so he [i.e., al-Khiḍr] restored it. [Moses] said, 'If you wished, you could have taken for it a payment.'"

— Surah Al-Kahf 18:77

This was the moment Al-Khidr declared their parting, promising now to explain the meaning behind everything Musa (AS) could not have patience with.

قَالَ هَٰذَا فِرَاقُ بَيْنِى وَبَيْنِكَ ۚ سَأُنَبِّئُكَ بِتَأْوِيلِ مَا لَمْ تَسْتَطِع عَّلَيْهِ صَبْرًا

"[Al-Khiḍr] said, 'This is parting between me and you. I will inform you of the interpretation of that about which you could not have patience.'"

— Surah Al-Kahf 18:78

First, the ship: it belonged to poor people who worked at sea, and a king nearby was seizing every good ship by force. Damaging it slightly was what kept it safe from being taken.

أَمَّا ٱلسَّفِينَةُ فَكَانَتْ لِمَسَٰكِينَ يَعْمَلُونَ فِى ٱلْبَحْرِ فَأَرَدتُّ أَنْ أَعِيبَهَا وَكَانَ وَرَآءَهُم مَّلِكٌۭ يَأْخُذُ كُلَّ سَفِينَةٍ غَصْبًۭا

"As for the ship, it belonged to poor people working at sea. So I intended to cause defect in it as there was after them a king who seized every [good] ship by force."

— Surah Al-Kahf 18:79

Next, the boy: his parents were believers, and Allah and Al-Khidr feared he would grow up to burden them with transgression and disbelief.

وَأَمَّا ٱلْغُلَٰمُ فَكَانَ أَبَوَاهُ مُؤْمِنَيْنِ فَخَشِينَآ أَن يُرْهِقَهُمَا طُغْيَٰنًۭا وَكُفْرًۭا

"And as for the boy, his parents were believers, and we feared that he would overburden them by transgression and disbelief."

— Surah Al-Kahf 18:80

So it was intended that their Lord would replace him with a child better in purity and nearer in mercy.

فَأَرَدْنَآ أَن يُبْدِلَهُمَا رَبُّهُمَا خَيْرًۭا مِّنْهُ زَكَوٰةًۭ وَأَقْرَبَ رُحْمًۭا

"So we intended that their Lord should substitute for them one better than him in purity and nearer to mercy."

— Surah Al-Kahf 18:81

Finally, the wall: beneath it lay a treasure belonging to two orphan boys in the city, whose father had been righteous. Allah intended for them to grow up and recover their treasure themselves, as a mercy from Him. Al-Khidr closed by affirming that none of what he did was from his own will — it was all the meaning behind what Musa (AS) could not have patience with.

وَأَمَّا ٱلْجِدَارُ فَكَانَ لِغُلَٰمَيْنِ يَتِيمَيْنِ فِى ٱلْمَدِينَةِ وَكَانَ تَحْتَهُۥ كَنزٌۭ لَّهُمَا وَكَانَ أَبُوهُمَا صَٰلِحًۭا فَأَرَادَ رَبُّكَ أَن يَبْلُغَآ أَشُدَّهُمَا وَيَسْتَخْرِجَا كَنزَهُمَا رَحْمَةًۭ مِّن رَّبِّكَ ۚ وَمَا فَعَلْتُهُۥ عَنْ أَمْرِى ۚ ذَٰلِكَ تَأْوِيلُ مَا لَمْ تَسْطِع عَّلَيْهِ صَبْرًۭا

"And as for the wall, it belonged to two orphan boys in the city, and there was beneath it a treasure for them, and their father had been righteous. So your Lord intended that they reach maturity and extract their treasure, as a mercy from your Lord. And I did it not of my own accord. That is the interpretation of that about which you could not have patience."

— Surah Al-Kahf 18:82

This story carries a deep lesson: even a prophet as great as Musa (AS) could not see the full wisdom behind events as they unfolded. True knowledge belongs to Allah alone, and what appears difficult or troubling on the surface may carry mercy and wisdom we cannot yet see.

chapters.title: Legacy and Lessons
chapters.content:
The story of Musa (AS) carries a status unlike most other prophets — a distinction Allah Himself highlights directly.

وَرُسُلًۭا قَدْ قَصَصْنَٰهُمْ عَلَيْكَ مِن قَبْلُ وَرُسُلًۭا لَّمْ نَقْصُصْهُمْ عَلَيْكَ ۚ وَكَلَّمَ ٱللَّهُ مُوسَىٰ تَكْلِيمًۭا

"And [We sent] messengers about whom We have related [their stories] to you before and messengers about whom We have not related to you. And Allāh spoke to Moses with [direct] speech."

— Surah An-Nisa 4:164

Among all the messengers sent — some whose stories Allah has told, and others whose stories were never told — Musa (AS) is singled out for a unique honor: Allah spoke to him directly. This is why he is known as Kalimullah, the one Allah spoke to.

The Quran affirms his sincerity and his rank clearly.

وَٱذْكُرْ فِى ٱلْكِتَٰبِ مُوسَىٰٓ ۚ إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ مُخْلَصًۭا وَكَانَ رَسُولًۭا نَّبِيًّۭا

"And mention in the Book, Moses. Indeed, he was chosen, and he was a messenger and a prophet."

— Surah Maryam 19:51

Allah describes him as chosen — a man of sincerity — carrying both ranks of messenger and prophet.

The closeness Allah granted him is described in vivid terms.

وَنَٰدَيْنَٰهُ مِن جَانِبِ ٱلطُّورِ ٱلْأَيْمَنِ وَقَرَّبْنَٰهُ نَجِيًّۭا

"And We called him from the side of the mount at [his] right and brought him near, confiding [to him]."

— Surah Maryam 19:52

Allah called him from the right side of the mount and drew him near in a private, confiding closeness — a moment of intimacy between Creator and servant that few are ever granted.

And in His mercy, Allah did not leave him to carry this mission alone.

وَوَهَبْنَا لَهُۥ مِن رَّحْمَتِنَآ أَخَاهُ هَٰرُونَ نَبِيًّۭا

"And We gave him out of Our mercy his brother Aaron as a prophet."

— Surah Maryam 19:53

Out of His mercy, Allah gave Musa (AS) his brother Harun as a prophet too — a companion in da'wah, a support in hardship, and a reminder that even the strongest of messengers were given help to carry their burden.

Beyond his personal honor, Musa's (AS) greatest legacy to humanity was the Book he was given.

ثُمَّ ءَاتَيْنَا مُوسَى ٱلْكِتَٰبَ تَمَامًا عَلَى ٱلَّذِىٓ أَحْسَنَ وَتَفْصِيلًۭا لِّكُلِّ شَىْءٍۢ وَهُدًۭى وَرَحْمَةًۭ لَّعَلَّهُم بِلِقَآءِ رَبِّهِمْ يُؤْمِنُونَ

"Then We gave Moses the Scripture, making complete [Our favor] upon the one who did good [i.e., Moses] and as a detailed explanation of all things and as guidance and mercy that perhaps in the meeting with their Lord they would believe."

— Surah Al-An'am 6:154

Allah gave Musa (AS) the Scripture as the completion of His favor upon him for the good he had done, containing detailed explanation for all things, and serving as guidance and mercy — so that people might come to believe in their eventual meeting with their Lord.

This gift of guidance came at a pivotal point in history.

وَلَقَدْ ءَاتَيْنَا مُوسَى ٱلْكِتَٰبَ مِنۢ بَعْدِ مَآ أَهْلَكْنَا ٱلْقُرُونَ ٱلْأُولَىٰ بَصَآئِرَ لِلنَّاسِ وَهُدًۭى وَرَحْمَةًۭ لَّعَلَّهُمْ يَتَذَكَّرُونَ

"And We gave Moses the Scripture, after We had destroyed the former generations, as enlightenment for the people and guidance and mercy that they might be reminded."

— Surah Al-Qasas 28:43

After Allah had already destroyed the earlier generations who rejected the truth, He gave Musa (AS) the Scripture as a source of enlightenment, guidance, and mercy for all people — so that they would remember and take heed.

Looking back across his entire story — from the basket on the river, to the fire at the mountain, to the staff before Pharaoh, to the sea splitting open, to the patience he tried to learn from Al-Khidr, to this final honor of direct speech with Allah — the life of Musa (AS) stands as one of the most detailed and repeated narratives in the Quran. His story teaches that Allah's help comes even in the most hopeless moments, that knowledge and patience must be sought humbly, that ingratitude carries real consequences, and that true honor lies not in wealth or worldly power, like Qarun assumed, but in sincerity, obedience, and closeness to Allah. Musa (AS) remains Kalimullah — the one Allah spoke to directly — a mercy and a guide for every generation that came after him.

title: The Story of Yusuf (AS) — The Most Beautiful Story
summary: Yusuf (AS) was betrayed by his own brothers, sold into slavery, tested through false accusation and imprisonment, and ultimately raised to a position of great trust in Egypt — reuniting with his family through patience, forgiveness, and unwavering trust in Allah. His story is told as a single continuous narrative in Surah Yusuf, described by Allah as "the most beautiful of stories."

chapters.title: The Dream and the Brothers' Jealousy
chapters.content:
The story of Yusuf (AS) begins with a dream — a dream that would shape the course of his entire life. He was still young, living with his father, the Prophet Ya'qub (AS), when he saw something amazing in his sleep.

إِذْ قَالَ يُوسُفُ لِأَبِيهِ يَٰٓأَبَتِ إِنِّى رَأَيْتُ أَحَدَ عَشَرَ كَوْكَبًۭا وَٱلشَّمْسَ وَٱلْقَمَرَ رَأَيْتُهُمْ لِى سَٰجِدِينَ

"[Of these stories mention] when Joseph said to his father, 'O my father, indeed I have seen [in a dream] eleven stars and the sun and the moon; I saw them prostrating to me.'"

— Surah Yusuf 12:4

Yusuf went to his father and told him about the dream. He said he saw eleven stars, the sun, and the moon — and all of them were bowing down to him. This was no ordinary dream. It was a sign from Allah, though its full meaning would not be clear until many years later.

Ya'qub (AS), being a wise and caring father, understood right away that this dream carried something important — and something dangerous if shared carelessly.

قَالَ يَٰبُنَىَّ لَا تَقْصُصْ رُءْيَاكَ عَلَىٰٓ إِخْوَتِكَ فَيَكِيدُوا۟ لَكَ كَيْدًا ۖ إِنَّ ٱلشَّيْطَٰنَ لِلْإِنسَٰنِ عَدُوٌّۭ مُّبِينٌۭ

"He said, 'O my son, do not relate your vision to your brothers or they will contrive against you a plan. Indeed Satan, to man, is a manifest enemy.'"

— Surah Yusuf 12:5

Ya'qub (AS) warned his son gently but seriously: do not tell this dream to your brothers. He knew that if they heard it, they might feel jealous and plan something against him. He reminded Yusuf that Shaytan works hard to turn people against each other, especially through feelings like jealousy and envy.

Then Ya'qub (AS) gave Yusuf some comforting and hopeful words about what this dream truly meant.

وَكَذَٰلِكَ يَجْتَبِيكَ رَبُّكَ وَيُعَلِّمُكَ مِن تَأْوِيلِ ٱلْأَحَادِيثِ وَيُتِمُّ نِعْمَتَهُۥ عَلَيْكَ وَعَلَىٰٓ ءَالِ يَعْقُوبَ كَمَآ أَتَمَّهَا عَلَىٰٓ أَبَوَيْكَ مِن قَبْلُ إِبْرَٰهِيمَ وَإِسْحَٰقَ ۚ إِنَّ رَبَّكَ عَلِيمٌ حَكِيمٌۭ

"And thus will your Lord choose you and teach you the interpretation of narratives [i.e., events or dreams] and complete His favor upon you and upon the family of Jacob, as He completed it upon your fathers before, Abraham and Isaac. Indeed, your Lord is Knowing and Wise."

— Surah Yusuf 12:6

Ya'qub (AS) told Yusuf that Allah was going to choose him for something special. Allah would teach him how to understand the deeper meaning of dreams and events, and would complete His blessing upon him and upon the whole family of Ya'qub — just as He had done for his forefathers, Ibrahim (AS) and Ishaq (AS). Allah is always Knowing and Wise, and everything happens exactly the way He plans it.

This short conversation between a father and his son sets the stage for everything that follows. A simple dream — and a father's wise caution — becomes the beginning of one of the most moving and beautiful stories in the entire Quran.

chapters.title: Thrown into the Well
chapters.content:
Allah tells us at the very start of this part of the story that there are important lessons here for anyone who wants to learn.

۞ لَّقَدْ كَانَ فِى يُوسُفَ وَإِخْوَتِهِۦٓ ءَايَٰتٌۭ لِّلسَّآئِلِينَ

"Certainly were there in Joseph and his brothers signs for those who ask, [such as]"

— Surah Yusuf 12:7

Allah lets us know that the story of Yusuf and his brothers holds real lessons for anyone who is sincerely looking for them.

The trouble began with jealousy in the hearts of Yusuf's brothers.

إِذْ قَالُوا۟ لَيُوسُفُ وَأَخُوهُ أَحَبُّ إِلَىٰٓ أَبِينَا مِنَّا وَنَحْنُ عُصْبَةٌ إِنَّ أَبَانَا لَفِى ضَلَٰلٍۢ مُّبِينٍ

"When they said, 'Joseph and his brother are more beloved to our father than we, while we are a clan. Indeed, our father is in clear error.'"

— Surah Yusuf 12:8

The brothers complained among themselves, saying that Yusuf and his younger brother were loved more by their father, even though they themselves were a strong group. They even said their father was clearly mistaken in loving Yusuf so much.

Their jealousy grew into a dangerous plan.

ٱقْتُلُوا۟ يُوسُفَ أَوِ ٱطْرَحُوهُ أَرْضًۭا يَخْلُ لَكُمْ وَجْهُ أَبِيكُمْ وَتَكُونُوا۟ مِنۢ بَعْدِهِۦ قَوْمًۭا صَٰلِحِينَ

"Kill Joseph or cast him out to [another] land; the countenance [i.e., attention] of your father will [then] be only for you, and you will be after that a righteous people."

— Surah Yusuf 12:9

Some of the brothers suggested either killing Yusuf or sending him far away, so that their father's attention would belong only to them. They told themselves that afterward, they could simply be good people again.

But one of the brothers softened the plan.

قَالَ قَآئِلٌۭ مِّنْهُمْ لَا تَقْتُلُوا۟ يُوسُفَ وَأَلْقُوهُ فِى غَيَٰبَتِ ٱلْجُبِّ يَلْتَقِطْهُ بَعْضُ ٱلسَّيَّارَةِ إِن كُنتُمْ فَٰعِلِينَ

"Said a speaker among them, 'Do not kill Joseph but throw him into the bottom of the well; some travelers will pick him up - if you would do [something].'"

— Surah Yusuf 12:10

One brother spoke up and said not to kill Yusuf, but instead to throw him into the bottom of a well. He suggested that some traveling people would likely find him and take him away — if they were going to do anything at all.

The brothers then went to their father with a plan to get Yusuf away from him.

قَالُوا۟ يَٰٓأَبَانَا مَا لَكَ لَا تَأْمَ۫نَّا عَلَىٰ يُوسُفَ وَإِنَّا لَهُۥ لَنَٰصِحُونَ

"They said, 'O our father, why do you not entrust us with Joseph while indeed, we are to him sincere counselors?'"

— Surah Yusuf 12:11

They asked their father why he wouldn't trust them with Yusuf, insisting that they truly cared about him and meant him well.

أَرْسِلْهُ مَعَنَا غَدًۭا يَرْتَعْ وَيَلْعَبْ وَإِنَّا لَهُۥ لَحَٰفِظُونَ

"Send him with us tomorrow that he may eat well and play. And indeed, we will be his guardians."

— Surah Yusuf 12:12

They asked their father to let Yusuf come out with them the next day to enjoy himself and play, promising that they would watch over him carefully.

Ya'qub (AS) hesitated, sharing his concern honestly.

قَالَ إِنِّى لَيَحْزُنُنِىٓ أَن تَذْهَبُوا۟ بِهِۦ وَأَخَافُ أَن يَأْكُلَهُ ٱلذِّئْبُ وَأَنتُمْ عَنْهُ غَٰفِلُونَ

"[Jacob] said, 'Indeed, it saddens me that you should take him, and I fear that a wolf would eat him while you are of him unaware.'"

— Surah Yusuf 12:13

Ya'qub (AS) told them it would sadden him if they took Yusuf away, and that he feared a wolf might harm him if they weren't paying close enough attention.

The brothers reassured him, confident in their own numbers.

قَالُوا۟ لَئِنْ أَكَلَهُ ٱلذِّئْبُ وَنَحْنُ عُصْبَةٌ إِنَّآ إِذًۭا لَّخَٰسِرُونَ

"They said, 'If a wolf should eat him while we are a [strong] clan, indeed, we would then be losers.'"

— Surah Yusuf 12:14

They told their father that if a wolf could harm Yusuf while so many of them were there to protect him, then they would truly have failed.

So Ya'qub (AS) allowed it — and the brothers carried out their plan.

فَلَمَّا ذَهَبُوا۟ بِهِۦ وَأَجْمَعُوٓا۟ أَن يَجْعَلُوهُ فِى غَيَٰبَتِ ٱلْجُبِّ ۚ وَأَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَيْهِ لَتُنَبِّئَنَّهُم بِأَمْرِهِمْ هَٰذَا وَهُمْ لَا يَشْعُرُونَ

"So when they took him [out] and agreed to put him into the bottom of the well... But We inspired to him, 'You will surely inform them [someday] about this affair of theirs while they do not perceive [your identity].'"

— Surah Yusuf 12:15

Once they had taken Yusuf out and agreed to put him at the bottom of the well, Allah inspired him with reassurance — that one day he would tell his brothers exactly what they had done, at a time when they wouldn't even recognize him.

The brothers then returned home, pretending to grieve.

وَجَآءُوٓ أَبَاهُمْ عِشَآءًۭ يَبْكُونَ

"And they came to their father at night, weeping."

— Surah Yusuf 12:16

They came back to their father at night, crying as if something terrible had truly happened.

قَالُوا۟ يَٰٓأَبَانَآ إِنَّا ذَهَبْنَا نَسْتَبِقُ وَتَرَكْنَا يُوسُفَ عِندَ مَتَٰعِنَا فَأَكَلَهُ ٱلذِّئْبُ ۖ وَمَآ أَنتَ بِمُؤْمِنٍۢ لَّنَا وَلَوْ كُنَّا صَٰدِقِينَ

"They said, 'O our father, indeed we went racing each other and left Joseph with our possessions, and a wolf ate him. But you would not believe us, even if we were truthful.'"

— Surah Yusuf 12:17

They told their father they had been racing one another and left Yusuf with their belongings, and that a wolf had eaten him. They added that he probably wouldn't believe them, even if they were telling the truth.

To support their lie, they brought false evidence.

وَجَآءُو عَلَىٰ قَمِيصِهِۦ بِدَمٍۢ كَذِبٍۢ ۚ قَالَ بَلْ سَوَّلَتْ لَكُمْ أَنفُسُكُمْ أَمْرًۭا ۖ فَصَبْرٌۭ جَمِيلٌۭ ۖ وَٱللَّهُ ٱلْمُسْتَعَانُ عَلَىٰ مَا تَصِفُونَ

"And they brought upon his shirt false blood. [Jacob] said, 'Rather, your souls have enticed you to something, so patience is most fitting. And Allāh is the one sought for help against that which you describe.'"

— Surah Yusuf 12:18

They brought Yusuf's shirt stained with blood that wasn't really his. But Ya'qub (AS) saw through it. He told them that their own desires had led them to do something wrong, and that beautiful patience was the only fitting response. He turned to Allah alone for help in facing what they had described.

This is one of the most painful moments in the story — a father's deep love met with his sons' deception. Yet even here, Ya'qub (AS) shows us the way forward: patience, and turning only to Allah.

chapters.title: Sold into Egypt
chapters.content:
Down in the bottom of the well, Yusuf (AS) was alone and frightened. But Allah's plan was already in motion, even in this dark moment.

وَجَآءَتْ سَيَّارَةٌۭ فَأَرْسَلُوا۟ وَارِدَهُمْ فَأَدْلَىٰ دَلْوَهُۥ ۖ قَالَ يَٰبُشْرَىٰ هَٰذَا غُلَٰمٌۭ ۚ وَأَسَرُّوهُ بِضَٰعَةًۭ ۚ وَٱللَّهُ عَلِيمٌۢ بِمَا يَعْمَلُونَ

"And there came a company of travelers; then they sent their water drawer, and he let down his bucket. He said, 'Good news! Here is a boy.' And they concealed him, [taking him] as merchandise; and Allāh was Knowing of what they did."

— Surah Yusuf 12:19

A group of travelers arrived near the well. They sent someone to draw water, and when he lowered his bucket, he was surprised to find a boy instead. Excited, he called out the good news to the others. The travelers then hid Yusuf away, planning to sell him as goods. But nothing was hidden from Allah — He knew exactly what they were doing, even when they thought no one could see.

They quickly sold him for very little.

وَشَرَوْهُ بِثَمَنٍۭ بَخْسٍۢ دَرَٰهِمَ مَعْدُودَةٍۢ وَكَانُوا۟ فِيهِ مِنَ ٱلزَّٰهِدِينَ

"And they sold him for a reduced price - a few dirhams - and they were, concerning him, of those content with little."

— Surah Yusuf 12:20

Yusuf was sold for a very small amount of money — just a few coins. Those who sold him didn't think he was worth very much at all, and they were satisfied with this small price.

In Egypt, a new chapter of his life began under the care of a man of position.

وَقَالَ ٱلَّذِى ٱشْتَرَىٰهُ مِن مِّصْرَ لِٱمْرَأَتِهِۦٓ أَكْرِمِى مَثْوَىٰهُ عَسَىٰٓ أَن يَنفَعَنَآ أَوْ نَتَّخِذَهُۥ وَلَدًۭا ۚ وَكَذَٰلِكَ مَكَّنَّا لِيُوسُفَ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ وَلِنُعَلِّمَهُۥ مِن تَأْوِيلِ ٱلْأَحَادِيثِ ۚ وَٱللَّهُ غَالِبٌ عَلَىٰٓ أَمْرِهِۦ وَلَٰكِنَّ أَكْثَرَ ٱلنَّاسِ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ

"And the one from Egypt who bought him said to his wife, 'Make his residence comfortable. Perhaps he will benefit us, or we will adopt him as a son.' And thus, We established Joseph in the land that We might teach him the interpretation of events [i.e., dreams]. And Allāh is predominant over His affair, but most of the people do not know."

— Surah Yusuf 12:21

The man from Egypt who bought Yusuf told his wife to treat him well and make him comfortable, hoping he might be useful to them or that they could even raise him like a son. Allah tells us that this was all part of His plan — to settle Yusuf firmly in the land of Egypt and to teach him the meaning of dreams and events. Allah's plan always succeeds, even though most people don't realize it while it's happening.

As Yusuf grew older, Allah blessed him with something even greater than comfort.

وَلَمَّا بَلَغَ أَشُدَّهُۥٓ ءَاتَيْنَٰهُ حُكْمًۭا وَعِلْمًۭا ۚ وَكَذَٰلِكَ نَجْزِى ٱلْمُحْسِنِينَ

"And when he [i.e., Joseph] reached maturity, We gave him judgement and knowledge. And thus We reward the doers of good."

— Surah Yusuf 12:22

When Yusuf reached full maturity, Allah gave him sound judgement and deep knowledge. This is how Allah rewards those who do good — even after hardship, even after being thrown into a well and sold far from home, Allah was preparing Yusuf for something far greater than he could have imagined.

What seemed like the worst moment of Yusuf's life — being sold as a slave in a foreign land — was, in truth, the very path Allah had chosen to raise him in status, wisdom, and knowledge.

chapters.title: The Temptation
chapters.content:
Yusuf (AS) was now living in the house in Egypt where he had been bought. Here, he faced one of the greatest tests of his life.

وَرَٰوَدَتْهُ ٱلَّتِى هُوَ فِى بَيْتِهَا عَن نَّفْسِهِۦ وَغَلَّقَتِ ٱلْأَبْوَٰبَ وَقَالَتْ هَيْتَ لَكَ ۚ قَالَ مَعَاذَ ٱللَّهِ ۖ إِنَّهُۥ رَبِّىٓ أَحْسَنَ مَثْوَاىَ ۖ إِنَّهُۥ لَا يُفْلِحُ ٱلظَّٰلِمُونَ

"And she, in whose house he was, sought to seduce him. She closed the doors and said, 'Come, you.' He said, '[I seek] the refuge of Allāh. Indeed, he is my master, who has made good my residence. Indeed, wrongdoers will not succeed.'"

— Surah Yusuf 12:23

The lady of the house tried to lead Yusuf (AS) astray. She closed the doors and called him to her. But Yusuf (AS) immediately sought refuge with Allah. He said that his Lord was his true master, who had made his stay good — and that wrongdoers never succeed.

This was a difficult moment, but Allah protected Yusuf (AS) by His grace.

وَلَقَدْ هَمَّتْ بِهِۦ ۖ وَهَمَّ بِهَا لَوْلَآ أَن رَّءَا بُرْهَٰنَ رَبِّهِۦ ۚ كَذَٰلِكَ لِنَصْرِفَ عَنْهُ ٱلسُّوٓءَ وَٱلْفَحْشَآءَ ۚ إِنَّهُۥ مِنْ عِبَادِنَا ٱلْمُخْلَصِينَ

"And she certainly determined [to seduce] him, and he would have inclined to her had he not seen the proof [i.e., sign] of his Lord. And thus [it was] that We should avert from him evil and immorality. Indeed, he was of Our chosen servants."

— Surah Yusuf 12:24

Allah tells us that had Yusuf (AS) not seen the proof from his Lord, he might have inclined toward her. But Allah turned evil and immorality away from him, because he was among Allah's chosen, sincere servants.

What happened next unfolded very quickly.

وَٱسْتَبَقَا ٱلْبَابَ وَقَدَّتْ قَمِيصَهُۥ مِن دُبُرٍۢ وَأَلْفَيَا سَيِّدَهَا لَدَا ٱلْبَابِ ۚ قَالَتْ مَا جَزَآءُ مَنْ أَرَادَ بِأَهْلِكَ سُوٓءًا إِلَّآ أَن يُسْجَنَ أَوْ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌۭ

"And they both raced to the door, and she tore his shirt from the back, and they found her husband at the door. She said, 'What is the recompense of one who intended evil for your wife but that he be imprisoned or a painful punishment?'"

— Surah Yusuf 12:25

Both of them raced to the door, and she tore his shirt from the back. At the door, they found her husband. She immediately accused Yusuf (AS), claiming he deserved imprisonment or punishment for wronging her.

Yusuf (AS) told the truth, and Allah sent a witness to bring that truth to light.

قَالَ هِىَ رَٰوَدَتْنِى عَن نَّفْسِى ۚ وَشَهِدَ شَاهِدٌۭ مِّنْ أَهْلِهَآ إِن كَانَ قَمِيصُهُۥ قُدَّ مِن قُبُلٍۢ فَصَدَقَتْ وَهُوَ مِنَ ٱلْكَٰذِبِينَ

"[Joseph] said, 'It was she who sought to seduce me.' And a witness from her family testified, 'If his shirt is torn from the front, then she has told the truth, and he is of the liars.'"

— Surah Yusuf 12:26

Yusuf (AS) clearly stated that it was she who had tried to seduce him. A witness from her own family proposed a simple test: if his shirt was torn from the front, she was telling the truth, and Yusuf (AS) was lying.

وَإِن كَانَ قَمِيصُهُۥ قُدَّ مِن دُبُرٍۢ فَكَذَبَتْ وَهُوَ مِنَ ٱلصَّٰدِقِينَ

"But if his shirt is torn from the back, then she has lied, and he is of the truthful."

— Surah Yusuf 12:27

But if the shirt was torn from the back, then she was lying, and Yusuf (AS) was telling the truth.

When the truth came out, her husband understood exactly what had happened.

فَلَمَّا رَءَا قَمِيصَهُۥ قُدَّ مِن دُبُرٍۢ قَالَ إِنَّهُۥ مِن كَيْدِكُنَّ ۖ إِنَّ كَيْدَكُنَّ عَظِيمٌۭ

"So when he [i.e., her husband] saw his shirt torn from the back, he said, 'Indeed, it is of your [i.e., women's] plan. Indeed, your plan is great [i.e., vehement].'"

— Surah Yusuf 12:28

When he saw the shirt torn from the back, he realized this was her doing, and remarked on how powerful such schemes can be.

He then gave instruction to both of them.

يُوسُفُ أَعْرِضْ عَنْ هَٰذَا ۚ وَٱسْتَغْفِرِى لِذَنۢبِكِ ۖ إِنَّكِ كُنتِ مِنَ ٱلْخَاطِـِٔينَ

"Joseph, ignore this. And, [my wife], ask forgiveness for your sin. Indeed, you were of the sinful."

— Surah Yusuf 12:29

He told Yusuf (AS) to let the matter go, and told his wife to seek forgiveness for her sin, since she was the one at fault.

This episode teaches us that truth comes to light in the end, and Allah protects His righteous servants in their most difficult moments — all they must do is place their trust in Him.

chapters.title: Scandal and Imprisonment
chapters.content:
News of what happened in the house did not stay hidden for long. It soon became the talk of the city.

۞ وَقَالَ نِسْوَةٌۭ فِى ٱلْمَدِينَةِ ٱمْرَأَتُ ٱلْعَزِيزِ تُرَٰوِدُ فَتَىٰهَا عَن نَّفْسِهِۦ ۖ قَدْ شَغَفَهَا حُبًّا ۖ إِنَّا لَنَرَىٰهَا فِى ضَلَٰلٍۢ مُّبِينٍۢ

"And women in the city said, 'The wife of al-ʿAzeez is seeking to seduce her slave boy; he has impassioned her with love. Indeed, we see her [to be] in clear error.'"

— Surah Yusuf 12:30

Women in the city began to gossip about her, saying she had tried to seduce her own servant and had fallen deeply in love with him. They judged her as being clearly in the wrong.

To silence this gossip, she devised a plan to prove her point in front of them.

فَلَمَّا سَمِعَتْ بِمَكْرِهِنَّ أَرْسَلَتْ إِلَيْهِنَّ وَأَعْتَدَتْ لَهُنَّ مُتَّكَـًۭٔا وَءَاتَتْ كُلَّ وَٰحِدَةٍۢ مِّنْهُنَّ سِكِّينًۭا وَقَالَتِ ٱخْرُجْ عَلَيْهِنَّ ۖ فَلَمَّا رَأَيْنَهُۥٓ أَكْبَرْنَهُۥ وَقَطَّعْنَ أَيْدِيَهُنَّ وَقُلْنَ حَٰشَ لِلَّهِ مَا هَٰذَا بَشَرًا إِنْ هَٰذَآ إِلَّا مَلَكٌۭ كَرِيمٌۭ

"So when she heard of their scheming, she sent for them and prepared for them a banquet and gave each one of them a knife and said [to Joseph], 'Come out before them.' And when they saw him, they greatly admired him and cut their hands and said, 'Perfect is Allāh! This is not a man; this is none but a noble angel.'"

— Surah Yusuf 12:31

She invited these women, arranged a gathering, and gave each of them a knife. Then she asked Yusuf (AS) to come out before them. When they saw him, they were so struck by his appearance that they cut their own hands without realizing it, exclaiming that he could not possibly be an ordinary man — he seemed like a noble angel.

She then made her position to them very clear.

قَالَتْ فَذَٰلِكُنَّ ٱلَّذِى لُمْتُنَّنِى فِيهِ ۖ وَلَقَدْ رَٰوَدتُّهُۥ عَن نَّفْسِهِۦ فَٱسْتَعْصَمَ ۖ وَلَئِن لَّمْ يَفْعَلْ مَآ ءَامُرُهُۥ لَيُسْجَنَنَّ وَلَيَكُونًۭا مِّنَ ٱلصَّٰغِرِينَ

"She said, 'That is the one about whom you blamed me. And I certainly sought to seduce him, but he firmly refused; and if he will not do what I order him, he will surely be imprisoned and will be of those debased.'"

— Surah Yusuf 12:32

She admitted openly that she had tried to seduce him, but he had firmly refused. She then threatened that if he continued to resist her wishes, he would be imprisoned and humiliated.

Faced with this pressure, Yusuf (AS) turned only to Allah.

قَالَ رَبِّ ٱلسِّجْنُ أَحَبُّ إِلَىَّ مِمَّا يَدْعُونَنِىٓ إِلَيْهِ ۖ وَإِلَّا تَصْرِفْ عَنِّى كَيْدَهُنَّ أَصْبُ إِلَيْهِنَّ وَأَكُن مِّنَ ٱلْجَٰهِلِينَ

"He said, 'My Lord, prison is more to my liking than that to which they invite me. And if You do not avert from me their plan, I might incline toward them and [thus] be of the ignorant.'"

— Surah Yusuf 12:33

Yusuf (AS) prayed to Allah, saying that he would rather go to prison than give in to what he was being invited toward. He asked Allah to protect him from their scheming, fearing that without Allah's help, he might fall into wrongdoing out of weakness.

Allah answered his sincere prayer.

فَٱسْتَجَابَ لَهُۥ رَبُّهُۥ فَصَرَفَ عَنْهُ كَيْدَهُنَّ ۚ إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ ٱلسَّمِيعُ ٱلْعَلِيمُ

"So his Lord responded to him and averted from him their plan. Indeed, He is the Hearing, the Knowing."

— Surah Yusuf 12:34

Allah responded to him and turned their scheming away from him. Allah is always Hearing every prayer and Knowing every circumstance, no matter how difficult it seems.

Even though his innocence was clear, the outcome was still imprisonment.

ثُمَّ بَدَا لَهُم مِّنۢ بَعْدِ مَا رَأَوُا۟ ٱلْءَايَٰتِ لَيَسْجُنُنَّهُۥ حَتَّىٰ حِينٍۢ

"Then it appeared to them after they had seen the signs that he [i.e., al-ʿAzeez] should surely imprison him for a time."

— Surah Yusuf 12:35

Even after seeing clear signs of his innocence, they still decided to imprison him for a period of time — likely to put an end to the public scandal and gossip surrounding the household.

This part of the story shows us that doing the right thing does not always lead to an easy outcome in this world. Yusuf (AS) chose patience and prayer over giving in to sin, even when it meant losing his freedom — trusting that Allah's plan was greater than his immediate circumstances.

chapters.title: Interpreting Dreams in Prison
chapters.content:
Inside the prison, Yusuf (AS) met two young men who would soon need his help.

وَدَخَلَ مَعَهُ ٱلسِّجْنَ فَتَيَانِ ۖ قَالَ أَحَدُهُمَآ إِنِّىٓ أَرَىٰنِىٓ أَعْصِرُ خَمْرًۭا ۖ وَقَالَ ٱلْءَاخَرُ إِنِّىٓ أَرَىٰنِىٓ أَحْمِلُ فَوْقَ رَأْسِى خُبْزًۭا تَأْكُلُ ٱلطَّيْرُ مِنْهُ ۖ نَبِّئْنَا بِتَأْوِيلِهِۦٓ ۖ إِنَّا نَرَىٰكَ مِنَ ٱلْمُحْسِنِينَ

"And there entered the prison with him two young men. One of them said, 'Indeed, I have seen myself [in a dream] pressing [grapes for] wine.' The other said, 'Indeed, I have seen myself carrying upon my head [some] bread, from which the birds were eating. Inform us of its interpretation; indeed, we see you to be of those who do good.'"

— Surah Yusuf 12:36

Two young men entered the prison along with Yusuf (AS). One of them dreamed of pressing grapes for wine, and the other dreamed of carrying bread on his head while birds ate from it. They both asked Yusuf (AS) to explain their dreams, since they could already see he was a man who did good.

Before answering, Yusuf (AS) used the moment to speak about something far greater than dreams.

قَالَ لَا يَأْتِيكُمَا طَعَامٌۭ تُرْزَقَانِهِۦٓ إِلَّا نَبَّأْتُكُمَا بِتَأْوِيلِهِۦ قَبْلَ أَن يَأْتِيَكُمَا ۚ ذَٰلِكُمَا مِمَّا عَلَّمَنِى رَبِّىٓ ۚ إِنِّى تَرَكْتُ مِلَّةَ قَوْمٍۢ لَّا يُؤْمِنُونَ بِٱللَّهِ وَهُم بِٱلْءَاخِرَةِ هُمْ كَٰفِرُونَ

"He said, 'You will not receive food that is provided to you except that I will inform you of its interpretation before it comes to you. That is from what my Lord has taught me. Indeed, I have left the religion of a people who do not believe in Allāh, and they, in the Hereafter, are disbelievers.'"

— Surah Yusuf 12:37

Yusuf (AS) told them that before their next meal even arrived, he would tell them the meaning of their dreams — a knowledge his Lord had taught him. He then mentioned that he had left behind the ways of people who did not believe in Allah and who denied the Hereafter.

وَٱتَّبَعْتُ مِلَّةَ ءَابَآءِىٓ إِبْرَٰهِيمَ وَإِسْحَٰقَ وَيَعْقُوبَ ۚ مَا كَانَ لَنَآ أَن نُّشْرِكَ بِٱللَّهِ مِن شَىْءٍۢ ۚ ذَٰلِكَ مِن فَضْلِ ٱللَّهِ عَلَيْنَا وَعَلَى ٱلنَّاسِ وَلَٰكِنَّ أَكْثَرَ ٱلنَّاسِ لَا يَشْكُرُونَ

"And I have followed the religion of my fathers, Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. And it was not for us to associate anything with Allāh. That is from the favor of Allāh upon us and upon the people, but most of the people are not grateful."

— Surah Yusuf 12:38

He said he followed the way of his forefathers — Ibrahim (AS), Ishaq (AS), and Ya'qub (AS) — and that it was never right for them to associate anything with Allah in worship. This was a favor from Allah upon them and upon all people, though most people remain ungrateful for it.

Yusuf (AS) then made a direct and powerful call to the truth.

يَٰصَىٰحِبَىِ ٱلسِّجْنِ ءَأَرْبَابٌۭ مُّتَفَرِّقُونَ خَيْرٌ أَمِ ٱللَّهُ ٱلْوَٰحِدُ ٱلْقَهَّارُ

"O [my] two companions of prison, are separate lords better or Allāh, the One, the Prevailing?"

— Surah Yusuf 12:39

He asked his two prison companions directly: which is better — many scattered lords, or Allah, the One, the All-Prevailing?

مَا تَعْبُدُونَ مِن دُونِهِۦٓ إِلَّآ أَسْمَآءًۭ سَمَّيْتُمُوهَآ أَنتُمْ وَءَابَآؤُكُم مَّآ أَنزَلَ ٱللَّهُ بِهَا مِن سُلْطَٰنٍ ۚ إِنِ ٱلْحُكْمُ إِلَّا لِلَّهِ ۚ أَمَرَ أَلَّا تَعْبُدُوٓا۟ إِلَّآ إِيَّاهُ ۚ ذَٰلِكَ ٱلدِّينُ ٱلْقَيِّمُ وَلَٰكِنَّ أَكْثَرَ ٱلنَّاسِ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ

"You worship not besides Him except [mere] names you have named them, you and your fathers, for which Allāh has sent down no evidence. Legislation is not but for Allāh. He has commanded that you worship not except Him. That is the correct religion, but most of the people do not know."

— Surah Yusuf 12:40

He explained that whatever they worshipped besides Allah were nothing but names they and their forefathers had invented, with no real authority sent down from Allah. All true authority belongs to Allah alone, and He has commanded that He alone be worshipped. This is the correct and straight religion, yet most people do not know it.

Then Yusuf (AS) gave them the interpretation they had been waiting for.

يَٰصَىٰحِبَىِ ٱلسِّجْنِ أَمَّآ أَحَدُكُمَا فَيَسْقِى رَبَّهُۥ خَمْرًۭا ۖ وَأَمَّا ٱلْءَاخَرُ فَيُصْلَبُ فَتَأْكُلُ ٱلطَّيْرُ مِن رَّأْسِهِۦ ۚ قُضِىَ ٱلْأَمْرُ ٱلَّذِى فِيهِ تَسْتَفْتِيَانِ

"O two companions of prison, as for one of you, he will give drink to his master of wine; but as for the other, he will be crucified, and the birds will eat from his head. The matter has been decreed about which you both inquire."

— Surah Yusuf 12:41

He told them that one of them would be released and return to serving his master wine, while the other would be executed, with birds eating from his head. This matter, he said, had already been decided by Allah.

As the man who would be freed left, Yusuf (AS) made a simple request — one that would not be honored right away.

وَقَالَ لِلَّذِى ظَنَّ أَنَّهُۥ نَاجٍۢ مِّنْهُمَا ٱذْكُرْنِى عِندَ رَبِّكَ فَأَنسَىٰهُ ٱلشَّيْطَٰنُ ذِكْرَ رَبِّهِۦ فَلَبِثَ فِى ٱلسِّجْنِ بِضْعَ سِنِينَ

"And he said to the one whom he knew would go free, 'Mention me before your master.' But Satan made him forget the mention [to] his master, and he [i.e., Joseph] remained in prison several years."

— Surah Yusuf 12:42

Yusuf (AS) asked the man who would be freed to mention him to his master. But Satan caused that man to forget, and as a result, Yusuf (AS) remained in prison for several more years.

Even in this delay, there is a lesson — Yusuf (AS)'s release would come, but only at the time Allah had already decreed, not a moment before.

chapters.title: The King's Dream and Yusuf's Release
chapters.content:
Years had passed since Yusuf (AS) interpreted the dreams of the two prisoners. Now, a dream troubled the king himself.

وَقَالَ ٱلْمَلِكُ إِنِّىٓ أَرَىٰ سَبْعَ بَقَرَٰتٍۢ سِمَانٍۢ يَأْكُلُهُنَّ سَبْعٌ عِجَافٌۭ وَسَبْعَ سُنۢبُلَٰتٍ خُضْرٍۢ وَأُخَرَ يَابِسَٰتٍۢ ۖ يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلْمَلَأُ أَفْتُونِى فِى رُءْيَٰىَ إِن كُنتُمْ لِلرُّءْيَا تَعْبُرُونَ

"And [subsequently] the king said, 'Indeed, I have seen [in a dream] seven fat cows being eaten by seven [that were] lean, and seven green spikes [of grain] and others [that were] dry. O eminent ones, explain to me my vision, if you should interpret visions.'"

— Surah Yusuf 12:43

The king described his dream to the people of his court: seven fat cows being eaten by seven thin cows, and seven green ears of grain alongside seven dry ones. He asked his advisors to explain the dream if they were able.

قَالُوٓا۟ أَضْغَٰثُ أَحْلَٰمٍۢ ۖ وَمَا نَحْنُ بِتَأْوِيلِ ٱلْأَحْلَٰمِ بِعَٰلِمِينَ

"They said, '[It is but] a mixture of false dreams, and we are not learned in the interpretation of dreams.'"

— Surah Yusuf 12:44

The advisors admitted they had no answer. They dismissed the dream as confused and meaningless, and confessed they had no real knowledge of dream interpretation.

This is when the man who had once been Yusuf (AS)'s prison companion finally remembered him.

وَقَالَ ٱلَّذِى نَجَا مِنْهُمَا وَٱدَّكَرَ بَعْدَ أُمَّةٍ أَنَا۠ أُنَبِّئُكُم بِتَأْوِيلِهِۦ فَأَرْسِلُونِ

"But the one who was freed and remembered after a time said, 'I will inform you of its interpretation, so send me forth.'"

— Surah Yusuf 12:45

The man who had once been freed from prison finally recalled Yusuf (AS), after a long delay. He told the king he could bring back the answer, and asked to be sent to find out.

He went to Yusuf (AS) and asked him directly.

يُوسُفُ أَيُّهَا ٱلصِّدِّيقُ أَفْتِنَا فِى سَبْعِ بَقَرَٰتٍۢ سِمَانٍۢ يَأْكُلُهُنَّ سَبْعٌ عِجَافٌۭ وَسَبْعِ سُنۢبُلَٰتٍ خُضْرٍۢ وَأُخَرَ يَابِسَٰتٍۢ لَّعَلِّىٓ أَرْجِعُ إِلَى ٱلنَّاسِ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَعْلَمُونَ

"[He said], 'Joseph, O man of truth, explain to us about seven fat cows eaten by seven [that were] lean, and seven green spikes [of grain] and others [that were] dry - that I may return to the people [i.e., the king and his court]; perhaps they will know [about you].'"

— Surah Yusuf 12:46

He addressed Yusuf (AS) as a man of truth, and asked him to explain the dream so he could bring the answer back, hoping the people would then come to recognize Yusuf (AS)'s worth.

Yusuf (AS) gave a full and detailed explanation of the dream's meaning.

قَالَ تَزْرَعُونَ سَبْعَ سِنِينَ دَأَبًۭا فَمَا حَصَدتُّمْ فَذَرُوهُ فِى سُنۢبُلِهِۦٓ إِلَّا قَلِيلًۭا مِّمَّا تَأْكُلُونَ

"[Joseph] said, 'You will plant for seven years consecutively; and what you harvest leave in its spikes, except a little from which you will eat.'"

— Surah Yusuf 12:47

Yusuf (AS) explained that there would be seven years of good harvest. He advised that whatever was harvested should be left in its grain husks for storage, except for a small amount kept aside for eating.

ثُمَّ يَأْتِى مِنۢ بَعْدِ ذَٰلِكَ سَبْعٌۭ شِدَادٌۭ يَأْكُلْنَ مَا قَدَّمْتُمْ لَهُنَّ إِلَّا قَلِيلًۭا مِّمَّا تُحْصِنُونَ

"Then will come after that seven difficult [years] which will consume what you advanced [i.e., saved] for them, except a little from which you will store."

— Surah Yusuf 12:48

After those seven good years, seven difficult years would follow, consuming whatever had been stored up, except for a small portion that would be kept safe.

ثُمَّ يَأْتِى مِنۢ بَعْدِ ذَٰلِكَ عَامٌۭ فِيهِ يُغَاثُ ٱلنَّاسُ وَفِيهِ يَعْصِرُونَ

"Then will come after that a year in which the people will be given rain and in which they will press [olives and grapes]."

— Surah Yusuf 12:49

After those difficult years, a year would come with abundant rain, and the people would once again be able to press olives and grapes in plenty.

This single explanation revealed not just Yusuf (AS)'s gift for understanding dreams, but his wisdom in planning ahead — knowledge that would soon prove vital for an entire nation.

chapters.title: Yusuf's Innocence Proven and His Rise to Honor
chapters.content:
With Yusuf (AS)'s interpretation of the dream now known, the king wished to meet him in person.

وَقَالَ ٱلْمَلِكُ ٱئْتُونِى بِهِۦ ۖ فَلَمَّا جَآءَهُ ٱلرَّسُولُ قَالَ ٱرْجِعْ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ فَسْـَٔلْهُ مَا بَالُ ٱلنِّسْوَةِ ٱلَّٰتِى قَطَّعْنَ أَيْدِيَهُنَّ ۚ إِنَّ رَبِّى بِكَيْدِهِنَّ عَلِيمٌۭ

"And the king said, 'Bring him to me.' But when the messenger came to him, [Joseph] said, 'Return to your master and ask him what is the case of the women who cut their hands. Indeed, my Lord is Knowing of their plan.'"

— Surah Yusuf 12:50

Even though the king summoned him directly, Yusuf (AS) did not rush out of prison to seek favor. Instead, he asked that the matter of the women — and the truth about his innocence — first be settled. He wanted his name cleared properly, not just his freedom granted quietly.

قَالَ مَا خَطْبُكُنَّ إِذْ رَٰوَدتُّنَّ يُوسُفَ عَن نَّفْسِهِۦ ۚ قُلْنَ حَٰشَ لِلَّهِ مَا عَلِمْنَا عَلَيْهِ مِن سُوٓءٍۢ ۚ قَالَتِ ٱمْرَأَتُ ٱلْعَزِيزِ ٱلْـَٰٔنَ حَصْحَصَ ٱلْحَقُّ أَنَا۠ رَٰوَدتُّهُۥ عَن نَّفْسِهِۦ وَإِنَّهُۥ لَمِنَ ٱلصَّٰدِقِينَ

"Said [the king to the women], 'What was your condition when you sought to seduce Joseph?' They said, 'Perfect is Allāh! We know about him no evil.' The wife of al-ʿAzeez said, 'Now the truth has become evident. It was I who sought to seduce him, and indeed, he is of the truthful.'"

— Surah Yusuf 12:51

The king questioned the women directly. They confirmed they knew nothing evil about Yusuf (AS). Then the wife of al-ʿAzeez herself confessed openly: it was she who had pursued him, and he had been truthful all along.

ذَٰلِكَ لِيَعْلَمَ أَنِّى لَمْ أَخُنْهُ بِٱلْغَيْبِ وَأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يَهْدِى كَيْدَ ٱلْخَآئِنِينَ

"That is so he [i.e., al-ʿAzeez] will know that I did not betray him in [his] absence and that Allāh does not guide the plan of betrayers."

— Surah Yusuf 12:52

She explained her confession was meant to prove that she had not deceived her husband behind his back, affirming that Allah does not let the schemes of betrayers succeed.
