"And said, 'Is it one human being among us that we should follow? Indeed, we would then be in error and madness.'"

— Surah Al-Qamar 54:24

They expressed their disbelief through arrogance, questioning why they should follow a single human being from among themselves, dismissing the very idea as leading to error and madness — failing to recognize that every prophet sent throughout history had come from among the people they were guiding.

أَءُلْقِىَ ٱلذِّكْرُ عَلَيْهِ مِنۢ بَيْنِنَا بَلْ هُوَ كَذَّابٌ أَشِرٌۭ

"Has the message been sent down upon him from among us? Rather, he is an insolent liar."

— Surah Al-Qamar 54:25

Their arrogance peaked as they questioned why divine revelation would single out Salih (AS) among them, rather than accepting the possibility, they dismissed him outright as an insolent liar.

سَيَعْلَمُونَ غَدًۭا مَّنِ ٱلْكَذَّابُ ٱلْأَشِرُ

"They will know tomorrow who is the insolent liar."

— Surah Al-Qamar 54:26

Allah responds directly to their accusation with a warning: soon, they would know with certainty who was truly the liar — and the answer would not be Salih (AS).

إِنَّا مُرْسِلُوا۟ ٱلنَّاقَةِ فِتْنَةًۭ لَّهُمْ فَٱرْتَقِبْهُمْ وَٱصْطَبِرْ

"Indeed, We are sending the she-camel as trial for them, so watch them and be patient."

— Surah Al-Qamar 54:27

Allah reveals the deeper purpose behind the she-camel: she was sent as a fitnah — a trial and test — to reveal the true state of their hearts. Salih (AS) was instructed to watch and remain patient as the test unfolded.

وَنَبِّئْهُمْ أَنَّ ٱلْمَآءَ قِسْمَةٌۢ بَيْنَهُمْ ۖ كُلُّ شِرْبٍۢ مُّحْتَضَرٌۭ

"And inform them that the water is shared between them, each [day of] drink attended [by turn]."

— Surah Al-Qamar 54:28

This verse adds an important detail: the water source was to be shared on a rotating basis — one day for the she-camel, another for the people — establishing a clear, fair system to test their patience and obedience.

فَنَادَوْا۟ صَاحِبَهُمْ فَتَعَاطَىٰ فَعَقَرَ

"But they called their companion, and he dared and hamstrung [her]."

— Surah Al-Qamar 54:29

The community called upon their companion — the most wretched among them, as mentioned in Surah Ash-Shams — and he stepped forward, daring to commit the act, and hamstrung the she-camel.

فَكَيْفَ كَانَ عَذَابِى وَنُذُرِ

"And how [severe] were My punishment and warning."

— Surah Al-Qamar 54:30

Allah poses a rhetorical question, inviting reflection on the severity of what followed — a punishment that matched the magnitude of their defiance.

إِنَّآ أَرْسَلْنَا عَلَيْهِمْ صَيْحَةًۭ وَٰحِدَةًۭ فَكَانُوا۟ كَهَشِيمِ ٱلْمُحْتَظِرِ

"Indeed, We sent upon them one shriek [i.e., blast from the sky], and they became like the dry twig fragments of an [animal] pen."

— Surah Al-Qamar 54:31

A single shriek was sufficient to destroy them entirely. The comparison is striking: they became like the dry, crumbled fragments of twigs found in an animal pen — withered, scattered, and utterly lifeless. The mighty builders of mountain homes were reduced to nothing in an instant.

وَلَقَدْ يَسَّرْنَا ٱلْقُرْءَانَ لِلذِّكْرِ فَهَلْ مِن مُّدَّكِرٍۢ

"And We have certainly made the Qur'ān easy for remembrance, so is there any who will remember?"

— Surah Al-Qamar 54:32

The chapter closes with a direct invitation to every reader, in every era: Allah has made the Quran easy to understand and remember. The story of Thamud is not merely ancient history — it is a living reminder, asking each of us whether we will take heed of the lessons within it. The fate of those who reject divine guidance, no matter how skilled or powerful they may be, remains a timeless warning for all who reflect.

title: The Story of Ismail (AS) — Dhabihullah — The one offered in sacrifice
summary: The story of Ismail (AS), son of Ibrahim, known for his truthfulness, his patience in the trial of sacrifice, and his role in building the Ka'bah.

chapters.title: Truthful to His Promise
chapters.content:
Before the Quran tells us about the great trial Ismail (AS) faced, or his role in building the Ka'bah, it first wants us to know exactly who he was. A short set of verses describes his character directly — and what they reveal sets the tone for everything that follows.

وَٱذْكُرْ فِى ٱلْكِتَٰبِ إِسْمَٰعِيلَ ۚ إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ صَادِقَ ٱلْوَعْدِ وَكَانَ رَسُولًۭا نَّبِيًّۭا

"And mention in the Book, Ishmael. Indeed, he was true to his promise, and he was a messenger and a prophet."

— Surah Maryam 19:54

Allah's first description of Ismail (AS) is that he was true to his promise. Whatever he committed to, he carried out — no matter how difficult it became. This single quality becomes especially significant later, when his promise is tested in the most extreme way possible. Alongside this, Allah confirms that Ismail (AS) held his own rank as a messenger and a prophet, continuing the same call to worship Allah alone that his father Ibrahim (AS) carried.

وَكَانَ يَأْمُرُ أَهْلَهُۥ بِٱلصَّلَوٰةِ وَٱلزَّكَوٰةِ وَكَانَ عِندَ رَبِّهِۦ مَرْضِيًّۭا

"And he used to enjoin on his people prayer and zakāh and was to his Lord pleasing [i.e., accepted by Him]."

— Surah Maryam 19:55

Ismail's (AS) faith was not kept to himself. He actively commanded his own family to establish prayer and give zakah, taking responsibility for the spiritual wellbeing of those around him. Because of this sincerity, Allah describes him as pleasing to his Lord.

وَإِسْمَٰعِيلَ وَإِدْرِيسَ وَذَا ٱلْكِفْلِ ۖ كُلٌّۭ مِّنَ ٱلصَّٰبِرِينَ

"And [mention] Ishmael and Idrees and Dhul-Kifl; all were of the patient."

— Surah Al-Anbiya 21:85

Here, Ismail (AS) is named alongside Idris (AS) and Dhul-Kifl (AS), united by one shared quality: patience. Patience runs through every stage of his life — as a child prepared for sacrifice, growing up apart from his mother's homeland, and standing beside his elderly father to raise the walls of the Ka'bah.

وَأَدْخَلْنَٰهُمْ فِى رَحْمَتِنَآ ۖ إِنَّهُم مِّنَ ٱلصَّٰلِحِينَ

"And We admitted them into Our mercy. Indeed, they were of the righteous."

— Surah Al-Anbiya 21:86

The description closes on the highest outcome possible: entry into Allah's mercy, granted because of their righteousness. Truthful, devoted to his family's faith, patient, and righteous — this is who Ismail (AS) was before we ever reach the trial that would define his legacy.

chapters.title: The Trial of the Vision
chapters.content:
Years after the glad tidings of his birth, Ismail (AS) grew into a young boy old enough to walk and work alongside his father. It was at this stage of his life — old enough to understand, old enough to choose — that Allah tested both father and son with a trial unlike any other.

فَبَشَّرْنَٰهُ بِغُلَٰمٍ حَلِيمٍۢ

"So We gave him good tidings of a forbearing boy."

— Surah As-Saffat 37:101

Before the trial itself, Allah describes Ismail (AS) with a single word that foreshadows everything to come: ḥalīm — forbearing, even-tempered, able to bear hardship without complaint. This was not a description given by chance. It was the very quality that would carry him through what was about to happen.

فَلَمَّا بَلَغَ مَعَهُ ٱلسَّعْىَ قَالَ يَٰبُنَىَّ إِنِّىٓ أَرَىٰ فِى ٱلْمَنَامِ أَنِّىٓ أَذْبَحُكَ فَٱنظُرْ مَاذَا تَرَىٰ ۚ قَالَ يَٰٓأَبَتِ ٱفْعَلْ مَا تُؤْمَرُ ۖ سَتَجِدُنِىٓ إِن شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ مِنَ ٱلصَّٰبِرِينَ

"And when he reached with him [the age of] exertion, he said, 'O my son, indeed I have seen in a dream that I [must] sacrifice you, so see what you think.' He said, 'O my father, do as you are commanded. You will find me, if Allāh wills, of the steadfast.'"

— Surah As-Saffat 37:102

Ibrahim (AS) did not hide the vision from his son or act on it without telling him. He shared it openly, asking Ismail (AS) for his own view. And Ismail's (AS) answer is one of the most remarkable responses recorded in the Quran. He did not hesitate, argue, or ask for proof. He simply said: do as you are commanded. He went further, promising his father that he would be found among the steadfast — and even in that promise, he placed the outcome in Allah's hands, saying "if Allah wills." This is the moment that fulfills what was said about him earlier in Surah Maryam: that he was true to his promise. Here, at the hardest possible moment, his word matched his character exactly.

فَلَمَّآ أَسْلَمَا وَتَلَّهُۥ لِلْجَبِينِ

"And when they had both submitted and he put him down upon his forehead,"

— Surah As-Saffat 37:103

This verse captures something easy to miss: it says "when they had both submitted" — not only Ibrahim (AS), but Ismail (AS) too. This was not a father forcing his son into something. It was two people, father and son, each individually surrendering their will to Allah's command.

وَنَٰدَيْنَٰهُ أَن يَٰٓإِبْرَٰهِيمُ

"We called to him, 'O Abraham,'"

— Surah As-Saffat 37:104

Then Allah's answer came immediately.

قَدْ صَدَّقْتَ ٱلرُّءْيَآ ۚ إِنَّا كَذَٰلِكَ نَجْزِى ٱلْمُحْسِنِينَ

"You have fulfilled the vision." Indeed, We thus reward the doers of good."

— Surah As-Saffat 37:105

At the very last moment, Allah's call came. The vision had already been fulfilled — not because the act was physically completed, but because both father and son had already submitted their hearts to it completely. Allah accepted their intention and obedience as the fulfillment itself.

إِنَّ هَٰذَا لَهُوَ ٱلْبَلَٰٓؤُا۟ ٱلْمُبِينُ

"Indeed, this was the clear trial."

— Surah As-Saffat 37:106

Allah names it directly: this was a clear, unmistakable trial — one designed to test the limits of submission for both father and son.

وَفَدَيْنَٰهُ بِذِبْحٍ عَظِيمٍۢ

"And We ransomed him with a great sacrifice,"

— Surah As-Saffat 37:107

In place of Ismail (AS), Allah provided a great sacrifice instead. His life was spared, and what he had been willing to give was accepted as if it had been given.

وَتَرَكْنَا عَلَيْهِ فِى ٱلْءَاخِرِينَ

"And We left for him [favorable mention] among later generations:"

— Surah As-Saffat 37:108

This trial did not end with that generation. Allah preserved its memory among every generation that followed — which is why, to this day, Muslims around the world commemorate this very submission each year during Eid al-Adha. Ismail's (AS) single sentence — "do as you are commanded" — remains one of the clearest examples of trust in Allah ever recorded.

chapters.title: A Son Beside His Father
chapters.content:
After the trial of the sacrifice, father and son were not separated by what had happened — they were drawn closer together. The same obedience that Ismail (AS) showed on the day of the vision now continued in a different form: building the most sacred house on earth, side by side, with their own hands.

وَإِذْ جَعَلْنَا ٱلْبَيْتَ مَثَابَةًۭ لِّلنَّاسِ وَأَمْنًۭا وَٱتَّخِذُوا۟ مِن مَّقَامِ إِبْرَٰهِۦمَ مُصَلًّۭى ۖ وَعَهِدْنَآ إِلَىٰٓ إِبْرَٰهِۦمَ وَإِسْمَٰعِيلَ أَن طَهِّرَا بَيْتِىَ لِلطَّآئِفِينَ وَٱلْعَٰكِفِينَ وَٱلرُّكَّعِ ٱلسُّجُودِ

"And [mention] when We made the House [i.e., the Kaʿbah] a place of return for the people and [a place of] security. And take, [O believers], from the standing place of Abraham a place of prayer. And We charged Abraham and Ishmael, [saying], 'Purify My House for those who perform ṭawāf and those who are staying [there] for worship and those who bow and prostrate [in prayer].'"

— Surah Al-Baqarah 2:125

Allah describes the Ka'bah as a mathābah — a place people return to, again and again, from every corner of the earth. It is also a place of aman, meaning safety and security. Allah then tells us that both Ibrahim (AS) and Ismail (AS) were given a specific command together: purify My House. Not just build it, but keep it pure — for those doing tawaf (circling it), for those staying there in worship, and for those praying. This was not simply a construction task. It was an act of sacred service that both father and son were responsible for equally.

وَإِذْ قَالَ إِبْرَٰهِۦمُ رَبِّ ٱجْعَلْ هَٰذَا بَلَدًا ءَامِنًۭا وَٱرْزُقْ أَهْلَهُۥ مِنَ ٱلثَّمَرَٰتِ مَنْ ءَامَنَ مِنْهُم بِٱللَّهِ وَٱلْيَوْمِ ٱلْءَاخِرِ ۖ قَالَ وَمَن كَفَرَ فَأُمَتِّعُهُۥ قَلِيلًۭا ثُمَّ أَضْطَرُّهُۥٓ إِلَىٰ عَذَابِ ٱلنَّارِ ۖ وَبِئْسَ ٱلْمَصِيرُ

"And [mention] when Abraham said, 'My Lord, make this a secure city and provide its people with fruits - whoever of them believes in Allāh and the Last Day.' [Allāh] said, 'And whoever disbelieves - I will grant him enjoyment for a little; then I will force him to the punishment of the Fire, and wretched is the destination.'"

— Surah Al-Baqarah 2:126

Ibrahim (AS) made dua for the city itself and for the people who would live in it. He asked for safety and for provision — fruits in a valley that had no farmland, no river, and no natural reason to thrive. This was the same trust in Allah that led him to leave his infant son and wife in that barren land years earlier. Now, with the House being built, he asked Allah to bless it for all who believed. Allah accepted his dua and answered it — but He also clarified that even those who disbelieve would be given provision for a time, before facing their consequence. No dua of a sincere prophet goes without a response.

وَإِذْ يَرْفَعُ إِبْرَٰهِۦمُ ٱلْقَوَاعِدَ مِنَ ٱلْبَيْتِ وَإِسْمَٰعِيلُ رَبَّنَا تَقَبَّلْ مِنَّآ ۖ إِنَّكَ أَنتَ ٱلسَّمِيعُ ٱلْعَلِيمُ

"And [mention] when Abraham was raising the foundations of the House and [with him] Ishmael, [saying], 'Our Lord, accept [this] from us. Indeed, You are the Hearing, the Knowing.'"

— Surah Al-Baqarah 2:127

This single verse holds an image that is hard to fully grasp: a prophet and his son, lifting stones with their hands to build the House of Allah, and while doing so, making dua that Allah would simply accept it from them. Two people performing one of the greatest acts in human history, and their concern in that moment is not whether the walls are straight — it is whether Allah will accept what they are doing. This is what sincere worship looks like. The work and the dua happen at the same time.

رَبَّنَا وَٱجْعَلْنَا مُسْلِمَيْنِ لَكَ وَمِن ذُرِّيَّتِنَآ أُمَّةًۭ مُّسْلِمَةًۭ لَّكَ وَأَرِنَا مَنَاسِكَنَا وَتُبْ عَلَيْنَآ ۖ إِنَّكَ أَنتَ ٱلتَّوَّابُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ

"Our Lord, and make us Muslims [in submission] to You and from our descendants a Muslim nation [in submission] to You. And show us our rites [of worship] and accept our repentance. Indeed, You are the Accepting of Repentance, the Merciful."

— Surah Al-Baqarah 2:128

Their dua then expanded beyond themselves. They asked Allah not just to keep them in submission, but to raise from their descendants an entire nation that submits to Allah. They also asked Allah to show them the correct rites of worship — meaning they were humble enough to ask for guidance even while performing the act of building His House. And they closed by asking for repentance to be accepted, because even the closest servants of Allah never consider themselves beyond the need for Allah's forgiveness and mercy.

رَبَّنَا وَٱبْعَثْ فِيهِمْ رَسُولًۭا مِّنْهُمْ يَتْلُوا۟ عَلَيْهِمْ ءَايَٰتِكَ وَيُعَلِّمُهُمُ ٱلْكِتَٰبَ وَٱلْحِكْمَةَ وَيُزَكِّيهِمْ ۚ إِنَّكَ أَنتَ ٱلْعَزِيزُ ٱلْحَكِيمُ

"Our Lord, and send among them a messenger from themselves who will recite to them Your verses and teach them the Book and wisdom and purify them. Indeed, You are the Exalted in Might, the Wise."

— Surah Al-Baqarah 2:129

The final dua is the one that connects Ismail (AS) to every Muslim alive today. While their hands were still on the stones of the Ka'bah, Ibrahim (AS) and Ismail (AS) asked Allah to send a messenger from among those very descendants — one who would recite Allah's verses to them, teach them the Book and wisdom, and purify them. Thousands of years later, that dua was answered in the form of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, who was born in the very city they were building for, from the very lineage of Ismail (AS). Every time we hear the Quran recited, every time we learn from it, we are witnessing the acceptance of a dua made by two prophets with stones in their hands.

title: The Story of Ishaq (AS) — A Righteous Prophet
subject: Ishaq
summary: The story of Ishaq (AS), son of Ibrahim, whose birth was announced by angels as a miracle, and who was raised among the righteous line of prophets.

chapters.title: The Good News of His Birth
chapters.content:
One day, some guests came to visit Ibrahim (AS). They were not ordinary guests — they were angels sent by Allah. Ibrahim (AS) did not know this at first.

وَلَقَدْ جَآءَتْ رُسُلُنَآ إِبْرَٰهِيمَ بِٱلْبُشْرَىٰ قَالُوا۟ سَلَٰمًۭا ۖ قَالَ سَلَٰمٌۭ ۖ فَمَا لَبِثَ أَن جَآءَ بِعِجْلٍ حَنِيذٍۢ

"And certainly did Our messengers [i.e., angels] come to Abraham with good tidings; they said, 'Peace.' He said, 'Peace,' and did not delay in bringing [them] a roasted calf."

— Surah Hud 11:69

The angels greeted Ibrahim (AS) with "Peace," and he greeted them back the same way. Being a generous host, he quickly brought them food — a roasted calf — without even asking who they were first.

فَلَمَّا رَءَآ أَيْدِيَهُمْ لَا تَصِلُ إِلَيْهِ نَكِرَهُمْ وَأَوْجَسَ مِنْهُمْ خِيفَةًۭ ۚ قَالُوا۟ لَا تَخَفْ إِنَّآ أُرْسِلْنَآ إِلَىٰ قَوْمِ لُوطٍۢ

"But when he saw their hands not reaching for it, he distrusted them and felt from them apprehension. They said, 'Fear not. We have been sent to the people of Lot.'"

— Surah Hud 11:70

Ibrahim (AS) noticed something strange — his guests did not eat the food. In his time, a guest who refused to eat could mean danger. So he became afraid. But then the guests told him the truth: they were angels, sent by Allah on a mission to the people of Lut (AS). This calmed his fear.

وَٱمْرَأَتُهُۥ قَآئِمَةٌۭ فَضَحِكَتْ فَبَشَّرْنَٰهَا بِإِسْحَٰقَ وَمِن وَرَآءِ إِسْحَٰقَ يَعْقُوبَ

"And his wife was standing, and she smiled. Then We gave her good tidings of Isaac and after Isaac, Jacob."

— Surah Hud 11:71

Ibrahim's (AS) wife was standing nearby and heard this. Right then, Allah gave her wonderful news: she would have a son named Ishaq (AS). And Allah gave her even more news — after Ishaq (AS), she would also have a grandson, Ya'qub (AS). This was a double blessing, two generations announced at once.

قَالَتْ يَٰوَيْلَتَىٰٓ ءَأَلِدُ وَأَنَا۠ عَجُوزٌۭ وَهَٰذَا بَعْلِى شَيْخًا ۖ إِنَّ هَٰذَا لَشَىْءٌ عَجِيبٌۭ

"She said, 'Woe to me! Shall I give birth while I am an old woman and this, my husband, is an old man? Indeed, this is an amazing thing!'"

— Surah Hud 11:72

This news surprised her deeply. She was old, and her husband was old too. Having a baby at that age seemed impossible by normal means. Her surprise was natural and honest — she said it out loud instead of hiding it.

قَالُوٓا۟ أَتَعْجَبِينَ مِنْ أَمْرِ ٱللَّهِ ۖ رَحْمَتُ ٱللَّهِ وَبَرَكَٰتُهُۥ عَلَيْكُمْ أَهْلَ ٱلْبَيْتِ ۚ إِنَّهُۥ حَمِيدٌۭ مَّجِيدٌۭ

"They said, 'Are you amazed at the decree of Allāh? May the mercy of Allāh and His blessings be upon you, people of the house. Indeed, He is Praiseworthy and Honorable.'"

— Surah Hud 11:73

The angels gently reminded her: nothing is impossible for Allah. What seems impossible to us is easy for Him. Then they gave her a beautiful dua — that Allah's mercy and blessings be upon her household. This teaches us something simple but powerful: age, biology, or any human limit is never a limit for Allah. If He decides something will happen, it happens.

chapters.title: A Righteous Legacy
chapters.content:
Ishaq (AS) was not only given as a son of glad tidings — Allah also honored him with a special status among the prophets, a legacy that carried forward through generations.

وَوَهَبْنَا لَهُۥٓ إِسْحَٰقَ وَيَعْقُوبَ نَافِلَةًۭ ۖ وَكُلًّۭا جَعَلْنَا صَٰلِحِينَ

And We gave him Isaac and Jacob in addition, and all [of them] We made righteous.

— Surah Al-Anbiya 21:72

Allah describes Ishaq (AS) and his son Yaqub (AS) as an extra gift to Ibrahim (AS), and both of them were made righteous — people whose hearts and actions were pleasing to Allah.

وَجَعَلْنَٰهُمْ أَئِمَّةًۭ يَهْدُونَ بِأَمْرِنَا وَأَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَيْهِمْ فِعْلَ ٱلْخَيْرَٰتِ وَإِقَامَ ٱلصَّلَوٰةِ وَإِيتَآءَ ٱلزَّكَوٰةِ ۖ وَكَانُوا۟ لَنَا عَٰبِدِينَ

And We made them leaders guiding by Our command. And We inspired to them the doing of good deeds, establishment of prayer, and giving of zakāh; and they were worshippers of Us.

— Surah Al-Anbiya 21:73

Allah gave them the role of imams — leaders who guide others toward good. They were inspired to do good deeds, to establish prayer, and to give zakah. Above all, they remained sincere worshippers of Allah alone.

وَبَشَّرْنَٰهُ بِإِسْحَٰقَ نَبِيًّۭا مِّنَ ٱلصَّٰلِحِينَ

And We gave him good tidings of Isaac, a prophet from among the righteous.

— Surah As-Saffat 37:112

Here Allah confirms directly: Ishaq (AS) himself became a prophet, one from among the righteous.

وَبَٰرَكْنَا عَلَيْهِ وَعَلَىٰٓ إِسْحَٰقَ ۚ وَمِن ذُرِّيَّتِهِمَا مُحْسِنٌۭ وَظَالِمٌۭ لِّنَفْسِهِۦ مُبِينٌۭ

And We blessed him and Isaac. But among their descendants is the doer of good and the clearly unjust to himself [i.e., sinner].

— Surah As-Saffat 37:113

Allah blessed both Ibrahim (AS) and Ishaq (AS). But this verse also teaches an honest lesson: not every descendant of a prophet automatically follows the right path. Among their children came both good, righteous people, and some who wronged themselves through sin. Being from a blessed family does not guarantee guidance — each person is judged by their own choices.

وَوَهَبْنَا لَهُۥٓ إِسْحَٰقَ وَيَعْقُوبَ ۚ كُلًّا هَدَيْنَا ۚ وَنُوحًا هَدَيْنَا مِن قَبْلُ ۖ وَمِن ذُرِّيَّتِهِۦ دَاوُۥدَ وَسُلَيْمَٰنَ وَأَيُّوبَ وَيُوسُفَ وَمُوسَىٰ وَهَٰرُونَ ۚ وَكَذَٰلِكَ نَجْزِى ٱلْمُحْسِنِينَ

And We gave to him [i.e., Abraham] Isaac and Jacob - all [of them] We guided. And Noah, We guided before; and among his descendants, David and Solomon and Job and Joseph and Moses and Aaron. Thus do We reward the doers of good.

— Surah Al-An'am 6:84

This verse shows the bigger picture: Ishaq (AS) is one link in a long chain of guided prophets, starting with Nuh (AS) before him, and continuing after him through Dawud (AS), Sulaiman (AS), Ayyub (AS), Yusuf (AS), Musa (AS), and Harun (AS). Ishaq's (AS) legacy was not just his own righteousness, but being part of the family through which Allah sent prophet after prophet to guide humanity. This is how Allah rewards those who do good — with an honored place and a lasting legacy.

title: The Story of Lut (AS) — Prophet to the People of Sodom
subject: Lut
summary: The story of Prophet Lut (AS), sent to warn his people against immorality, and his rescue on the night his city was destroyed for their persistent sin.

chapters.title: A Warner to a Corrupt People
chapters.content:
Lut (AS) was sent by Allah to a people who had fallen into a sin that no nation before them had ever committed.

وَلُوطًا إِذْ قَالَ لِقَوْمِهِۦٓ أَتَأْتُونَ ٱلْفَٰحِشَةَ مَا سَبَقَكُم بِهَا مِنْ أَحَدٍۢ مِّنَ ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ

And [We had sent] Lot when he said to his people, "Do you commit such immorality as no one has preceded you with from among the worlds [i.e., peoples]?

— Surah Al-A'raf 7:80

Lut (AS) confronted his people directly, naming the sin they had normalized among themselves — something entirely new to human history at that time.

إِنَّكُمْ لَتَأْتُونَ ٱلرِّجَالَ شَهْوَةًۭ مِّن دُونِ ٱلنِّسَآءِ ۚ بَلْ أَنتُمْ قَوْمٌۭ مُّسْرِفُونَ

Indeed, you approach men with desire, instead of women. Rather, you are a transgressing people."

— Surah Al-A'raf 7:81

His people did not respond to his warning with reflection. Instead, they responded with rejection and hostility.

وَمَا كَانَ جَوَابَ قَوْمِهِۦٓ إِلَّآ أَن قَالُوٓا۟ أَخْرِجُوهُم مِّن قَرْيَتِكُمْ ۖ إِنَّهُمْ أُنَاسٌۭ يَتَطَهَّرُونَ

But the answer of his people was only that they said, "Evict them from your city! Indeed, they are men who keep themselves pure."

— Surah Al-A'raf 7:82

Astonishingly, they mocked Lut (AS) and his followers for wanting to stay pure, treating righteousness itself as something strange and unwelcome. The same warning is repeated in Surah Ash-Shu'ara, where Lut (AS) reminds them he asks for nothing in return — only that they fear Allah.

كَذَّبَتْ قَوْمُ لُوطٍ ٱلْمُرْسَلِينَ

The people of Lot denied the messengers

— Surah Ash-Shu'ara 26:160

Their own brother came to warn them.

إِذْ قَالَ لَهُمْ أَخُوهُمْ لُوطٌ أَلَا تَتَّقُونَ

When their brother Lot said to them, "Will you not fear Allāh?

— Surah Ash-Shu'ara 26:161

He introduced himself as one they could trust.

إِنِّى لَكُمْ رَسُولٌ أَمِينٌۭ

Indeed, I am to you a trustworthy messenger.

— Surah Ash-Shu'ara 26:162

He called them to the same message every messenger brought.

فَٱتَّقُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ وَأَطِيعُونِ

So fear Allāh and obey me.

— Surah Ash-Shu'ara 26:163

He made clear he sought nothing from them in return.

وَمَآ أَسْـَٔلُكُمْ عَلَيْهِ مِنْ أَجْرٍ ۖ إِنْ أَجْرِىَ إِلَّا عَلَىٰ رَبِّ ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ

And I do not ask you for it any payment. My payment is only from the Lord of the worlds.

— Surah Ash-Shu'ara 26:164

Then he named their sin plainly once more, and pointed out the natural alternative Allah had created for them.

أَتَأْتُونَ ٱلذُّكْرَانَ مِنَ ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ

Do you approach males among the worlds

— Surah Ash-Shu'ara 26:165

He pointed out exactly what they were turning away from.

وَتَذَرُونَ مَا خَلَقَ لَكُمْ رَبُّكُم مِّنْ أَزْوَٰجِكُم ۚ بَلْ أَنتُمْ قَوْمٌ عَادُونَ

And leave what your Lord has created for you as mates? But you are a people transgressing."

— Surah Ash-Shu'ara 26:166

Their response was a direct threat — they told him to stop or face expulsion from the city.

قَالُوا۟ لَئِن لَّمْ تَنتَهِ يَٰلُوطُ لَتَكُونَنَّ مِنَ ٱلْمُخْرَجِينَ

They said, "If you do not desist, O Lot, you will surely be of those evicted."

— Surah Ash-Shu'ara 26:167

Lut (AS) responded without wavering.

قَالَ إِنِّى لِعَمَلِكُم مِّنَ ٱلْقَالِينَ

He said, "Indeed, I am, toward your deed, of those who detest [it].

— Surah Ash-Shu'ara 26:168

Despite every threat, Lut (AS) did not compromise his message. He made his stance completely clear: he detested what they were doing and would never accept it, no matter the cost to himself. His firmness in the face of rejection set the stage for what would happen next.

chapters.title: The Night of Rescue
chapters.content:
Yaqub's (AS) story with his son Yusuf begins with a dream — one that carries meaning far beyond what a father could imagine at the time.

Before the angels reached Lut (AS), they had first visited Ibrahim (AS) with the news of what they were about to do.

وَلَمَّا جَآءَتْ رُسُلُنَآ إِبْرَٰهِيمَ بِٱلْبُشْرَىٰ قَالُوٓا۟ إِنَّا مُهْلِكُوٓا۟ أَهْلِ هَٰذِهِ ٱلْقَرْيَةِ ۖ إِنَّ أَهْلَهَا كَانُوا۟ ظَٰلِمِينَ

And when Our messengers [i.e., angels] came to Abraham with the good tidings, they said, "Indeed, we will destroy the people of that [i.e., Lot's] city. Indeed, its people have been wrongdoers."

— Surah Al-Ankabut 29:31

Ibrahim (AS) was concerned for Lut (AS), who lived among that city. The angels reassured him that Lut and his family would be saved, except his wife.

قَالَ إِنَّ فِيهَا لُوطًۭا ۚ قَالُوا۟ نَحْنُ أَعْلَمُ بِمَن فِيهَا ۖ لَنُنَجِّيَنَّهُۥ وَأَهْلَهُۥٓ إِلَّا ٱمْرَأَتَهُۥ كَانَتْ مِنَ ٱلْغَٰبِرِينَ

[Abraham] said, "Indeed, within it is Lot." They said, "We are more knowing of who is within it. We will surely save him and his family, except his wife. She is to be of those who remain behind."

— Surah Al-Ankabut 29:32

The angels then arrived at Lut's (AS) home, appearing as guests. Not knowing they were angels, Lut (AS) felt deep anguish — he feared for their safety among his people.

وَلَمَّا جَآءَتْ رُسُلُنَا لُوطًۭا سِىٓءَ بِهِمْ وَضَاقَ بِهِمْ ذَرْعًۭا وَقَالَ هَٰذَا يَوْمٌ عَصِيبٌۭ

And when Our messengers, [the angels], came to Lot, he was anguished for them and felt for them great discomfort and said, "This is a trying day."

— Surah Hud 11:77

His fear was justified. His people, who had a long history of this evil behavior, rushed toward his house upon hearing about the guests.

وَجَآءَهُۥ قَوْمُهُۥ يُهْرَعُونَ إِلَيْهِ وَمِن قَبْلُ كَانُوا۟ يَعْمَلُونَ ٱلسَّيِّـَٔاتِ ۚ قَالَ يَٰقَوْمِ هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ بَنَاتِى هُنَّ أَطْهَرُ لَكُمْ ۖ فَٱتَّقُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ وَلَا تُخْزُونِ فِى ضَيْفِىٓ ۖ أَلَيْسَ مِنكُمْ رَجُلٌۭ رَّشِيدٌۭ

And his people came hastening to him, and before [this] they had been doing evil deeds. He said, "O my people, these are my daughters; they are purer for you. So fear Allāh and do not disgrace me concerning my guests. Is there not among you a man of reason?"

— Surah Hud 11:78

Lut (AS), desperate to protect his guests and uphold what was right, offered his daughters in marriage as the lawful alternative — but his people made their true intention unmistakably clear.

قَالُوا۟ لَقَدْ عَلِمْتَ مَا لَنَا فِى بَنَاتِكَ مِنْ حَقٍّۢ وَإِنَّكَ لَتَعْلَمُ مَا نُرِيدُ

They said, "You have already known that we have not concerning your daughters [i.e., women] any claim [i.e., desire], and indeed, you know what we want."

— Surah Hud 11:79

Feeling helpless against the mob and having no strong support to turn to, Lut (AS) expressed his distress.

قَالَ لَوْ أَنَّ لِى بِكُمْ قُوَّةً أَوْ ءَاوِىٓ إِلَىٰ رُكْنٍۢ شَدِيدٍۢ

He said, "If only I had against you some power or could take refuge in a strong support."

— Surah Hud 11:80

At this critical moment, the guests revealed the truth — they were not ordinary men, but angels sent by Allah. They comforted him and gave him urgent instructions.

قَالُوا۟ يَٰلُوطُ إِنَّا رُسُلُ رَبِّكَ لَن يَصِلُوٓا۟ إِلَيْكَ ۖ فَأَسْرِ بِأَهْلِكَ بِقِطْعٍۢ مِّنَ ٱلَّيْلِ وَلَا يَلْتَفِتْ مِنكُمْ أَحَدٌ إِلَّا ٱمْرَأَتَكَ ۖ إِنَّهُۥ مُصِيبُهَا مَآ أَصَابَهُمْ ۚ إِنَّ مَوْعِدَهُمُ ٱلصُّبْحُ ۚ أَلَيْسَ ٱلصُّبْحُ بِقَرِيبٍۢ

They [the angels] said, "O Lot, indeed we are messengers of your Lord; [therefore], they will never reach you. So set out with your family during a portion of the night and let not any among you look back - except your wife; indeed, she will be struck by that which strikes them. Indeed, their appointment is [for] the morning. Is not the morning near?"

— Surah Hud 11:81

The same instruction is confirmed in Surah Al-Ankabut, where the angels comfort Lut (AS) directly, telling him not to fear or grieve.

وَلَمَّآ أَن جَآءَتْ رُسُلُنَا لُوطًۭا سِىٓءَ بِهِمْ وَضَاقَ بِهِمْ ذَرْعًۭا وَقَالُوا۟ لَا تَخَفْ وَلَا تَحْزَنْ ۖ إِنَّا مُنَجُّوكَ وَأَهْلَكَ إِلَّا ٱمْرَأَتَكَ كَانَتْ مِنَ ٱلْغَٰبِرِينَ

And when Our messengers [i.e., angels] came to Lot, he was distressed for them and felt for them great discomfort. They said, "Fear not, nor grieve. Indeed, we will save you and your family, except your wife; she is to be of those who remain behind.

— Surah Al-Ankabut 29:33

Lut's (AS) wife had secretly sided with the disbelieving people rather than supporting her husband's message — and so she was not included among those saved. This night marked the turning point: Lut (AS) and his true family quietly left the city under cover of darkness, just before the punishment arrived at dawn.

chapters.title: The Punishment and the Sign
chapters.content:
The brothers' jealousy of Yusuf grows into a plan that will bring years of sorrow to their father.

Before the punishment arrived, Lut (AS) turned to Allah with a heartfelt prayer, asking to be saved from his people's corruption.

رَبِّ نَجِّنِى وَأَهْلِى مِمَّا يَعْمَلُونَ

My Lord, save me and my family from [the consequence of] what they do."

— Surah Ash-Shu'ara 26:169

Allah answered his prayer and saved him and his family, with one exception.

فَنَجَّيْنَٰهُ وَأَهْلَهُۥٓ أَجْمَعِينَ

So We saved him and his family, all,

— Surah Ash-Shu'ara 26:170

Only one person was left behind.

إِلَّا عَجُوزًۭا فِى ٱلْغَٰبِرِينَ

Except an old woman among those who remained behind.

— Surah Ash-Shu'ara 26:171

Then the punishment fell on the rest of the people — the city was destroyed completely.

ثُمَّ دَمَّرْنَا ٱلْءَاخَرِينَ

Then We destroyed the others.

— Surah Ash-Shu'ara 26:172

Their end came suddenly.

وَأَمْطَرْنَا عَلَيْهِم مَّطَرًۭا ۖ فَسَآءَ مَطَرُ ٱلْمُنذَرِينَ

And We rained upon them a rain [of stones], and evil was the rain of those who were warned.

— Surah Ash-Shu'ara 26:173

The same event is described in Surah Al-A'raf, describing the totality of their end.

فَأَنجَيْنَٰهُ وَأَهْلَهُۥٓ إِلَّا ٱمْرَأَتَهُۥ كَانَتْ مِنَ ٱلْغَٰبِرِينَ

So We saved him and his family, except for his wife; she was of those who remained [with the evildoers].

— Surah Al-A'raf 7:83

The result of their punishment was total.

وَأَمْطَرْنَا عَلَيْهِم مَّطَرًۭا ۖ فَٱنظُرْ كَيْفَ كَانَ عَٰقِبَةُ ٱلْمُجْرِمِينَ

And We rained upon them a rain [of stones]. Then see how was the end of the criminals.

— Surah Al-A'raf 7:84

Surah Hud describes the exact nature of the destruction — the city was overturned, flipped upside down.

فَلَمَّا جَآءَ أَمْرُنَا جَعَلْنَا عَٰلِيَهَا سَافِلَهَا وَأَمْطَرْنَا عَلَيْهَا حِجَارَةًۭ مِّن سِجِّيلٍۢ مَّنضُودٍۢ

So when Our command came, We made the highest part [of the city] its lowest and rained upon them stones of layered hard clay, [which were]

— Surah Hud 11:82

This punishment was no random event.

مُّسَوَّمَةً عِندَ رَبِّكَ ۖ وَمَا هِىَ مِنَ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ بِبَعِيدٍۢ

Marked from your Lord. And it [i.e., Allāh's punishment] is not from the wrongdoers [very] far.

— Surah Hud 11:83

Allah explains the reason behind this destruction — it was a direct consequence of their persistent defiance.

إِنَّا مُنزِلُونَ عَلَىٰٓ أَهْلِ هَٰذِهِ ٱلْقَرْيَةِ رِجْزًۭا مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ بِمَا كَانُوا۟ يَفْسُقُونَ

Indeed, we will bring down on the people of this city punishment from the sky because they have been defiantly disobedient."

— Surah Al-Ankabut 29:34

Allah tells us clearly why this story is preserved in the Quran — not merely as history, but as a lasting sign.

وَلَقَد تَّرَكْنَا مِنْهَآ ءَايَةًۢ بَيِّنَةًۭ لِّقَوْمٍۢ يَعْقِلُونَ

And We have certainly left of it a sign as clear evidence for a people who use reason.

— Surah Al-Ankabut 29:35

Surah Al-Qamar summarizes the whole story once more, ending with a piercing question for every generation to come.

كَذَّبَتْ قَوْمُ لُوطٍۭ بِٱلنُّذُرِ

The people of Lot denied the warning.

— Surah Al-Qamar 54:33

Yet Allah saved those who believed.

إِنَّآ أَرْسَلْنَا عَلَيْهِمْ حَاصِبًا إِلَّآ ءَالَ لُوطٍۢ ۖ نَّجَّيْنَٰهُم بِسَحَرٍۢ

Indeed, We sent upon them a storm of stones, except the family of Lot - We saved them before dawn.

— Surah Al-Qamar 54:34

This rescue was a mercy from Allah.

نِّعْمَةًۭ مِّنْ عِندِنَا ۚ كَذَٰلِكَ نَجْزِى مَن شَكَرَ

As favor from Us. Thus do We reward he who is grateful.

— Surah Al-Qamar 54:35

Lut (AS) had already given them a clear warning.

وَلَقَدْ أَنذَرَهُم بَطْشَتَنَا فَتَمَارَوْا۟ بِٱلنُّذُرِ

And he had already warned them of Our assault, but they disputed the warning.

— Surah Al-Qamar 54:36

Their persistence in wrongdoing led to their downfall.

وَلَقَدْ رَٰوَدُوهُ عَن ضَيْفِهِۦ فَطَمَسْنَآ أَعْيُنَهُمْ فَذُوقُوا۟ عَذَابِى وَنُذُرِ

And they had demanded from him his guests, but We obliterated their eyes, [saying], "Taste My punishment and warning."

— Surah Al-Qamar 54:37

The punishment arrived exactly as promised.

وَلَقَدْ صَبَّحَهُم بُكْرَةً عَذَابٌۭ مُّسْتَقِرٌّۭ

And there came upon them by morning an abiding punishment.

— Surah Al-Qamar 54:38

The warning was repeated once more.

فَذُوقُوا۟ عَذَابِى وَنُذُرِ

So taste My punishment and warning.

— Surah Al-Qamar 54:39

The story of Lut (AS) teaches a timeless lesson: no matter how normalized a sin becomes within a society, it does not become acceptable in the sight of Allah. Lut (AS) stood firm in delivering the truth even when he stood almost alone, and Allah honored that firmness by saving him and his true family, while leaving the ruins of that city as a lasting sign for anyone willing to reflect and use their reason.

title: The Story of Yaqub (AS) — Israel — Servant of Allah
subject: Yaqub
summary: The story of Prophet Yaqub (AS), a father who bore the loss of his beloved son Yusuf with beautiful patience, never losing hope in Allah, until Allah reunited them.

chapters.title: The Dream and the Warning
chapters.content:
إِذْ قَالَ يُوسُفُ لِأَبِيهِ يَٰٓأَبَتِ إِنِّى رَأَيْتُ أَحَدَ عَشَرَ كَوْكَبًۭا وَٱلشَّمْسَ وَٱلْقَمَرَ رَأَيْتُهُمْ لِى سَٰجِدِينَ

[Of these stories mention] when Joseph said to his father, "O my father, indeed I have seen [in a dream] eleven stars and the sun and the moon; I saw them prostrating to me."

— Surah Yusuf 12:4

Yaqub (AS) had a young son named Yusuf who had a special dream. In the dream, eleven stars, the sun, and the moon all bowed down to him. This was not an ordinary dream — it was a sign from Allah that Yusuf would one day rise to greatness.

قَالَ يَٰبُنَىَّ لَا تَقْصُصْ رُءْيَاكَ عَلَىٰٓ إِخْوَتِكَ فَيَكِيدُوا۟ لَكَ كَيْدًا ۖ إِنَّ ٱلشَّيْطَٰنَ لِلْإِنسَٰنِ عَدُوٌّۭ مُّبِينٌۭ

He said, "O my son, do not relate your vision to your brothers or they will contrive against you a plan. Indeed Satan, to man, is a manifest enemy.

— Surah Yusuf 12:5

Yaqub (AS) was a wise father. He immediately understood that if Yusuf shared this dream with his brothers, it might cause jealousy. So he gently warned Yusuf to keep the dream private — not out of fear, but out of love and wisdom, knowing how Shaytan can plant envy between people.

وَكَذَٰلِكَ يَجْتَبِيكَ رَبُّكَ وَيُعَلِّمُكَ مِن تَأْوِيلِ ٱلْأَحَادِيثِ وَيُتِمُّ نِعْمَتَهُۥ عَلَيْكَ وَعَلَىٰٓ ءَالِ يَعْقُوبَ كَمَآ أَتَمَّهَا عَلَىٰٓ أَبَوَيْكَ مِن قَبْلُ إِبْرَٰهِيمَ وَإِسْحَٰقَ ۚ إِنَّ رَبَّكَ عَلِيمٌ حَكِيمٌۭ

And thus will your Lord choose you and teach you the interpretation of narratives [i.e., events or dreams] and complete His favor upon you and upon the family of Jacob, as He completed it upon your fathers before, Abraham and Isaac. Indeed, your Lord is Knowing and Wise."

— Surah Yusuf 12:6

Yaqub (AS) told Yusuf that Allah had chosen him for something great — he would be taught how to understand the meaning of dreams and events, just like his grandfather Ibrahim (AS) and father Ishaq (AS) before him. This was Allah continuing His blessing through the family line of prophets.

chapters.title: The Brothers' Plot and a Father's Grief
chapters.content:
إِذْ قَالُوا۟ لَيُوسُفُ وَأَخُوهُ أَحَبُّ إِلَىٰٓ أَبِينَا مِنَّا وَنَحْنُ عُصْبَةٌ إِنَّ أَبَانَا لَفِى ضَلَٰلٍۢ مُّبِينٍ

When they said, "Joseph and his brother are more beloved to our father than we, while we are a clan. Indeed, our father is in clear error.

— Surah Yusuf 12:8

Yusuf's brothers grew jealous. They felt their father loved Yusuf and his younger brother more than the rest of them, even though they were many.

ٱقْتُلُوا۟ يُوسُفَ أَوِ ٱطْرَحُوهُ أَرْضًۭا يَخْلُ لَكُمْ وَجْهُ أَبِيكُمْ وَتَكُونُوا۟ مِنۢ بَعْدِهِۦ قَوْمًۭا صَٰلِحِينَ

Kill Joseph or cast him out to [another] land; the countenance [i.e., attention] of your father will [then] be only for you, and you will be after that a righteous people."

— Surah Yusuf 12:9

Their jealousy grew so strong that they even suggested killing Yusuf, or sending him far away, just so their father's attention would return fully to them.

قَالَ قَآئِلٌۭ مِّنْهُمْ لَا تَقْتُلُوا۟ يُوسُفَ وَأَلْقُوهُ فِى غَيَٰبَتِ ٱلْجُبِّ يَلْتَقِطْهُ بَعْضُ ٱلسَّيَّارَةِ إِن كُنتُمْ فَٰعِلِينَ

Said a speaker among them, "Do not kill Joseph but throw him into the bottom of the well; some travelers will pick him up - if you would do [something]."

— Surah Yusuf 12:10

One brother suggested a lesser evil — instead of killing him, throw him into a well. Someone would find him and take him away.

قَالُوا۟ يَٰٓأَبَانَا مَا لَكَ لَا تَأْمَ۫نَّا عَلَىٰ يُوسُفَ وَإِنَّا لَهُۥ لَنَٰصِحُونَ

They said, "O our father, why do you not entrust us with Joseph while indeed, we are to him sincere counselors?

— Surah Yusuf 12:11

They pressed their request further.

أَرْسِلْهُ مَعَنَا غَدًۭا يَرْتَعْ وَيَلْعَبْ وَإِنَّا لَهُۥ لَحَٰفِظُونَ

Send him with us tomorrow that he may eat well and play. And indeed, we will be his guardians."

— Surah Yusuf 12:12

The brothers went to their father with false kindness, asking him to let Yusuf come out with them, promising to protect him.

قَالَ إِنِّى لَيَحْزُنُنِىٓ أَن تَذْهَبُوا۟ بِهِۦ وَأَخَافُ أَن يَأْكُلَهُ ٱلذِّئْبُ وَأَنتُمْ عَنْهُ غَٰفِلُونَ

[Jacob] said, "Indeed, it saddens me that you should take him, and I fear that a wolf would eat him while you are of him unaware."

— Surah Yusuf 12:13

Yaqub (AS) felt uneasy. As a caring father, he expressed his fear — not accusing his sons, but worried a wolf might harm Yusuf if they were not careful.

قَالُوا۟ لَئِنْ أَكَلَهُ ٱلذِّئْبُ وَنَحْنُ عُصْبَةٌ إِنَّآ إِذًۭا لَّخَٰسِرُونَ

They said, "If a wolf should eat him while we are a [strong] clan, indeed, we would then be losers."

— Surah Yusuf 12:14

The brothers reassured him confidently, and eventually he agreed to let Yusuf go with them.

فَلَمَّا ذَهَبُوا۟ بِهِۦ وَأَجْمَعُوٓا۟ أَن يَجْعَلُوهُ فِى غَيَٰبَتِ ٱلْجُبِّ ۚ وَأَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَيْهِ لَتُنَبِّئَنَّهُم بِأَمْرِهِمْ هَٰذَا وَهُمْ لَا يَشْعُرُونَ

So when they took him [out] and agreed to put him into the bottom of the well... But We inspired to him, "You will surely inform them [someday] about this affair of theirs while they do not perceive [your identity]."

— Surah Yusuf 12:15

Once they had Yusuf alone, the brothers carried out their plan and lowered him into the well. But Allah comforted Yusuf even in that dark moment, promising him that one day he would remind his brothers of this — when they would not even recognize him.

وَجَآءُوٓ أَبَاهُمْ عِشَآءًۭ يَبْكُونَ

And they came to their father at night, weeping.

— Surah Yusuf 12:16

They gave their father a fabricated story.

قَالُوا۟ يَٰٓأَبَانَآ إِنَّا ذَهَبْنَا نَسْتَبِقُ وَتَرَكْنَا يُوسُفَ عِندَ مَتَٰعِنَا فَأَكَلَهُ ٱلذِّئْبُ ۖ وَمَآ أَنتَ بِمُؤْمِنٍۢ لَّنَا وَلَوْ كُنَّا صَٰدِقِينَ

They said, "O our father, indeed we went racing each other and left Joseph with our possessions, and a wolf ate him. But you would not believe us, even if we were truthful."

— Surah Yusuf 12:17

They presented false evidence to support their claim.

وَجَآءُو عَلَىٰ قَمِيصِهِۦ بِدَمٍۢ كَذِبٍۢ ۚ قَالَ بَلْ سَوَّلَتْ لَكُمْ أَنفُسُكُمْ أَمْرًۭا ۖ فَصَبْرٌۭ جَمِيلٌۭ ۖ وَٱللَّهُ ٱلْمُسْتَعَانُ عَلَىٰ مَا تَصِفُونَ

And they brought upon his shirt false blood. [Jacob] said, "Rather, your souls have enticed you to something, so patience is most fitting. And Allāh is the one sought for help against that which you describe."

— Surah Yusuf 12:18

The brothers came back that night crying, telling their father a wolf had eaten Yusuf, showing him Yusuf's shirt stained with false blood. But Yaqub (AS) was not fooled — his fatherly heart sensed something was wrong. Instead of lashing out in anger, he chose beautiful patience (sabr jameel) and turned to Allah for help.

chapters.title: Years of Patience
chapters.content:
قَالَ بَلْ سَوَّلَتْ لَكُمْ أَنفُسُكُمْ أَمْرًۭا ۖ فَصَبْرٌۭ جَمِيلٌ ۖ عَسَى ٱللَّهُ أَن يَأْتِيَنِى بِهِمْ جَمِيعًا ۚ إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ ٱلْعَلِيمُ ٱلْحَكِيمُ

[Jacob] said, "Rather, your souls have enticed you to something, so patience is most fitting. Perhaps Allāh will bring them to me all together. Indeed, it is He who is the Knowing, the Wise."

— Surah Yusuf 12:83

Years later, when another son was also kept away from him (in later parts of the story), Yaqub (AS) repeated the same beautiful patience — never losing hope that Allah would return his sons to him one day.

وَتَوَلَّىٰ عَنْهُمْ وَقَالَ يَٰٓأَسَفَىٰ عَلَىٰ يُوسُفَ وَٱبْيَضَّتْ عَيْنَاهُ مِنَ ٱلْحُزْنِ فَهُوَ كَظِيمٌۭ

And he turned away from them and said, "Oh, my sorrow over Joseph," and his eyes became white from grief, for he was [of that] a suppressor.

— Surah Yusuf 12:84

Yaqub (AS)'s grief for Yusuf was so deep and lasted so long that his eyes turned white — many scholars explain this as him losing his eyesight from constant weeping. Yet he held his sorrow inside with dignity, not complaining to people.

قَالُوا۟ تَٱللَّهِ تَفْتَؤُا۟ تَذْكُرُ يُوسُفَ حَتَّىٰ تَكُونَ حَرَضًا أَوْ تَكُونَ مِنَ ٱلْهَٰلِكِينَ

They said, "By Allāh, you will not cease remembering Joseph until you become fatally ill or become of those who perish."

— Surah Yusuf 12:85

His sons worried that his constant grief would harm his health.

قَالَ إِنَّمَآ أَشْكُوا۟ بَثِّى وَحُزْنِىٓ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ وَأَعْلَمُ مِنَ ٱللَّهِ مَا لَا تَعْلَمُونَ

He said, "I only complain of my suffering and my grief to Allāh, and I know from Allāh that which you do not know.

— Surah Yusuf 12:86

Yaqub (AS) gave one of the most powerful lessons in the Quran here: he did not complain to people about his pain — he complained only to Allah. This teaches us where a believer should truly take their sadness.

يَٰبَنِىَّ ٱذْهَبُوا۟ فَتَحَسَّسُوا۟ مِن يُوسُفَ وَأَخِيهِ وَلَا تَا۟يْـَٔسُوا۟ مِن رَّوْحِ ٱللَّهِ ۖ إِنَّهُۥ لَا يَا۟يْـَٔسُ مِن رَّوْحِ ٱللَّهِ إِلَّا ٱلْقَوْمُ ٱلْكَٰفِرُونَ

O my sons, go and find out about Joseph and his brother and despair not of relief from Allāh. Indeed, no one despairs of relief from Allāh except the disbelieving people."

— Surah Yusuf 12:87

Even after all those years, Yaqub (AS) never gave up hope. He told his sons to go search for Yusuf again, reminding them that only disbelievers lose hope in Allah's mercy. This is a timeless lesson — no matter how long the trial, a believer never despairs.

chapters.title: The Scent of Yusuf
chapters.content:
ٱذْهَبُوا۟ بِقَمِيصِى هَٰذَا فَأَلْقُوهُ عَلَىٰ وَجْهِ أَبِى يَأْتِ بَصِيرًۭا وَأْتُونِى بِأَهْلِكُمْ أَجْمَعِينَ

Take this, my shirt, and cast it over the face of my father; he will become seeing. And bring me your family, all together."

— Surah Yusuf 12:93

After many years, Yusuf — now a powerful leader in Egypt — revealed his true identity to his brothers. He gave them his shirt and told them to place it over their father's face, promising that his eyesight would return.

وَلَمَّا فَصَلَتِ ٱلْعِيرُ قَالَ أَبُوهُمْ إِنِّى لَأَجِدُ رِيحَ يُوسُفَ ۖ لَوْلَآ أَن تُفَنِّدُونِ

And when the caravan departed [from Egypt], their father said, "Indeed, I find the smell of Joseph [and would say that he was alive] if you did not think me weakened in mind."

— Surah Yusuf 12:94

Even before the shirt arrived, Yaqub (AS) — far away — sensed the scent of Yusuf. His heart, connected to his son through years of love and hope, felt something others around him could not.

قَالُوا۟ تَٱللَّهِ إِنَّكَ لَفِى ضَلَٰلِكَ ٱلْقَدِيمِ

They said, "By Allāh, indeed you are in your [same] old error."

— Surah Yusuf 12:95

Those around him doubted him, thinking his old age or lasting grief was affecting his judgment.

فَلَمَّآ أَن جَآءَ ٱلْبَشِيرُ أَلْقَىٰهُ عَلَىٰ وَجْهِهِۦ فَٱرْتَدَّ بَصِيرًۭا ۖ قَالَ أَلَمْ أَقُل لَّكُمْ إِنِّىٓ أَعْلَمُ مِنَ ٱللَّهِ مَا لَا تَعْلَمُونَ

And when the bearer of good tidings arrived, he cast it over his face, and he returned [once again] seeing. He said, "Did I not tell you that I know from Allāh that which you do not know?"

— Surah Yusuf 12:96

When the shirt finally reached him and was placed over his face, his eyesight returned instantly, just as Yusuf had promised. Yaqub (AS)'s faith was proven true.

قَالُوا۟ يَٰٓأَبَانَا ٱسْتَغْفِرْ لَنَا ذُنُوبَنَآ إِنَّا كُنَّا خَٰطِـِٔينَ

They said, "O our father, ask for us forgiveness of our sins; indeed, we have been sinners."

— Surah Yusuf 12:97

Yaqub (AS) responded with mercy in his heart.

قَالَ سَوْفَ أَسْتَغْفِرُ لَكُمْ رَبِّىٓ ۖ إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ ٱلْغَفُورُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ

He said, "I will ask forgiveness for you from my Lord. Indeed, it is He who is the Forgiving, the Merciful."

— Surah Yusuf 12:98

His sons finally admitted their wrongdoing and asked for forgiveness. Yaqub (AS), showing mercy and forgiveness himself, promised to pray for them.

فَلَمَّا دَخَلُوا۟ عَلَىٰ يُوسُفَ ءَاوَىٰٓ إِلَيْهِ أَبَوَيْهِ وَقَالَ ٱدْخُلُوا۟ مِصْرَ إِن شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ ءَامِنِينَ

And when they entered upon Joseph, he took his parents to himself [i.e., embraced them] and said, "Enter Egypt, Allāh willing, safe [and secure]."

— Surah Yusuf 12:99

He then honored his parents in a special way.

وَرَفَعَ أَبَوَيْهِ عَلَى ٱلْعَرْشِ وَخَرُّوا۟ لَهُۥ سُجَّدًۭا ۖ وَقَالَ يَٰٓأَبَتِ هَٰذَا تَأْوِيلُ رُءْيَٰىَ مِن قَبْلُ قَدْ جَعَلَهَا رَبِّى حَقًّۭا ۖ وَقَدْ أَحْسَنَ بِىٓ إِذْ أَخْرَجَنِى مِنَ ٱلسِّجْنِ وَجَآءَ بِكُم مِّنَ ٱلْبَدْوِ مِنۢ بَعْدِ أَن نَّزَغَ ٱلشَّيْطَٰنُ بَيْنِى وَبَيْنَ إِخْوَتِىٓ ۚ إِنَّ رَبِّى لَطِيفٌۭ لِّمَا يَشَآءُ ۚ إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ ٱلْعَلِيمُ ٱلْحَكِيمُ

And he raised his parents upon the throne, and they bowed to him in prostration. And he said, "O my father, this is the explanation of my vision of before. My Lord has made it reality. And He was certainly good to me when He took me out of prison and brought you [here] from bedouin life after Satan had induced [estrangement] between me and my brothers. Indeed, my Lord is Subtle in what He wills. Indeed, it is He who is the Knowing, the Wise.

— Surah Yusuf 12:100

Finally, the family was reunited in Egypt. Yusuf embraced his parents, and the dream from the very first chapter came true — the eleven stars, the sun, and the moon (his brothers and parents) bowed before him. The whole journey — the well, the years apart, the patience — all made sense in the end.

chapters.title: A Legacy of Faith
chapters.content:
فَلَمَّا ٱعْتَزَلَهُمْ وَمَا يَعْبُدُونَ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ وَهَبْنَا لَهُۥٓ إِسْحَٰقَ وَيَعْقُوبَ ۖ وَكُلًّۭا جَعَلْنَا نَبِيًّۭا

So when he had left them and those they worshipped other than Allāh, We gave him Isaac and Jacob, and each [of them] We made a prophet.

— Surah Maryam 19:49

Allah describes the honor He gave this blessed family.

وَوَهَبْنَا لَهُم مِّن رَّحْمَتِنَا وَجَعَلْنَا لَهُمْ لِسَانَ صِدْقٍ عَلِيًّۭا

And We gave them of Our mercy, and We made for them a mention [i.e., reputation] of high honor.

— Surah Maryam 19:50

Allah blessed Yaqub (AS), his father Ishaq (AS) before him, and gave the family a lasting reputation of honor and truthfulness among the people.

وَوَصَّىٰ بِهَآ إِبْرَٰهِۦمُ بَنِيهِ وَيَعْقُوبُ يَٰبَنِىَّ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ ٱصْطَفَىٰ لَكُمُ ٱلدِّينَ فَلَا تَمُوتُنَّ إِلَّا وَأَنتُم مُّسْلِمُونَ

And Abraham instructed his sons [to do the same] and [so did] Jacob, [saying], "O my sons, indeed Allāh has chosen for you this religion, so do not die except while you are Muslims."

— Surah Al-Baqarah 2:132

Just as Ibrahim (AS) had done, Yaqub (AS) instructed his sons to hold firmly to Islam — the religion of submission to Allah alone — until their very last breath.

أَمْ كُنتُمْ شُهَدَآءَ إِذْ حَضَرَ يَعْقُوبَ ٱلْمَوْتُ إِذْ قَالَ لِبَنِيهِ مَا تَعْبُدُونَ مِنۢ بَعْدِى قَالُوا۟ نَعْبُدُ إِلَٰهَكَ وَإِلَٰهَ ءَابَآئِكَ إِبْرَٰهِۦمَ وَإِسْمَٰعِيلَ وَإِسْحَٰقَ إِلَٰهًۭا وَٰحِدًۭا وَنَحْنُ لَهُۥ مُسْلِمُونَ

Or were you witnesses when death approached Jacob, when he said to his sons, "What will you worship after me?" They said, "We will worship your God and the God of your fathers, Abraham and Ishmael and Isaac - one God. And we are Muslims [in submission] to Him."

— Surah Al-Baqarah 2:133

On his deathbed, Yaqub (AS) asked his sons the most important question a father could ask: "What will you worship after me?" Their answer showed that his lifelong teaching had succeeded — they affirmed belief in the one God, the same God worshipped by Ibrahim, Ismail, and Ishaq (AS). Yaqub (AS)'s greatest legacy was not wealth or land, but faith passed safely to the next generation.

title: The Story of Ayyub (AS) — Symbol of Patience
subject: Ayyub
summary: The story of Prophet Ayyub (AS), tested with severe hardship, who never stopped calling on Allah, and was rewarded with healing, his family restored, and mercy from His Lord.

chapters.title: Touched by Hardship
chapters.content:
Before the Quran tells us about the healing Ayyub (AS) received, or the mercy Allah showed him, it first wants us to know how he responded when hardship touched him. A few short verses show us his heart in the middle of suffering — and that sets the tone for everything that follows.

وَٱذْكُرْ عَبْدَنَآ أَيُّوبَ إِذْ نَادَىٰ رَبَّهُۥٓ أَنِّى مَسَّنِىَ ٱلشَّيْطَٰنُ بِنُصْبٍۢ وَعَذَابٍ

And remember Our servant Job, when he called to his Lord, "Indeed, Satan has touched me with hardship and torment."

— Surah Sad 38:41

Ayyub (AS) went through a very hard time in his life. The Quran calls him "Our servant" — showing how close and beloved he was to Allah, even during his suffering. He turned to Allah and told Him honestly about his pain.

وَأَيُّوبَ إِذْ نَادَىٰ رَبَّهُۥٓ أَنِّى مَسَّنِىَ ٱلضُّرُّ وَأَنتَ أَرْحَمُ ٱلرَّٰحِمِينَ

And [mention] Job, when he called to his Lord, "Indeed, adversity has touched me, and You are the most merciful of the merciful."

— Surah Al-Anbiya 21:83

Ayyub (AS) did not complain to people. He simply told Allah about his hardship, and reminded himself (and us) of a beautiful truth — Allah is the Most Merciful of all those who show mercy. Even in pain, he trusted Allah's mercy completely.

chapters.title: Allah's Mercy and Healing
chapters.content:
ٱرْكُضْ بِرِجْلِكَ ۖ هَٰذَا مُغْتَسَلٌۢ بَارِدٌۭ وَشَرَابٌۭ

[So he was told], "Strike [the ground] with your foot; this is a [spring for a] cool bath and drink."

— Surah Sad 38:42

Allah answered Ayyub (AS) directly. He was told to strike the ground with his foot, and a cool spring of water came out — enough for him to bathe and drink from, bringing him healing.

فَٱسْتَجَبْنَا لَهُۥ فَكَشَفْنَا مَا بِهِۦ مِن ضُرٍّۢ ۖ وَءَاتَيْنَٰهُ أَهْلَهُۥ وَمِثْلَهُم مَّعَهُمْ رَحْمَةًۭ مِّنْ عِندِنَا وَذِكْرَىٰ لِلْعَٰبِدِينَ

So We responded to him and removed what afflicted him of adversity. And We gave him [back] his family and the like thereof with them as mercy from Us and a reminder for the worshippers [of Allāh].

— Surah Al-Anbiya 21:84

Allah removed Ayyub's hardship completely, and gave him back his family — and even more besides, as a special mercy. This is written in the Quran as a "reminder for the worshippers" — meaning it teaches every believer that patience with Allah always leads to relief.

وَوَهَبْنَا لَهُۥٓ أَهْلَهُۥ وَمِثْلَهُم مَّعَهُمْ رَحْمَةًۭ مِّنَّا وَذِكْرَىٰ لِأُو۟لِى ٱلْأَلْبَٰبِ

And We granted him his family and a like [number] with them as mercy from Us and a reminder for those of understanding.

— Surah Sad 38:43

This same mercy is repeated again in a different Surah, confirming it clearly — Allah gave Ayyub (AS) his family back, doubled, as a sign for people who reflect and understand.

وَخُذْ بِيَدِكَ ضِغْثًۭا فَٱضْرِب بِّهِۦ وَلَا تَحْنَثْ ۗ إِنَّا وَجَدْنَٰهُ صَابِرًۭا ۚ نِّعْمَ ٱلْعَبْدُ ۖ إِنَّهُۥٓ أَوَّابٌۭ

[We said], "And take in your hand a bunch [of grass] and strike with it and do not break your oath." Indeed, We found him patient, an excellent servant. Indeed, he was one repeatedly turning back [to Allāh].

— Surah Sad 38:44

Allah also gave Ayyub (AS) a kind way to keep a promise he had made (his oath), without causing harm to anyone. Then Allah gave him the highest praise a servant can receive: patient, an excellent servant, and one who always turns back to Allah.

chapters.title: Remembered Among the Prophets
chapters.content:
۞ إِنَّآ أَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَيْكَ كَمَآ أَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَىٰ نُوحٍۢ وَٱلنَّبِيِّۦنَ مِنۢ بَعْدِهِۦ ۚ وَأَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَىٰٓ إِبْرَٰهِيمَ وَإِسْمَٰعِيلَ وَإِسْحَٰقَ وَيَعْقُوبَ وَٱلْأَسْبَاطِ وَعِيسَىٰ وَأَيُّوبَ وَيُونُسَ وَهَٰرُونَ وَسُلَيْمَٰنَ ۚ وَءَاتَيْنَا دَاوُۥدَ زَبُورًۭا

Indeed, We have revealed to you, [O Muḥammad], as We revealed to Noah and the prophets after him. And We revealed to Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, the Descendants, Jesus, Job, Jonah, Aaron, and Solomon, and to David We gave the book [of Psalms].

— Surah An-Nisa 4:163

Ayyub (AS) is named directly by Allah alongside the greatest prophets — Nuh, Ibrahim, Ismail, Ishaq, Yaqub, Isa, Yunus, Harun, Sulayman, and Dawud. This shows his high honor. His patience and closeness to Allah earned him a permanent place among the chain of chosen messengers.

title: The Story of Shu'ayb (AS) — Prophet to Midian
subject: Shuayb
summary: The story of Prophet Shu'ayb (AS), sent to the people of Madyan, who called them to worship Allah alone and to deal honestly in trade — and their arrogant rejection that led to their destruction.

chapters.title: A Trustworthy Messenger Calls for Honesty
chapters.content:
Before the Quran tells us about the people of Madyan's arrogant rejection, or the punishment that followed, it first wants us to know what Shu'ayb (AS) actually called his people to. A few clear verses show his message directly — worship Allah alone, and deal with people honestly — and that sets the tone for everything that follows.

وَإِلَىٰ مَدْيَنَ أَخَاهُمْ شُعَيْبًۭا ۗ قَالَ يَٰقَوْمِ ٱعْبُدُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ مَا لَكُم مِّنْ إِلَٰهٍ غَيْرُهُۥ ۖ قَدْ جَآءَتْكُم بَيِّنَةٌۭ مِّن رَّبِّكُمْ ۖ فَأَوْفُوا۟ ٱلْكَيْلَ وَٱلْمِيزَانَ وَلَا تَبْخَسُوا۟ ٱلنَّاسَ أَشْيَآءَهُمْ وَلَا تُفْسِدُوا۟ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ بَعْدَ إِصْلَٰحِهَا ۚ ذَٰلِكُمْ خَيْرٌۭ لَّكُمْ إِن كُنتُم مُّؤْمِنِينَ

And to [the people of] Madyan [We sent] their brother Shuʿayb. He said, "O my people, worship Allāh; you have no deity other than Him. There has come to you clear evidence from your Lord. So fulfill the measure and weight and do not deprive people of their due and cause not corruption upon the earth after its reformation. That is better for you, if you should be believers.

— Surah Al-A'raf 7:85

Shu'ayb (AS) was sent to the people of Madyan as their own brother — one of them, not a stranger. His message had two parts: worship Allah alone, and deal honestly in trade, giving people their full due.

۞ وَإِلَىٰ مَدْيَنَ أَخَاهُمْ شُعَيْبًۭا ۚ قَالَ يَٰقَوْمِ ٱعْبُدُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ مَا لَكُم مِّنْ إِلَٰهٍ غَيْرُهُۥ ۖ وَلَا تَنقُصُوا۟ ٱلْمِكْيَالَ وَٱلْمِيزَانَ ۚ إِنِّىٓ أَرَىٰكُم بِخَيْرٍۢ وَإِنِّىٓ أَخَافُ عَلَيْكُمْ عَذَابَ يَوْمٍۢ مُّحِيطٍۢ

And to Madyan [We sent] their brother Shuʿayb. He said, "O my people, worship Allāh; you have no deity other than Him. And do not decrease from the measure and the scale. Indeed, I see you in prosperity, but indeed, I fear for you the punishment of an all-encompassing Day.

— Surah Hud 11:84

Even though his people were prosperous, Shu'ayb (AS) warned them sincerely — worldly wealth does not protect anyone from Allah's punishment if injustice continues.

وَيَٰقَوْمِ أَوْفُوا۟ ٱلْمِكْيَالَ وَٱلْمِيزَانَ بِٱلْقِسْطِ ۖ وَلَا تَبْخَسُوا۟ ٱلنَّاسَ أَشْيَآءَهُمْ وَلَا تَعْثَوْا۟ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ مُفْسِدِينَ

And O my people, give full measure and weight in justice and do not deprive the people of their due and do not commit abuse on the earth, spreading corruption.

— Surah Hud 11:85

He reminded them that honest dealing was always the better path.

بَقِيَّتُ ٱللَّهِ خَيْرٌۭ لَّكُمْ إِن كُنتُم مُّؤْمِنِينَ ۚ وَمَآ أَنَا۠ عَلَيْكُم بِحَفِيظٍۭ

What remains [lawful] from Allāh is best for you, if you would be believers. But I am not a guardian over you."

— Surah Hud 11:86

Shu'ayb (AS) taught them a timeless principle: what Allah allows through honest, lawful earning is always better than what is gained through cheating people. He reminded them he was only a messenger, not their controller.

كَذَّبَ أَصْحَٰبُ لْـَٔيْكَةِ ٱلْمُرْسَلِينَ

The companions of the thicket [i.e., the people of Madyan] denied the messengers

— Surah Ash-Shu'ara 26:176

Their brother came to call them to the truth.

إِذْ قَالَ لَهُمْ شُعَيْبٌ أَلَا تَتَّقُونَ

When Shuʿayb said to them, "Will you not fear Allāh?

— Surah Ash-Shu'ara 26:177

He introduced himself as someone they could trust.

إِنِّى لَكُمْ رَسُولٌ أَمِينٌۭ

Indeed, I am to you a trustworthy messenger.

— Surah Ash-Shu'ara 26:178

He called them to the same message every messenger brought.

فَٱتَّقُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ وَأَطِيعُونِ

So fear Allāh and obey me.

— Surah Ash-Shu'ara 26:179

He made clear he sought nothing from them in return.

وَمَآ أَسْـَٔلُكُمْ عَلَيْهِ مِنْ أَجْرٍ ۖ إِنْ أَجْرِىَ إِلَّا عَلَىٰ رَبِّ ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ

And I do not ask you for it any payment. My payment is only from the Lord of the worlds.

— Surah Ash-Shu'ara 26:180

Shu'ayb (AS) reminded his people that he was a trustworthy messenger, asking for no payment. His only reward would come from Allah — proving his call was sincere, not for personal gain.

۞ أَوْفُوا۟ ٱلْكَيْلَ وَلَا تَكُونُوا۟ مِنَ ٱلْمُخْسِرِينَ

Give full measure and do not be of those who cause loss.

— Surah Ash-Shu'ara 26:181

He repeated his call for honest dealing plainly.

وَزِنُوا۟ بِٱلْقِسْطَاسِ ٱلْمُسْتَقِيمِ

And weigh with an even [i.e., honest] balance.

— Surah Ash-Shu'ara 26:182

He continued this same instruction.

وَلَا تَبْخَسُوا۟ ٱلنَّاسَ أَشْيَآءَهُمْ وَلَا تَعْثَوْا۟ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ مُفْسِدِينَ

And do not deprive people of their due and do not commit abuse on earth, spreading corruption.

— Surah Ash-Shu'ara 26:183

He tied this instruction to fearing their Creator.

وَٱتَّقُوا۟ ٱلَّذِى خَلَقَكُمْ وَٱلْجِبِلَّةَ ٱلْأَوَّلِينَ

And fear He who created you and the former creation."

— Surah Ash-Shu'ara 26:184

Shu'ayb (AS) repeated his call for honest weighing and measuring clearly — this was not a small side-issue, but central to his message, tied directly to fearing the One who created them all.

chapters.title: The People's Arrogant Rejection
chapters.content:
وَلَا تَقْعُدُوا۟ بِكُلِّ صِرَٰطٍۢ تُوعِدُونَ وَتَصُدُّونَ عَن سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ مَنْ ءَامَنَ بِهِۦ وَتَبْغُونَهَا عِوَجًۭا ۚ وَٱذْكُرُوٓا۟ إِذْ كُنتُمْ قَلِيلًۭا فَكَثَّرَكُمْ ۖ وَٱنظُرُوا۟ كَيْفَ كَانَ عَٰقِبَةُ ٱلْمُفْسِدِينَ

And do not sit on every path, threatening and averting from the way of Allāh those who believe in Him, seeking to make it [seem] deviant. And remember when you were few and He increased you. And see how was the end of the corrupters.

— Surah Al-A'raf 7:86

He reminded the believers among them to be patient.

وَإِن كَانَ طَآئِفَةٌۭ مِّنكُمْ ءَامَنُوا۟ بِٱلَّذِىٓ أُرْسِلْتُ بِهِۦ وَطَآئِفَةٌۭ لَّمْ يُؤْمِنُوا۟ فَٱصْبِرُوا۟ حَتَّىٰ يَحْكُمَ ٱللَّهُ بَيْنَنَا ۚ وَهُوَ خَيْرُ ٱلْحَٰكِمِينَ

And if there should be a group among you who has believed in that with which I have been sent and a group that has not believed, then be patient until Allāh judges between us. And He is the best of judges."

— Surah Al-A'raf 7:87

Shu'ayb (AS) also warned his people against blocking others from believing, and reminded them of Allah's past favor on them. To the believers among his people, he encouraged patience, trusting Allah to judge fairly in the end.

۞ قَالَ ٱلْمَلَأُ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱسْتَكْبَرُوا۟ مِن قَوْمِهِۦ لَنُخْرِجَنَّكَ يَٰشُعَيْبُ وَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ مَعَكَ مِن قَرْيَتِنَآ أَوْ لَتَعُودُنَّ فِى مِلَّتِنَا ۚ قَالَ أَوَلَوْ كُنَّا كَٰرِهِينَ

Said the eminent ones who were arrogant among his people, "We will surely evict you, O Shuʿayb, and those who have believed with you from our city, or you must return to our religion." He said, "Even if we were unwilling?

— Surah Al-A'raf 7:88

Instead of listening, the arrogant leaders among his people threatened to expel him and the believers, or force them back into their old religion.

قَدِ ٱفْتَرَيْنَا عَلَى ٱللَّهِ كَذِبًا إِنْ عُدْنَا فِى مِلَّتِكُم بَعْدَ إِذْ نَجَّىٰنَا ٱللَّهُ مِنْهَا ۚ وَمَا يَكُونُ لَنَآ أَن نَّعُودَ فِيهَآ إِلَّآ أَن يَشَآءَ ٱللَّهُ رَبُّنَا ۚ وَسِعَ رَبُّنَا كُلَّ شَىْءٍ عِلْمًا ۚ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ تَوَكَّلْنَا ۚ رَبَّنَا ٱفْتَحْ بَيْنَنَا وَبَيْنَ قَوْمِنَا بِٱلْحَقِّ وَأَنتَ خَيْرُ ٱلْفَٰتِحِينَ

We would have invented against Allāh a lie if we returned to your religion after Allāh had saved us from it. And it is not for us to return to it except that Allāh, our Lord, should will. Our Lord has encompassed all things in knowledge. Upon Allāh we have relied. Our Lord, decide between us and our people in truth, and You are the best of those who give decision."

— Surah Al-A'raf 7:89

Shu'ayb (AS) refused firmly, and turned the matter over to Allah, asking Him to judge between them with truth.

وَقَالَ ٱلْمَلَأُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ مِن قَوْمِهِۦ لَئِنِ ٱتَّبَعْتُمْ شُعَيْبًا إِنَّكُمْ إِذًۭا لَّخَٰسِرُونَ

Said the eminent ones who disbelieved among his people, "If you should follow Shuʿayb, indeed, you would then be losers."

— Surah Al-A'raf 7:90

The disbelieving leaders tried to scare others away from following Shu'ayb (AS), falsely warning that it would lead to loss.

قَالُوا۟ يَٰشُعَيْبُ أَصَلَوٰتُكَ تَأْمُرُكَ أَن نَّتْرُكَ مَا يَعْبُدُ ءَابَآؤُنَآ أَوْ أَن نَّفْعَلَ فِىٓ أَمْوَٰلِنَا مَا نَشَٰٓؤُا۟ ۖ إِنَّكَ لَأَنتَ ٱلْحَلِيمُ ٱلرَّشِيدُ

They said, "O Shuʿayb, does your prayer [i.e., religion] command you that we should leave what our fathers worship or not do with our wealth what we please? Indeed, you are the forbearing, the discerning!"

— Surah Hud 11:87

They mocked him, sarcastically calling him "forbearing" and "discerning," refusing to give up their false gods or their unfair business habits.

قَالُوا۟ يَٰشُعَيْبُ مَا نَفْقَهُ كَثِيرًۭا مِّمَّا تَقُولُ وَإِنَّا لَنَرَىٰكَ فِينَا ضَعِيفًۭا ۖ وَلَوْلَا رَهْطُكَ لَرَجَمْنَٰكَ ۖ وَمَآ أَنتَ عَلَيْنَا بِعَزِيزٍۢ

They said, "O Shuʿayb, we do not understand much of what you say, and indeed, we consider you among us as weak. And if not for your family, we would have stoned you [to death]; and you are not to us one respected."

— Surah Hud 11:91

Their arrogance grew worse — they even threatened to stone him, and only spared him out of respect for his family, not for him personally.

قَالُوٓا۟ إِنَّمَآ أَنتَ مِنَ ٱلْمُسَحَّرِينَ

They said, "You are only of those affected by magic.

— Surah Ash-Shu'ara 26:185

They continued their insults.

وَمَآ أَنتَ إِلَّا بَشَرٌۭ مِّثْلُنَا وَإِن نَّظُنُّكَ لَمِنَ ٱلْكَٰذِبِينَ

You are but a man like ourselves, and indeed, we think you are among the liars.

— Surah Ash-Shu'ara 26:186

They demanded impossible proof.

فَأَسْقِطْ عَلَيْنَا كِسَفًۭا مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ إِن كُنتَ مِنَ ٱلصَّٰدِقِينَ

So cause to fall upon us fragments of the sky, if you should be of the truthful."

— Surah Ash-Shu'ara 26:187

They went as far as accusing him of being under a magic spell, calling him a liar, and arrogantly demanding he bring down pieces of the sky as proof.

قَالَ رَبِّىٓ أَعْلَمُ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ

He said, "My Lord is most knowing of what you do."

— Surah Ash-Shu'ara 26:188

Shu'ayb (AS) did not argue back with anger. He simply reminded them that Allah fully knew everything they were doing.

chapters.title: Shu'ayb's Firm Reply and Final Warning
chapters.content:
قَالَ يَٰقَوْمِ أَرَءَيْتُمْ إِن كُنتُ عَلَىٰ بَيِّنَةٍۢ مِّن رَّبِّى وَرَزَقَنِى مِنْهُ رِزْقًا حَسَنًۭا ۚ وَمَآ أُرِيدُ أَنْ أُخَالِفَكُمْ إِلَىٰ مَآ أَنْهَىٰكُمْ عَنْهُ ۚ إِنْ أُرِيدُ إِلَّا ٱلْإِصْلَٰحَ مَا ٱسْتَطَعْتُ ۚ وَمَا تَوْفِيقِىٓ إِلَّا بِٱللَّهِ ۚ عَلَيْهِ تَوَكَّلْتُ وَإِلَيْهِ أُنِيبُ

He said, "O my people, have you considered: if I am upon clear evidence from my Lord and He has provided me with a good provision from Him...? And I do not intend to differ from you in that which I have forbidden you; I only intend reform as much as I am able. And my success is not but through Allāh. Upon Him I have relied, and to Him I return.

— Surah Hud 11:88

Shu'ayb (AS) explained that he was not asking anything of them that he did not also hold himself to. His only goal was reform — improving their situation, not harming them — and his reliance was fully on Allah.

وَيَٰقَوْمِ لَا يَجْرِمَنَّكُمْ شِقَاقِىٓ أَن يُصِيبَكُم مِّثْلُ مَآ أَصَابَ قَوْمَ نُوحٍ أَوْ قَوْمَ هُودٍ أَوْ قَوْمَ صَٰلِحٍۢ ۚ وَمَا قَوْمُ لُوطٍۢ مِّنكُم بِبَعِيدٍۢ

And O my people, let not [your] dissension from me cause you to be struck by that similar to what struck the people of Noah or the people of Hūd or the people of Ṣāliḥ. And the people of Lot are not from you far away.

— Surah Hud 11:89

He reminded them of what happened to the nations before them — the people of Nuh, Hud, Salih, and Lut — all destroyed for rejecting their prophets. He warned that Madyan was not far from that same fate.

وَٱسْتَغْفِرُوا۟ رَبَّكُمْ ثُمَّ تُوبُوٓا۟ إِلَيْهِ ۚ إِنَّ رَبِّى رَحِيمٌۭ وَدُودٌۭ

And ask forgiveness of your Lord and then repent to Him. Indeed, my Lord is Merciful and Affectionate."

— Surah Hud 11:90

Even after all their mockery, Shu'ayb (AS) still called them gently to seek Allah's forgiveness, reminding them that his Lord is Merciful and full of love for His servants who turn back to Him.

قَالَ يَٰقَوْمِ أَرَهْطِىٓ أَعَزُّ عَلَيْكُم مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ وَٱتَّخَذْتُمُوهُ وَرَآءَكُمْ ظِهْرِيًّا ۖ إِنَّ رَبِّى بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ مُحِيطٌۭ

He said, "O my people, is my family more respected for power by you than Allāh? But you put Him behind your backs [in neglect]. Indeed, my Lord is encompassing of what you do.

— Surah Hud 11:92

Shu'ayb (AS) pointed out something striking — they respected his family's power more than they respected Allah Himself, pushing Allah's command completely aside.

وَيَٰقَوْمِ ٱعْمَلُوا۟ عَلَىٰ مَكَانَتِكُمْ إِنِّى عَٰمِلٌۭ ۖ سَوْفَ تَعْلَمُونَ مَن يَأْتِيهِ عَذَابٌۭ يُخْزِيهِ وَمَنْ هُوَ كَٰذِبٌۭ ۖ وَٱرْتَقِبُوٓا۟ إِنِّى مَعَكُمْ رَقِيبٌۭ

And O my people, work according to your position; indeed, I am working. You are going to know to whom will come a punishment that will disgrace him and who is a liar. So watch; indeed, I am with you a watcher, [awaiting the outcome]."

— Surah Hud 11:93

Shu'ayb (AS) gave his final, firm warning — the truth would soon become clear to everyone, whoever was truly lying would be known, and a disgracing punishment awaited those who continued to reject the truth.

chapters.title: The Punishment and Allah's Mercy
chapters.content:
فَأَخَذَتْهُمُ ٱلرَّجْفَةُ فَأَصْبَحُوا۟ فِى دَارِهِمْ جَٰثِمِينَ

So the earthquake seized them, and they became within their home [corpses] fallen prone.

— Surah Al-A'raf 7:91

Allah describes the totality of their end.

ٱلَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوا۟ شُعَيْبًۭا كَأَن لَّمْ يَغْنَوْا۟ فِيهَا ۚ ٱلَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوا۟ شُعَيْبًۭا كَانُوا۟ هُمُ ٱلْخَٰسِرِينَ

Those who denied Shuʿayb - it was as though they had never resided there. Those who denied Shuʿayb - it was they who were the losers.

— Surah Al-A'raf 7:92

After all their arrogance and threats, an earthquake seized the people who rejected him. They were wiped out completely — as if they had never lived there at all.

فَتَوَلَّىٰ عَنْهُمْ وَقَالَ يَٰقَوْمِ لَقَدْ أَبْلَغْتُكُمْ رِسَٰلَٰتِ رَبِّى وَنَصَحْتُ لَكُمْ ۖ فَكَيْفَ ءَاسَىٰ عَلَىٰ قَوْمٍۢ كَٰفِرِينَ

And he [i.e., Shuʿayb] turned away from them and said, "O my people, I had certainly conveyed to you the messages of my Lord and advised you, so how could I grieve for a disbelieving people?"

— Surah Al-A'raf 7:93

Shu'ayb (AS) turned away from the ruins of his people, having delivered the message fully and sincerely. He had done everything he could — the choice they made was their own.

وَلَمَّا جَآءَ أَمْرُنَا نَجَّيْنَا شُعَيْبًۭا وَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ مَعَهُۥ بِرَحْمَةٍۢ مِّنَّا وَأَخَذَتِ ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا۟ ٱلصَّيْحَةُ فَأَصْبَحُوا۟ فِى دِيَٰرِهِمْ جَٰثِمِينَ

And when Our command came, We saved Shuʿayb and those who believed with him, by mercy from Us. And the shriek seized those who had wronged, and they became within their homes [corpses] fallen prone

— Surah Hud 11:94

The outcome for the wrongdoers was complete.

كَأَن لَّمْ يَغْنَوْا۟ فِيهَآ ۗ أَلَا بُعْدًۭا لِّمَدْيَنَ كَمَا بَعِدَتْ ثَمُودُ

As if they had never prospered therein. Then, away with Madyan as Thamūd was taken away.

— Surah Hud 11:95

Allah saved Shu'ayb (AS) and the believers with him, out of pure mercy. The wrongdoers were struck by a mighty shriek — the same kind of end that befell the people of Thamud before them.

فَكَذَّبُوهُ فَأَخَذَهُمْ عَذَابُ يَوْمِ ٱلظُّلَّةِ ۚ إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ عَذَابَ يَوْمٍ عَظِيمٍ

And they denied him, so the punishment of the day of the black cloud seized them. Indeed, it was the punishment of a terrible day.

— Surah Ash-Shu'ara 26:189

In another surah, the punishment is described as coming through a dark, terrible cloud — a separate and equally powerful sign of Allah's justice against a people who refused to change.

إِنَّ فِى ذَٰلِكَ لَءَايَةًۭ ۖ وَمَا كَانَ أَكْثَرُهُم مُّؤْمِنِينَ

Indeed in that is a sign, but most of them were not to be believers.

— Surah Ash-Shu'ara 26:190

Yet the Quran reminds us of Allah's nature even in judgment.

وَإِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَهُوَ ٱلْعَزِيزُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ

And indeed, your Lord - He is the Exalted in Might, the Merciful.

— Surah Ash-Shu'ara 26:191

The Quran ends Shu'ayb's (AS) story with a reminder that this is a sign for all people — and closes with two of Allah's beautiful names together: the Exalted in Might, and the Merciful, showing that His justice and His mercy are never separate.

title: The Story of Harun (AS) — Brother and Helper of Musa
subject: Harun
summary: The story of Harun (AS), brother and helper of Musa (AS), who stood beside him before Fir'awn and faced the trial of the golden calf.

chapters.title: Harun, Brother and Helper of Musa
chapters.content:
Harun (AS) was the older brother of Musa (AS), and Allah chose him as a prophet to stand beside his brother in a mission that would test them both. This chapter begins with how Allah described this gift of mercy, and how Musa himself asked for Harun's support before facing Fir'awn.

وَوَهَبْنَا لَهُۥ مِن رَّحْمَتِنَآ أَخَاهُ هَٰرُونَ نَبِيًّۭا

And We gave him out of Our mercy his brother Aaron as a prophet.

— Surah Maryam 19:53

Before Musa (AS) even set out to speak to Fir'awn, he asked Allah for his brother to be sent with him as a source of strength and companionship in his mission.

وَٱجْعَل لِّى وَزِيرًۭا مِّنْ أَهْلِى

And appoint for me a minister [i.e., assistant] from my family -

— Surah Ta-Ha 20:29

He named exactly who he meant.

هَٰرُونَ أَخِى

Aaron, my brother.

— Surah Ta-Ha 20:30

He asked for strength through him.

ٱشْدُدْ بِهِۦٓ أَزْرِى

Increase through him my strength

— Surah Ta-Ha 20:31

He asked that Harun share in his task.

وَأَشْرِكْهُ فِىٓ أَمْرِى

And let him share my task

— Surah Ta-Ha 20:32

This was so they could worship Allah together.

كَىْ نُسَبِّحَكَ كَثِيرًۭا

That we may exalt You much

— Surah Ta-Ha 20:33

And remember Him often.

وَنَذْكُرَكَ كَثِيرًا

And remember You much.

— Surah Ta-Ha 20:34

He closed his request with trust in Allah.

إِنَّكَ كُنتَ بِنَا بَصِيرًۭا

Indeed, You are of us ever Seeing."

— Surah Ta-Ha 20:35

Allah accepted Musa's request right away, granting him exactly what he asked for.

قَالَ قَدْ أُوتِيتَ سُؤْلَكَ يَٰمُوسَىٰ

[Allāh] said, "You have been granted your request, O Moses.

— Surah Ta-Ha 20:36

chapters.title: Facing Fir'awn Together
chapters.content:
With Harun (AS) at his side, Musa (AS) was ready to deliver the message to Fir'awn. This chapter follows their meeting with Fir'awn, his refusal, and the dramatic moment when the royal magicians ended up believing in Allah.

قَالَ رَبِّ إِنِّىٓ أَخَافُ أَن يُكَذِّبُونِ

He said, "My Lord, indeed I fear that they will deny me

— Surah Ash-Shu'ara 26:12

He continued expressing his fear.

وَيَضِيقُ صَدْرِى وَلَا يَنطَلِقُ لِسَانِى فَأَرْسِلْ إِلَىٰ هَٰرُونَ

And that my breast will tighten and my tongue will not be fluent, so send for Aaron.

— Surah Ash-Shu'ara 26:13

He explained further.

وَلَهُمْ عَلَىَّ ذَنۢبٌۭ فَأَخَافُ أَن يَقْتُلُونِ

And they have upon me a [claim due to] sin, so I fear that they will kill me."

— Surah Ash-Shu'ara 26:14

Allah reassured him immediately.

قَالَ كَلَّا ۖ فَٱذْهَبَا بِـَٔايَٰتِنَآ ۖ إِنَّا مَعَكُم مُّسْتَمِعُونَ

[Allāh] said, "No. Go both of you with Our signs; indeed, We are with you, listening.

— Surah Ash-Shu'ara 26:15

Allah then told them exactly what to say.

فَأْتِيَا فِرْعَوْنَ فَقُولَآ إِنَّا رَسُولُ رَبِّ ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ

Go to Pharaoh and say, 'We are the messengers of the Lord of the worlds,

— Surah Ash-Shu'ara 26:16

He specified precisely what to request.

أَنْ أَرْسِلْ مَعَنَا بَنِىٓ إِسْرَٰٓءِيلَ

[Commanded to say], "Send with us the Children of Israel."'"

— Surah Ash-Shu'ara 26:17

They stood before Fir'awn, who mocked Musa's upbringing and past, but Musa answered him with calm and clear words about Allah, the Lord of all creation.

قَالَ أَلَمْ نُرَبِّكَ فِينَا وَلِيدًۭا وَلَبِثْتَ فِينَا مِنْ عُمُرِكَ سِنِينَ

[Pharaoh] said, "Did we not raise you among us as a child, and you remained among us for years of your life?

— Surah Ash-Shu'ara 26:18

Pharaoh continued his accusation.

وَفَعَلْتَ فَعْلَتَكَ ٱلَّتِى فَعَلْتَ وَأَنتَ مِنَ ٱلْكَٰفِرِينَ

And [then] you did your deed which you did, and you were of the ungrateful."

— Surah Ash-Shu'ara 26:19

Musa (AS) admitted what had happened.

قَالَ فَعَلْتُهَآ إِذًۭا وَأَنَا۠ مِنَ ٱلضَّآلِّينَ

[Moses] said, "I did it, then, while I was of those astray [i.e., ignorant].

— Surah Ash-Shu'ara 26:20

He explained what followed after that.

فَفَرَرْتُ مِنكُمْ لَمَّا خِفْتُكُمْ فَوَهَبَ لِى رَبِّى حُكْمًۭا وَجَعَلَنِى مِنَ ٱلْمُرْسَلِينَ

So I fled from you when I feared you. Then my Lord granted me judgement [i.e., wisdom and prophet hood] and appointed me [as one] of the messengers.

— Surah Ash-Shu'ara 26:21

He then turned the accusation back on Pharaoh.

وَتِلْكَ نِعْمَةٌۭ تَمُنُّهَا عَلَىَّ أَنْ عَبَّدتَّ بَنِىٓ إِسْرَٰٓءِيلَ

And is this a favor of which you remind me - that you have enslaved the Children of Israel?"

— Surah Ash-Shu'ara 26:22

Pharaoh changed the subject.

قَالَ فِرْعَوْنُ وَمَا رَبُّ ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ

Said Pharaoh, "And what is the Lord of the worlds?"

— Surah Ash-Shu'ara 26:23

Musa (AS) answered him plainly.

قَالَ رَبُّ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَآ ۖ إِن كُنتُم مُّوقِنِينَ

[Moses] said, "The Lord of the heavens and earth and that between them, if you should be convinced."

— Surah Ash-Shu'ara 26:24

Pharaoh turned to those around him.

قَالَ لِمَنْ حَوْلَهُۥٓ أَلَا تَسْتَمِعُونَ

[Pharaoh] said to those around him, "Do you not hear?"

— Surah Ash-Shu'ara 26:25

Musa (AS) answered once more.

قَالَ رَبُّكُمْ وَرَبُّ ءَابَآئِكُمُ ٱلْأَوَّلِينَ

[Moses] said, "Your Lord and the Lord of your first forefathers."

— Surah Ash-Shu'ara 26:26

Pharaoh accused him of madness.

قَالَ إِنَّ رَسُولَكُمُ ٱلَّذِىٓ أُرْسِلَ إِلَيْكُمْ لَمَجْنُونٌۭ

[Pharaoh] said, "Indeed, your 'messenger' who has been sent to you is mad."

— Surah Ash-Shu'ara 26:27

Musa (AS) continued his answer calmly.

قَالَ رَبُّ ٱلْمَشْرِقِ وَٱلْمَغْرِبِ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَآ ۖ إِن كُنتُمْ تَعْقِلُونَ

[Moses] said, "Lord of the east and the west and that between them, if you were to reason."

— Surah Ash-Shu'ara 26:28

Pharaoh then threatened him.

قَالَ لَئِنِ ٱتَّخَذْتَ إِلَٰهًا غَيْرِى لَأَجْعَلَنَّكَ مِنَ ٱلْمَسْجُونِينَ

[Pharaoh] said, "If you take a god other than me, I will surely place you among those imprisoned."

— Surah Ash-Shu'ara 26:29

Musa (AS) offered clear proof of his message, and Fir'awn gathered the kingdom's best magicians to challenge him.

قَالَ أَوَلَوْ جِئْتُكَ بِشَىْءٍۢ مُّبِينٍۢ

[Moses] said, "Even if I brought you something [i.e., proof] manifest?"

— Surah Ash-Shu'ara 26:30

Pharaoh demanded he show it.

قَالَ فَأْتِ بِهِۦٓ إِن كُنتَ مِنَ ٱلصَّٰدِقِينَ

[Pharaoh] said, "Then bring it, if you should be of the truthful."

— Surah Ash-Shu'ara 26:31

Musa (AS) threw down his staff.

فَأَلْقَىٰ عَصَاهُ فَإِذَا هِىَ ثُعْبَانٌۭ مُّبِينٌۭ

So [Moses] threw his staff, and suddenly it was a serpent manifest.

— Surah Ash-Shu'ara 26:32

He then drew out his hand.

وَنَزَعَ يَدَهُۥ فَإِذَا هِىَ بَيْضَآءُ لِلنَّٰظِرِينَ

And he drew out his hand; thereupon it was white for the observers.

— Surah Ash-Shu'ara 26:33

Pharaoh turned to his advisors.

قَالَ لِلْمَلَإِ حَوْلَهُۥٓ إِنَّ هَٰذَا لَسَٰحِرٌ عَلِيمٌۭ

[Pharaoh] said to the eminent ones around him, "Indeed, this is a learned magician.

— Surah Ash-Shu'ara 26:34

He warned them of the danger he saw.

يُرِيدُ أَن يُخْرِجَكُم مِّنْ أَرْضِكُم بِسِحْرِهِۦ فَمَاذَا تَأْمُرُونَ

He wants to drive you out of your land by his magic, so what do you advise?"

— Surah Ash-Shu'ara 26:35

They gave him their advice.

قَالُوٓا۟ أَرْجِهْ وَأَخَاهُ وَٱبْعَثْ فِى ٱلْمَدَآئِنِ حَٰشِرِينَ

They said, "Postpone [the matter of] him and his brother and send among the cities gatherers

— Surah Ash-Shu'ara 26:36
